Section 1.1 — What Ethics Is, Why It Is Necessary, and What It Is For
Kifungu 1.1 — Maadili ni Nini, Kwa Nini Yanahitajika, na Ni ya Nini

Every man who stands to preach is already an ethicist, whether he has ever used the word or not. The moment he tells a congregation what they ought to do, he has made a claim about right and wrong, and behind that claim stands some authority. The only question is which one. So before we ever ask what is the right thing to do, we have to ask a deeper question: who has the right to tell me what right is? That question is where Christian ethics begins, and it is where it parts ways with almost everything the world will offer you.

Kila mtu anayesimama kuhubiri tayari ni mwanamaadili, awe amewahi kulitumia neno hilo au la. Mara tu anapoliambia kusanyiko kile linalopaswa kufanya, ametoa dai kuhusu mema na mabaya, na nyuma ya dai hilo kuna mamlaka fulani. Swali pekee ni mamlaka gani. Kwa hiyo kabla hatujauliza kamwe ni jambo gani lililo sahihi kufanya, lazima tuulize swali la ndani zaidi: ni nani mwenye haki ya kuniambia jema ni nini? Swali hilo ndipo maadili ya Kikristo yanapoanzia, na ndipo yanapoachana na karibu kila kitu ambacho ulimwengu utakupa.

Let me give you the plain definition first and then unfold it. Christian ethics is the disciplined study of how God's people are to live, judged by the standard of God's own character as He has revealed it in His Word. Notice what that definition does. It does not start with us. It does not start with what feels right, what works, or what the majority has decided. It starts with God — with who He is — and it measures every action against Him. Ethics, for the believer, is not the search for a standard. The standard has already been given. Ethics is the careful, prayerful work of learning to live inside it.

Acha nikupe kwanza ufafanuzi ulio wazi, kisha niufafanue. Maadili ya Kikristo ni somo lenye nidhamu kuhusu jinsi watu wa Mungu wanavyopaswa kuishi, likipimwa kwa kipimo cha tabia ya Mungu Mwenyewe kama alivyoifunua katika Neno lake. Angalia ufafanuzi huo unavyofanya. Hauanzi na sisi. Hauanzi na kile kinachoonekana kuwa sawa kwa hisia, kile kinachofanya kazi, au kile ambacho wengi wameamua. Unaanza na Mungu — na jinsi alivyo — na unapima kila tendo kwa kumlinganisha Yeye. Kwa mwamini, maadili si kutafuta kipimo. Kipimo tayari kimetolewa. Maadili ni kazi ya uangalifu na ya maombi ya kujifunza kuishi ndani yake.

Why is such a study necessary? You might think that a man who loves God and reads his Bible would simply know how to act, and to a degree that is true. But Scripture itself assumes otherwise. Paul prays that the Philippians' love would "abound still more and more in knowledge and all discernment, that you may approve the things that are excellent" (Philippians 1:9–10). Discernment is not automatic. It is trained. The writer of Hebrews rebukes believers who ought to be teachers but still need milk, because "solid food belongs to those who are of full age, that is, those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil" (Hebrews 5:14). Hear that phrase — by reason of use. Ethical maturity is not a gift dropped on the new convert. It is the fruit of exercise, of practice, of a mind drilled again and again in the things of God until it can tell good from evil the way a trained ear tells a true note from a flat one.

Kwa nini somo kama hili linahitajika? Unaweza kudhani kwamba mtu anayempenda Mungu na kusoma Biblia yake angejua tu jinsi ya kutenda, na kwa kiasi fulani hilo ni kweli. Lakini Maandiko yenyewe yanadhani vinginevyo. Paulo anaomba kwamba upendo wa Wafilipi "uzidi kuwa mwingi sana, katika hekima na ufahamu wote; mpate kuyakubali yaliyo bora" (Wafilipi 1:9–10). Kupambanua si jambo linalokuja lenyewe. Hufunzwa. Mwandishi wa Waebrania anawakemea waamini ambao walipaswa kuwa walimu lakini bado wanahitaji maziwa, kwa sababu "chakula kigumu ni cha watu wazima, ambao akili zao, kwa kutumiwa, zimezoezwa kupambanua mema na mabaya" (Waebrania 5:14). Sikia maneno hayo — kwa kutumiwa. Ukomavu wa kimaadili si zawadi inayodondoshwa juu ya mwongofu mpya. Ni tunda la mazoezi, la kufanya mara kwa mara, la akili iliyozoezwa tena na tena katika mambo ya Mungu hadi inaweza kutofautisha jema na baya kama sikio lililofunzwa linavyotofautisha sauti sahihi ya muziki na sauti iliyoshuka.

And what is it all for? Here the world and the church diverge completely. The world studies ethics to make society function, to keep people from destroying one another, to be happy. None of those are bad things. But they are not the goal. The goal of Christian ethics is the glory of God. "Whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God" (1 Corinthians 10:31). That single verse reorders the entire enterprise. We do not pursue holiness to feel good about ourselves, or even mainly to help others, though it will do both. We pursue it because a holy God is worthy of a holy people, and because every right thing we do puts His character on display before a watching world. Ethics is worship with our hands and feet.

Na hayo yote ni kwa ajili ya nini? Hapa ulimwengu na kanisa vinaachana kabisa. Ulimwengu hujifunza maadili ili jamii ifanye kazi, ili kuwazuia watu wasiangamizane, ili kuwa na furaha. Hakuna kati ya hayo lililo baya. Lakini hayo si lengo. Lengo la maadili ya Kikristo ni utukufu wa Mungu. "Basi, mlapo, au mnywapo, au mfanyapo jambo lo lote, fanyeni yote kwa utukufu wa Mungu" (1 Wakorintho 10:31). Mstari huo mmoja unapanga upya kazi yote. Hatufuati utakatifu ili tujione vizuri, wala hata hasa ili tuwasaidie wengine, ingawa utafanya yote mawili. Tunaufuata kwa sababu Mungu mtakatifu anastahili watu watakatifu, na kwa sababu kila jambo jema tunalofanya linaonyesha tabia yake mbele ya ulimwengu unaotutazama. Maadili ni ibada kwa mikono na miguu yetu.
Section 1.2 — The Absolute Authority of Scripture
Kifungu 1.2 — Mamlaka Kamili ya Maandiko

Everything I have just said hangs on one conviction, and if that conviction goes, the whole structure comes down. The conviction is this: that Scripture is the very Word of God, and therefore carries God's own authority over how we live.

Kila kitu nilichosema hivi punde kinategemea imani moja thabiti, na imani hiyo ikiondoka, jengo lote linaanguka. Imani hiyo ni hii: kwamba Maandiko ni Neno la Mungu lenyewe, na kwa hiyo yana mamlaka ya Mungu Mwenyewe juu ya jinsi tunavyoishi.

"All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work."2 Timothy 3:16–17 (NKJV)

"Kila andiko lenye pumzi ya Mungu lafaa kwa mafundisho, na kwa kuwaonya watu makosa yao, na kwa kuwaongoza, na kwa kuwaadibu katika haki; ili mtu wa Mungu awe kamili, amekamilishwa apate kutenda kila tendo jema."<cite>2 Timotheo 3:16–17 (SUV)</cite>

Read that passage slowly, because Paul packs an entire doctrine of ethics into two verses. Scripture is God-breathed — it comes out of the mouth of God as surely as breath comes out of yours. That is its authority. And then notice the four uses Paul gives it: doctrine teaches us what is true, reproof shows us where we have gone wrong, correction sets us back on the path, and instruction in righteousness trains us to walk that path going forward. Teaching, rebuking, correcting, training — that is the full motion of a life being shaped by the Word. And mark the result Paul aims at: that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work. The Word is not merely sufficient to save us. It is sufficient to form us. There is no good work for which Scripture leaves the man of God unequipped.

Soma kifungu hicho polepole, kwa sababu Paulo anaweka fundisho zima la maadili katika mistari miwili. Maandiko yana pumzi ya Mungu — yanatoka kinywani mwa Mungu kwa uhakika kama pumzi inavyotoka kinywani mwako. Hayo ndiyo mamlaka yake. Kisha angalia matumizi manne ambayo Paulo anayataja: mafundisho hutufundisha yaliyo kweli, kuonya hutuonyesha tulipokosea, kuongoza hutuweka tena njiani, na kuadibu katika haki hutufunza kuitembea njia hiyo kuendelea mbele. Kufundisha, kukemea, kusahihisha, kufunza — huo ndio mwendo kamili wa maisha yanayoumbwa na Neno. Na tazama matokeo ambayo Paulo anayalenga: kwamba mtu wa Mungu awe kamili, amekamilishwa apate kutenda kila tendo jema. Neno halitoshi tu kutuokoa. Linatosha kutuunda. Hakuna tendo jema ambalo Maandiko yanamwacha mtu wa Mungu bila maandalizi kwalo.

This is what we mean by the sufficiency of Scripture, and for the pastor it is not an abstraction. It means that when a couple sits across from you with a marriage in pieces, when a young man confesses an addiction he cannot break, when an elder asks how the church should handle a member in open sin — you are not thrown back on your own cleverness or the latest book of techniques. You have a Word from God that is living and powerful, that judges the thoughts and intents of the heart (Hebrews 4:12), and that is able to make the man of God complete. The world will tell you that the Bible is an old book with nothing to say to modern problems. The man who has actually used it in the trenches of ministry knows better.

Hiki ndicho tunachomaanisha kwa utoshelevu wa Maandiko, na kwa mchungaji si wazo la kinadharia tu. Maana yake ni kwamba wanandoa wanapoketi mbele yako ndoa yao ikiwa imevunjika vipande vipande, kijana anapokiri uraibu ambao hawezi kuuvunja, mzee wa kanisa anapouliza jinsi kanisa linavyopaswa kumshughulikia mshirika aliye katika dhambi ya wazi — hutupwi kwenye werevu wako mwenyewe au kitabu cha karibuni cha mbinu. Una Neno kutoka kwa Mungu lililo hai, tena lenye nguvu, linalotambua mawazo na makusudi ya moyo (Waebrania 4:12), na linaloweza kumfanya mtu wa Mungu kuwa kamili. Ulimwengu utakuambia kwamba Biblia ni kitabu cha zamani kisicho na la kusema kuhusu matatizo ya kisasa. Mtu ambaye ameitumia kwa kweli katika mapambano ya huduma anajua zaidi.

Now, I want to be careful here, because the authority of Scripture is often misunderstood as a claim that the Bible gives a direct verse for every situation. It does not. There is no chapter and verse on whether to take a particular job or which medical treatment to pursue for a dying parent. But the sufficiency of Scripture does not mean Scripture answers every question by direct command; it means Scripture gives us everything we need — the truth about God, about ourselves, about right and wrong, and the wisdom of a renewed mind — to discern how to honor God in every situation. The Bible is not a card catalog of answers. It is the authoritative foundation on which all right reasoning is built.

Sasa, nataka kuwa mwangalifu hapa, kwa sababu mamlaka ya Maandiko mara nyingi hueleweka vibaya kana kwamba ni dai kwamba Biblia inatoa mstari wa moja kwa moja kwa kila hali. Haifanyi hivyo. Hakuna sura na mstari kuhusu iwapo uchukue kazi fulani au matibabu gani ya kumfuatilia mzazi anayekufa. Lakini utoshelevu wa Maandiko haumaanishi kwamba Maandiko yanajibu kila swali kwa amri ya moja kwa moja; unamaanisha kwamba Maandiko yanatupa kila kitu tunachohitaji — ukweli kuhusu Mungu, kuhusu sisi wenyewe, kuhusu mema na mabaya, na hekima ya akili iliyofanywa upya — ili kupambanua jinsi ya kumheshimu Mungu katika kila hali. Biblia si katalogi ya kadi za majibu. Ni msingi wenye mamlaka ambao juu yake hoja zote sahihi hujengwa.
Section 1.3 — The Contrast with Secular and Relativistic Approaches
Kifungu 1.3 — Tofauti na Mitazamo ya Kidunia na ya Uhusiano (Relativism)

To see what we have, it helps to see clearly what the world offers in its place. Strip away the labels and the academic vocabulary, and several real traditions recur. Consequentialism, including utilitarianism, locates the standard in outcomes: an act is right if it produces the greatest good for the greatest number. Deontological approaches locate it in reason and duty: right is whatever a rational person would will as a universal rule, regardless of outcome. Virtue ethics locates it in character: right action is what a person of practical wisdom would do, aimed at genuine human flourishing. Natural-law traditions — which this course itself draws on later, in its treatment of ordinary and extraordinary means at the end of life — hold that a real moral order is built into human nature and can be known by reason even without special revelation. Some thinkers in each of these traditions defend real, objective moral truth without grounding it explicitly in God; we should engage them honestly rather than caricature them. And some, though by no means all who reject a Christian foundation, land in relativism, the view that there is no fixed right and wrong, only your truth and my truth.

Ili kuona tulicho nacho, inasaidia kuona waziwazi kile ambacho ulimwengu unatoa mahali pake. Ukiondoa majina na msamiati wa kitaaluma, mapokeo kadhaa halisi hujitokeza tena na tena. Mtazamo wa matokeo (consequentialism), pamoja na falsafa ya manufaa (utilitarianism), huweka kipimo katika matokeo: tendo ni sahihi ikiwa linaleta wema mkubwa zaidi kwa idadi kubwa zaidi ya watu. Mitazamo ya wajibu (deontological) huweka kipimo katika akili na wajibu: sahihi ni kile ambacho mtu mwenye busara angetaka kiwe kanuni ya ulimwengu wote, bila kujali matokeo. Maadili ya fadhila (virtue ethics) huweka kipimo katika tabia: tendo sahihi ni lile ambalo mtu mwenye hekima ya kivitendo angefanya, likilenga ustawi halisi wa mwanadamu. Mapokeo ya sheria ya asili (natural law) — ambayo kozi hii yenyewe inayatumia baadaye, katika kushughulikia njia za kawaida na zisizo za kawaida za matibabu mwishoni mwa maisha — yanashikilia kwamba mpangilio halisi wa kimaadili umejengwa ndani ya asili ya mwanadamu na unaweza kujulikana kwa akili hata bila ufunuo maalum. Baadhi ya wanafikra katika kila moja ya mapokeo haya hutetea ukweli halisi wa kimaadili usiotegemea maoni bila kuuweka waziwazi juu ya Mungu; tunapaswa kujadiliana nao kwa uaminifu badala ya kuwakejeli. Na baadhi, ingawa si wote kamwe wanaokataa msingi wa Kikristo, huishia katika mtazamo wa uhusiano (relativism), yaani wazo kwamba hakuna jema na baya lisilobadilika, bali tu ukweli wako na ukweli wangu.

I am not asking you to dismiss these systems as if they contained nothing true. The man who studies consequences is right that actions have results and that love considers them. The relativist has correctly noticed that human judgments are fallible and culturally shaped. The error is never that these views see nothing; the error is where they finally rest their weight. They rest it on the creature. And a standard built on the creature can be no more stable, no more holy, and no more authoritative than the creature himself — which is to say, not very. The most honest secular thinkers admit this. Cut the moral law loose from God and you are left, in the end, with preference dressed up as principle.

Sikuombi uyatupilie mbali mifumo hii kana kwamba haina chochote cha kweli. Mtu anayechunguza matokeo yuko sahihi kwamba matendo yana matokeo na kwamba upendo huyazingatia. Mfuasi wa mtazamo wa uhusiano ametambua kwa usahihi kwamba hukumu za wanadamu zinaweza kukosea na zinaundwa na utamaduni. Kosa kamwe si kwamba mitazamo hii haioni chochote; kosa ni mahali inapoweka uzito wake hatimaye. Inauweka juu ya kiumbe. Na kipimo kilichojengwa juu ya kiumbe hakiwezi kuwa thabiti zaidi, kitakatifu zaidi, wala chenye mamlaka zaidi kuliko kiumbe chenyewe — yaani, si sana. Wanafikra wa kidunia walio waaminifu zaidi wanakiri hili. Ikate sheria ya kimaadili kutoka kwa Mungu na mwishowe unabaki na matakwa yaliyovikwa vazi la kanuni.

Here is the heart of the matter, and I want you to feel its weight as a pastor and not merely understand it as a student. Relativism cannot be lived. The man who tells you there is no objective right and wrong will, the moment you wrong him, appeal to a justice he claims does not exist. He cannot help it, because he is made in the image of God and the work of the law is written on his heart (Romans 2:15). This is your great point of contact with a lost world. You are not importing a foreign morality into people who have none. You are calling them back to the One whose law they already know in their conscience and have spent their lives suppressing. The relativist is not your opponent so much as your mission field, and the law he cannot escape is the schoolmaster meant to bring him to Christ.

Hapa ndipo kiini cha jambo, na nataka uhisi uzito wake kama mchungaji na si kulielewa tu kama mwanafunzi. Mtazamo wa uhusiano hauwezi kutekelezwa maishani. Mtu anayekuambia kwamba hakuna jema na baya halisi, mara tu utakapomkosea, atadai haki ambayo anasema haipo. Hawezi kujizuia, kwa sababu ameumbwa kwa sura ya Mungu na kazi ya torati imeandikwa moyoni mwake (Warumi 2:15). Hiki ndicho kituo chako kikuu cha kukutana na ulimwengu uliopotea. Huingizi maadili ya kigeni kwa watu wasio na maadili yoyote. Unawaita warudi kwa Yule ambaye sheria yake tayari wanaijua katika dhamiri yao na wametumia maisha yao kuikandamiza. Mfuasi wa mtazamo wa uhusiano si adui yako kama alivyo shamba lako la utume, na sheria asiyoweza kuikwepa ni kiongozi (mwalimu) aliyekusudiwa kumleta kwa Kristo.

Section 1.4 — Why Pastors Must Pursue Ethical Formation
Kifungu 1.4 — Kwa Nini Wachungaji Lazima Wafuatilie Malezi ya Kimaadili

Let me close this first unit by speaking to you directly about why this study matters for you in particular, more than for almost any other man in your congregation. There are at least three reasons, and each one should land on you with some weight.

Acha nimalizie sehemu hii ya kwanza kwa kusema nawe moja kwa moja kuhusu kwa nini somo hili lina maana kwako hasa, zaidi kuliko kwa karibu mtu mwingine yeyote katika kusanyiko lako. Kuna angalau sababu tatu, na kila moja inapaswa kukuangukia kwa uzito fulani.

The first is that you are held to a higher account. "My brethren, let not many of you become teachers, knowing that we shall receive a stricter judgment" (James 3:1). The man who teaches others how to live has taken up a burden the ordinary believer has not. God will not grade you on a curve because the work was hard. The teacher is judged as a teacher. That should sober you every time you open the Book to instruct another soul.

Ya kwanza ni kwamba unawajibishwa kwa kiwango cha juu zaidi. "Ndugu zangu, msiwe waalimu wengi, mkijua kwamba tutapata hukumu kubwa zaidi" (Yakobo 3:1). Mtu anayewafundisha wengine jinsi ya kuishi amebeba mzigo ambao mwamini wa kawaida hajabeba. Mungu hatakupa alama kwa kukulinganisha na wengine kwa sababu kazi ilikuwa ngumu. Mwalimu huhukumiwa kama mwalimu. Hilo linapaswa kukutia kiasi kila mara unapofungua Kitabu ili kufundisha nafsi nyingine.

The second is that you lead by example, not merely by instruction. Peter charges the elders to shepherd the flock "being examples to the flock" (1 Peter 5:3). Paul can say to the Corinthians, with no false modesty, "Imitate me, just as I also imitate Christ" (1 Corinthians 11:1). This is the heaviest and most searching part of pastoral ethics, and I have said something like it about preaching for years: it is not finally something you do, it is something you are. You can preach a sermon you have not lived, but you cannot pastor a people you are not. The congregation will absorb your character far more deeply than your words, and where the two contradict each other, your character will win the argument every time. A man may forget your finest sermon by Tuesday; he will never forget the year he watched how you treated your wife, or how you handled the deacon who opposed you, or what you did when no one but God was looking.

Ya pili ni kwamba unaongoza kwa mfano, si kwa mafundisho tu. Petro anawaagiza wazee kulichunga kundi "kwa kuwa vielelezo kwa lile kundi" (1 Petro 5:3). Paulo anaweza kuwaambia Wakorintho, bila unyenyekevu wa uongo, "Mnifuate mimi, kama mimi ninavyomfuata Kristo" (1 Wakorintho 11:1). Hii ndiyo sehemu nzito zaidi na inayochunguza zaidi ya maadili ya kichungaji, na nimesema jambo linalofanana na hili kuhusu kuhubiri kwa miaka mingi: hatimaye si kitu unachofanya, ni kitu ulicho. Unaweza kuhubiri mahubiri ambayo hujayaishi, lakini huwezi kuwachunga watu kwa kile usicho. Kusanyiko litapokea tabia yako kwa kina zaidi kuliko maneno yako, na mahali ambapo hayo mawili yanapingana, tabia yako itashinda hoja kila mara. Mtu anaweza kusahau mahubiri yako bora kufikia Jumanne; hatasahau kamwe mwaka ule alipoona jinsi ulivyomtendea mke wako, au jinsi ulivyomshughulikia shemasi aliyekupinga, au ulichofanya wakati hakuna aliyekuwa akitazama isipokuwa Mungu.

The third reason is the simplest and the most often forgotten. You pursue ethical formation because the gospel demands it of you as it demands it of every believer — not as the price of your salvation, which Christ has paid in full, but as its proper fruit. "We are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them" (Ephesians 2:10). You were not saved by your good works, but you were most certainly saved for them. The whole of this course rests on that order and never reverses it: grace first, always first, and then the holy life that grace produces. Keep that order straight and ethics becomes the joyful study of how a forgiven man learns to walk worthy of the One who bought him. Reverse it, and ethics curdles into a law that crushes. We will be careful, all the way through, to keep it straight.

Sababu ya tatu ni rahisi zaidi na ndiyo inayosahaulika mara nyingi zaidi. Unafuatilia malezi ya kimaadili kwa sababu injili inakudai hilo kama inavyomdai kila mwamini — si kama gharama ya wokovu wako, ambayo Kristo ameilipa kikamilifu, bali kama tunda lake linalostahili. "Maana tu kazi yake, tuliumbwa katika Kristo Yesu, tutende matendo mema, ambayo tangu awali Mungu aliyatengeneza ili tuenende nayo" (Waefeso 2:10). Hukuokolewa kwa matendo yako mema, lakini kwa hakika uliokolewa kwa ajili ya matendo hayo. Kozi hii yote inasimama juu ya mpangilio huo na kamwe haiugeuzi: neema kwanza, daima kwanza, kisha maisha matakatifu ambayo neema huzaa. Shika mpangilio huo sawasawa na maadili yanakuwa somo la furaha la jinsi mtu aliyesamehewa anavyojifunza kuenenda kama inavyostahili kwa Yule aliyemnunua. Ugeuze, na maadili yanageuka kuwa sheria inayoponda. Tutakuwa waangalifu, njia yote, kuushika sawasawa.

Section 10.1 — The Christian in the World: Citizenship, Culture, and Discernment
Kipengele 10.1 — Mkristo Ulimwenguni: Uraia, Utamaduni na Utambuzi

The believer lives in two kingdoms at once, and learning to do so faithfully is no small part of Christian ethics. Our Lord settled the basic principle when He held up a coin and said, "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's" (Matthew 22:21). The Christian owes the governing authorities real obedience — Paul tells us they are ordained of God and we are to be subject to them (Romans 13:1) — and yet that obedience is never absolute, for Caesar himself belongs to God, and when the state commands what God forbids or forbids what God commands, we must obey God rather than men. The pastor must teach his people to be the best of citizens and never the state's lapdogs, honoring the magistrate without ever handing him the conscience that belongs to God alone.

Mwamini anaishi katika falme mbili kwa wakati mmoja, na kujifunza kufanya hivyo kwa uaminifu si sehemu ndogo ya maadili ya Kikristo. Bwana wetu aliiweka kanuni ya msingi alipoinua sarafu na kusema, "Mlipeni Kaisari yaliyo ya Kaisari, na Mungu yaliyo ya Mungu" (Mathayo 22:21). Mkristo anawiwa na mamlaka zinazotawala utii wa kweli — Paulo anatuambia kwamba zimeamriwa na Mungu na kwamba tunapaswa kuzitii (Warumi 13:1) — lakini utii huo kamwe si wa mwisho kabisa, kwa maana Kaisari mwenyewe ni mali ya Mungu, na serikali inapoamuru kile ambacho Mungu anakataza au kukataza kile ambacho Mungu anaamuru, imetupasa kumtii Mungu kuliko wanadamu. Mchungaji anapaswa kuwafundisha watu wake kuwa raia bora kuliko wote na kamwe wasiwe vibaraka wa serikali, wakimheshimu mtawala bila kamwe kumkabidhi dhamiri iliyo mali ya Mungu peke yake.

The same wisdom governs the believer's stance toward the wider culture, and here two opposite errors beckon. One is the fortress — withdrawal into a Christian bunker, refusing all engagement, hiding the light under a basket. The other is the chameleon — blending so completely into the surrounding culture that the church becomes indistinguishable from the world it was meant to transform. Scripture rejects both: "do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind" (Romans 12:2). We are neither to flee the world nor to be squeezed into its mold, but to engage it with discernment — and that discernment extends to the screens, the media, and the technologies that now disciple our people more hours of the week than we do. Teach your flock to weigh what they watch and consume, neither swallowing the culture whole nor fearing it, but testing all things and holding fast what is good.

Hekima ileile inaongoza msimamo wa mwamini kuelekea utamaduni mpana, na hapa makosa mawili yanayopingana yanavutia. Moja ni ngome — kujitenga ndani ya handaki la Kikristo, kukataa kujihusisha kwa namna yoyote, kuificha taa chini ya pishi. Lingine ni kinyonga — kujichanganya kabisa na utamaduni unaozunguka hata kanisa linakuwa halitofautiani na ulimwengu ambao lilikusudiwa kuubadilisha. Maandiko yanakataa yote mawili: "Wala msiifuatishe namna ya dunia hii; bali mgeuzwe kwa kufanywa upya nia zenu" (Warumi 12:2). Hatupaswi kuukimbia ulimwengu wala kubanwa katika kalibu yake, bali kujihusisha nao kwa utambuzi — na utambuzi huo unafikia hata skrini, vyombo vya habari, na teknolojia ambazo sasa zinawafundisha watu wetu kama wanafunzi saa nyingi zaidi kwa juma kuliko tunavyofanya sisi. Lifundishe kundi lako kupima kile wanachotazama na kutumia, wasiumeze utamaduni wote mzima wala kuuogopa, bali wakijaribu mambo yote na kulishika lililo jema.

One further sphere belongs here: the care of God's creation. The dominion granted to humanity in the beginning was never a license to plunder but a charge to steward; Adam was placed in the garden "to tend and keep it" (Genesis 2:15). The Christian neither worships the creation as the pagan does nor despises it as the careless do, but cares for it as a faithful steward of what belongs to God — one more arena in which our ethics confess whose world this is.

Eneo moja zaidi linahusika hapa: kuutunza uumbaji wa Mungu. Mamlaka ya kutawala waliyopewa wanadamu hapo mwanzo hayakuwa kamwe ruhusa ya kuteka nyara bali agizo la kuwa mawakili; Adamu aliwekwa bustanini "ailime na kuitunza" (Mwanzo 2:15). Mkristo haubudu uumbaji kama mpagani afanyavyo, wala haudharau kama wazembe wafanyavyo, bali anautunza kama wakili mwaminifu wa kile kilicho mali ya Mungu — uwanja mmoja zaidi ambamo maadili yetu yanakiri kwamba ulimwengu huu ni wa nani.
Section 10.2 — Judged for Judging: Discernment Without Hypocrisy
Kipengele 10.2 — Kuhukumiwa kwa Kuhukumu: Utambuzi Usio na Unafiki

No verse is more often hurled at the faithful pastor than our Lord's "Judge not, that you be not judged" (Matthew 7:1), wielded by a culture that means by it that no one may ever call anything wrong. So we must understand the passage rightly, because a misreading disarms the church and a right reading arms her. Jesus is not forbidding all moral discernment — that would contradict His own commands and the rest of Scripture. He is forbidding hypocritical judgment, the judgment of a man with a plank in his own eye fussing over the speck in his brother's. And notice what He commands after the rebuke: "First remove the plank from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye" (Matthew 7:5). The goal is not to stop helping the brother; it is to deal with yourself first so that you can help him without hypocrisy. Self-examination comes first — always first — and that order must be at least as sharp in the pastor's heart as his readiness to correct others, or he becomes the very hypocrite the Lord condemns.

Hakuna mstari unaorushwa mara nyingi zaidi kwa mchungaji mwaminifu kuliko ule wa Bwana wetu, "Msihukumu, msije mkahukumiwa" (Mathayo 7:1), unaotumiwa na utamaduni unaomaanisha kwa maneno hayo kwamba hakuna mtu anayeruhusiwa kamwe kusema jambo lolote ni baya. Kwa hiyo ni lazima tuelewe kifungu hiki sawasawa, kwa sababu kukisoma vibaya kunalinyang'anya kanisa silaha na kukisoma sawasawa kunalipa silaha. Yesu hakatazi utambuzi wote wa kimaadili — jambo hilo lingepingana na amri zake mwenyewe na Maandiko mengine yote. Anakataza hukumu ya kinafiki, hukumu ya mtu mwenye boriti katika jicho lake mwenyewe anayehangaika na kibanzi kilicho katika jicho la ndugu yake. Na angalia anachoamuru baada ya karipio hilo: "Toa kwanza boriti iliyo katika jicho lako mwenyewe, ndipo utakapoona vema kukitoa kibanzi kilicho katika jicho la ndugu yako" (Mathayo 7:5). Lengo si kuacha kumsaidia ndugu; ni kujishughulikia mwenyewe kwanza ili uweze kumsaidia bila unafiki. Kujichunguza huja kwanza — daima kwanza — na mpangilio huo unapaswa kuwa mkali katika moyo wa mchungaji angalau kama utayari wake wa kuwasahihisha wengine, la sivyo anakuwa yule mnafiki halisi ambaye Bwana anamhukumu.

Once the plank is out, however, the church is not only permitted but commanded to judge. Our Lord said elsewhere, "Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment" (John 7:24) — not do not judge, but judge rightly. Paul rebuked the Corinthians for failing to judge a sinning member, saying plainly that while we do not judge outsiders, "do you not judge those who are inside?" (1 Corinthians 5:12). The discernment that distinguishes good from evil, names sin as sin, and lovingly corrects the erring brother is not the forbidden thing; it is Christian maturity, the very thing Hebrews said the mature possess. What is forbidden is the censorious, hypocritical, self-righteous spirit that condemns others to feel superior.

Lakini boriti ikishaondolewa, kanisa si kwamba linaruhusiwa tu bali linaamriwa kuhukumu. Bwana wetu alisema mahali pengine, "Msihukumu kwa macho tu, bali hukumuni hukumu iliyo ya haki" (Yohana 7:24) — si msihukumu, bali hukumuni kwa haki. Paulo aliwakemea Wakorintho kwa kushindwa kumhukumu mshiriki aliyekuwa akitenda dhambi, akisema waziwazi kwamba ingawa hatuwahukumu walio nje, "Je! Ninyi hamwahukumu walio ndani?" (1 Wakorintho 5:12). Utambuzi unaotofautisha mema na mabaya, unaoiita dhambi kuwa dhambi, na unaomsahihisha kwa upendo ndugu aliyekosa si jambo lililokatazwa; ni ukomavu wa Kikristo, jambo lilelile ambalo Waebrania walisema watu wazima kiroho wanalo. Kinachokatazwa ni roho ya kulaumu, ya kinafiki, ya kujiona mwenye haki, inayowahukumu wengine ili kujiona bora kuliko wao.

So the faithful pastor needs courage — courage to teach the truth and call sin by its name in an age that will brand him "judgmental" for doing so. But that courage must be wedded, every step, to the humility of a man who has first judged himself. Discernment without self-examination curdles into Pharisaism; self-examination without discernment collapses into cowardice. The shepherd is called to both at once.

Kwa hiyo mchungaji mwaminifu anahitaji ujasiri — ujasiri wa kufundisha kweli na kuiita dhambi kwa jina lake katika zama zitakazomwita "mtu wa kuhukumu" kwa kufanya hivyo. Lakini ujasiri huo unapaswa kuunganishwa, kila hatua, na unyenyekevu wa mtu ambaye kwanza amejihukumu mwenyewe. Utambuzi usio na kujichunguza huchachuka na kuwa Ufarisayo; kujichunguza kusiko na utambuzi huporomoka na kuwa woga. Mchungaji ameitwa kwa yote mawili kwa wakati mmoja.
Section 10.3 — Restoring the Fallen: The Goal of All Discipline
Kipengele 10.3 — Kuwarejesha Walioanguka: Lengo la Nidhamu Yote

We said in Unit 6 that the first purpose of all church discipline is the restoration of the sinner, never his destruction. Now we must learn how that restoration is actually accomplished, for it is one of the most delicate and most neglected works of the ministry. The pattern is given in 2 Corinthians 2, where Paul writes about a repentant offender under discipline — traditionally identified with the man of 1 Corinthians 5, though scholars debate whether this is the same case or a separate offense from Paul's painful visit; the pastoral principle holds either way. The man has now repented — and Paul's instruction is urgent and tender. The punishment has done its work; therefore, he says, the church must do three things: "you ought rather to forgive and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one be swallowed up with too much sorrow" (2 Corinthians 2:7), and then, "reaffirm your love to him" (2:8). Forgive, comfort, reaffirm love. Discipline that does not aim relentlessly at this glad ending has missed its purpose entirely.

Tulisema katika Sehemu ya 6 kwamba kusudi la kwanza la nidhamu yote ya kanisa ni kurejeshwa kwa mwenye dhambi, kamwe si kuangamizwa kwake. Sasa ni lazima tujifunze jinsi urejesho huo unavyotimizwa hasa, kwa maana ni mojawapo ya kazi za huduma zinazohitaji uangalifu mkubwa zaidi na zinazopuuzwa zaidi. Kielelezo kimetolewa katika 2 Wakorintho 2, ambapo Paulo anaandika kuhusu mkosaji aliyetubu aliye chini ya nidhamu — ambaye kwa mapokeo hutambuliwa kuwa yule mtu wa 1 Wakorintho 5, ingawa wasomi wanajadiliana kama hili ni tukio lilelile au kosa jingine linalohusiana na ziara ya Paulo yenye maumivu; kanuni ya kichungaji inasimama vyovyote vile. Mtu huyo sasa ametubu — na agizo la Paulo ni la haraka na la upole. Adhabu imefanya kazi yake; kwa hiyo, anasema, kanisa linapaswa kufanya mambo matatu: "afadhali mmsamehe na kumfariji, mtu huyo asije akamezwa na huzuni yake iliyozidi" (2 Wakorintho 2:7), kisha, "mmthibitishie upendo wenu" (2:8). Kusamehe, kufariji, kuthibitisha upendo. Nidhamu isiyolenga bila kukoma mwisho huu wa furaha imelikosa kusudi lake kabisa.

Two warnings frame the process. Paul says to restore the penitent "lest Satan should take advantage of us" (2 Corinthians 2:11) — for the enemy is as pleased by a church that will not forgive the repentant as by the sin that began it all. The danger runs in both directions. But genuine restoration also requires the discernment we have just studied: the pastor must distinguish true repentance from its counterfeit, "godly sorrow" that "produces repentance leading to salvation" from the merely "sorrow of the world" that is only regret at being caught (2 Corinthians 7:10). Real repentance bears fruit; it is not mere tears but a turning.

Maonyo mawili yanauzunguka mchakato huu. Paulo anasema mwenye kutubu arejeshwe "Shetani asije akapata nafasi ya kutushinda" (2 Wakorintho 2:11) — kwa maana adui hufurahishwa na kanisa lisilotaka kumsamehe aliyetubu kama anavyofurahishwa na dhambi iliyoanzisha yote. Hatari inakwenda pande zote mbili. Lakini urejesho wa kweli pia unahitaji utambuzi ambao tumetoka kujifunza: mchungaji anapaswa kutofautisha toba ya kweli na ile ya kuigiza, "huzuni iliyo ya kimungu" ambayo "hufanya toba iletayo wokovu" na ile "huzuni ya kidunia" ambayo ni majuto tu ya kukamatwa (2 Wakorintho 7:10). Toba halisi huzaa matunda; si machozi tu bali ni kugeuka.

From this flow the practical wisdom of restoration: a process that is neither rushed nor refused. To restore a fallen man too quickly — especially a fallen leader — before repentance has been tested and trust rebuilt, is to wound the church and often the man himself; but to refuse ever to restore a truly penitent brother is the unforgiving cruelty Paul expressly forbids. Wise restoration often takes the form of a clear, written path: defined steps, a season of proven faithfulness, gradual reintegration into fellowship and, where appropriate and only in time, into service, with ongoing care long after the formal process has ended. The aim throughout is a brother fully healed and a body made whole, to the glory of the God who restores.

Kutokana na hili hutokea hekima ya kivitendo ya urejesho: mchakato usioharakishwa wala usiokataliwa. Kumrejesha mtu aliyeanguka haraka mno — hasa kiongozi aliyeanguka — kabla toba yake haijajaribiwa na uaminifu kujengwa upya, ni kulijeruhi kanisa na mara nyingi mtu huyo mwenyewe; lakini kukataa kabisa kumrejesha ndugu aliyetubu kweli ni ukatili usiosamehe ambao Paulo anaukataza waziwazi. Urejesho wenye hekima mara nyingi huchukua umbo la njia iliyo wazi na iliyoandikwa: hatua zilizoelezwa, kipindi cha uaminifu uliothibitishwa, kurudishwa hatua kwa hatua katika ushirika na, inapofaa na kwa wakati wake tu, katika huduma, pamoja na uangalizi unaoendelea muda mrefu baada ya mchakato rasmi kumalizika. Lengo katika yote ni ndugu aliyeponywa kabisa na mwili uliofanywa mzima, kwa utukufu wa Mungu anayerejesha.

Section 10.4 — Capstone: Living and Finishing Faithfully
Kipengele 10.4 — Hitimisho Kuu: Kuishi na Kumaliza kwa Uaminifu

We come to the end of our course, and it is fitting to gather what we have learned into a life rather than leave it as a list. Across ten units we have seen one truth hold everything together: Christian ethics is never a ladder we climb to earn God's favor, but the fruit of a favor already given. We began there in Unit 1, and we have refused all the way through to reverse it. Grace first, always first — and then the holy life that grace produces. Every duty we have studied, from the guarding of the marriage bed to the handling of the church's money to the restoration of the fallen, is simply what gratitude looks like when it is worked out in the thousand decisions of a ministry.

Tumefika mwisho wa kozi yetu, na inafaa tukusanye yale tuliyojifunza yawe maisha badala ya kuyaacha kama orodha. Katika sehemu zote kumi tumeona kweli moja ikishikilia kila kitu pamoja: maadili ya Kikristo kamwe si ngazi tunayopanda ili kupata kibali cha Mungu, bali ni tunda la kibali ambacho tayari tumepewa. Tulianzia hapo katika Sehemu ya 1, na tumekataa njia yote kuugeuza mpangilio huo. Neema kwanza, daima kwanza — kisha maisha matakatifu ambayo neema huyazaa. Kila wajibu tuliojifunza, kuanzia kulinda kitanda cha ndoa hadi kushughulikia fedha za kanisa hadi kuwarejesha walioanguka, ni namna shukrani inavyoonekana tu inapotendwa katika maamuzi elfu ya huduma.

To help you carry it, I urge you to do what faithful ministers have long done: write your own Pastoral Ethics Statement — a settled, personal declaration of the convictions and commitments by which you will conduct your ministry, drawn from all we have covered. Decide in the calm, as we said of the ministerial code in Unit 5, what you will do in the storm. Commit it to paper, submit it to accountability, and review it on your knees. And resolve upon a lifetime of vigilance, for as we learned in Unit 3, no man falls all at once; he drifts, and only watchfulness and honest brothers keep a man from the slow slide.

Ili kukusaidia kubeba haya, nakusihi ufanye kile ambacho wahudumu waaminifu wamefanya kwa muda mrefu: andika Tamko lako la Maadili ya Kichungaji — tangazo la kibinafsi, lililotulia, la misimamo na ahadi ambazo kwazo utaiendesha huduma yako, likitokana na yote tuliyojifunza. Amua wakati wa utulivu, kama tulivyosema kuhusu kanuni za maadili za mhudumu katika Sehemu ya 5, utakachofanya wakati wa dhoruba. Liandike kwenye karatasi, liweke chini ya uwajibikaji, na lipitie tena ukiwa umepiga magoti. Na uazimie kuwa macho maisha yako yote, kwa maana kama tulivyojifunza katika Sehemu ya 3, hakuna mtu anayeanguka mara moja; huteleza polepole, na ni kukesha tu na ndugu waaminifu wanaomwambia kweli ndio humzuia mtu asiteleze polepole na kuanguka.

Let me leave you with the sobering picture our Lord Himself used, the rich man and Lazarus (Luke 16). A wealthy man feasted in comfort every day while a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, longing for the crumbs. The rich man did Lazarus no violence; his sin was simply that he stepped over him, day after day, and did nothing. Then both men died, and the comfortable man "in torments... lifted up his eyes" and saw, too late, across an unbridgeable gulf, the beggar he had ignored now comforted in glory. There is the great reversal that ought to govern how a pastor lives, gives, judges, and shepherds now — for we will all lift up our eyes one day and give account. Do not be the man who steps over the Lazarus at his gate, whether that Lazarus is the poor, the fallen brother awaiting restoration, the wounded soul in the pew, or the family in his own home. See the person God has set before you. Spend yourself for him.

Niwaachie picha ya kutia moyo uzito ambayo Bwana wetu mwenyewe aliitumia, ile ya tajiri na Lazaro (Luka 16). Tajiri mmoja alifanya karamu kwa starehe kila siku huku mwombaji aitwaye Lazaro akilala langoni pake, akitamani makombo. Tajiri hakumtendea Lazaro jeuri yoyote; dhambi yake ilikuwa tu kwamba alimpita juu yake, siku baada ya siku, na hakufanya lolote. Kisha watu wote wawili wakafa, na yule aliyekuwa akistarehe, "alipokuwa katika mateso, akainua macho yake" akaona, wakati umekwisha pita, ng'ambo ya shimo kubwa lisilovukika, yule mwombaji aliyempuuza sasa akifarijiwa katika utukufu. Hapo ndipo ulipo ule mgeuko mkuu unaopaswa kuongoza jinsi mchungaji anavyoishi, anavyotoa, anavyohukumu, na anavyochunga sasa — kwa maana sote tutainua macho yetu siku moja na kutoa hesabu. Usiwe mtu anayempita Lazaro aliye langoni pake, awe Lazaro huyo ni maskini, ndugu aliyeanguka anayengoja kurejeshwa, nafsi iliyojeruhiwa iliyoketi kanisani, au familia iliyo katika nyumba yake mwenyewe. Mwone mtu ambaye Mungu amemweka mbele yako. Jitoe kwa ajili yake.

And so we end where a faithful ministry ends, with the testimony first sounded in Unit 3: "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith" (2 Timothy 4:7). The goal was never merely to begin well, nor to be admired, nor to avoid scandal. The goal is to finish — to stand at the last having been, by the grace of God, a faithful and holy shepherd of the flock He bought with His own blood. May God grant it to every man who has studied these things, and may the grace that called you keep you to the end.

Na hivyo tunamaliza mahali ambapo huduma ya uaminifu humalizikia, kwa ushuhuda uliotolewa kwanza katika Sehemu ya 3: "Nimevipiga vita vilivyo vizuri, mwendo nimeumaliza, imani nimeilinda" (2 Timotheo 4:7). Lengo halikuwa kamwe kuanza vizuri tu, wala kusifiwa, wala kuepuka kashfa. Lengo ni kumaliza — kusimama mwishoni ukiwa umekuwa, kwa neema ya Mungu, mchungaji mwaminifu na mtakatifu wa kundi alilolinunua kwa damu yake mwenyewe. Mungu amjalie hilo kila mtu aliyejifunza mambo haya, na neema iliyokuita ikulinde hadi mwisho.

Section 2.1 — The Holy Character of God as the Ground of All Ethics
Kifungu 2.1 — Tabia Takatifu ya Mungu kama Msingi wa Maadili Yote

In the first unit we said that Christian ethics measures every action against God's own character. Now we must ask the obvious next question: what is that character, and why should it be the measure of anything? If you do not settle this, everything that follows will float free of its anchor. So let us put the anchor down deep. The ground of all ethics is the holiness of God — not a rule He keeps, but the very purity of who He is. "Be holy, for I am holy" (1 Peter 1:16, citing Leviticus). Notice the logic of that command. God does not say, be holy because holiness works, or because the community needs it. He says, be holy because I am. The reason for the standard is the nature of God Himself.

Katika sehemu ya kwanza tulisema kwamba maadili ya Kikristo hupima kila tendo kwa kulinganisha na tabia ya Mungu Mwenyewe. Sasa lazima tuulize swali linalofuata waziwazi: tabia hiyo ni nini, na kwa nini iwe kipimo cha chochote? Usipolitatua hili, kila kitu kinachofuata kitaelea bila nanga yake. Basi na tuishushe nanga chini kabisa. Msingi wa maadili yote ni utakatifu wa Mungu — si kanuni anayoishika, bali usafi wenyewe wa jinsi alivyo. "Mtakuwa watakatifu kwa kuwa mimi ni mtakatifu" (1 Petro 1:16, akinukuu Mambo ya Walawi). Angalia mantiki ya amri hiyo. Mungu hasemi, iweni watakatifu kwa sababu utakatifu unafanya kazi, au kwa sababu jamii inauhitaji. Anasema, iweni watakatifu kwa kuwa Mimi ni. Sababu ya kipimo ni asili ya Mungu Mwenyewe.

Let me give you a picture I have carried since boyhood. My father grew up on a farm, and in those days a farmer had to do his own carpentry, so for a few years he made his living as a carpenter. In our garage there were some very old tools, and one of them was a plumb line made of brass. It was a simple thing — a weight on a string — but it did one job perfectly: hung against a wall, gravity pulled it true, and it showed you at once whether the wall was straight. The plumb line does not argue and it does not flatter; it simply does not lie. When the Lord showed Amos a plumb line set in the midst of His people, that was the point. Ethics is not finally a matter of our preferences, our traditions, or how a thing looks from the outside. There is a standard, fixed and true, and it measures us whether we consent to it or not. The whole of Christian ethics begins here: not with what we feel is right, but with the straight line God Himself has set beside our lives.

Acha nikupe picha ambayo nimeibeba tangu utotoni. Baba yangu alikulia shambani, na siku zile mkulima alilazimika kufanya useremala wake mwenyewe, kwa hiyo kwa miaka michache alijipatia riziki kama seremala. Katika gereji yetu kulikuwa na zana za zamani sana, na mojawapo ilikuwa timazi la shaba. Kilikuwa kitu rahisi — uzito uliofungwa kwenye uzi — lakini kilifanya kazi moja kikamilifu: kikining'inizwa kando ya ukuta, nguvu ya uvutano ilikivuta sawasawa, nacho kilikuonyesha mara moja kama ukuta umesimama wima. Timazi halibishani wala halibembelezi; halidanganyi tu. BWANA alipomwonyesha Amosi timazi katikati ya watu wake, hilo ndilo lilikuwa kusudi. Maadili hatimaye si suala la matakwa yetu, mapokeo yetu, au jinsi jambo linavyoonekana kwa nje. Kuna kipimo, kisichobadilika na cha kweli, nacho kinatupima tukikubali au tusikubali. Maadili yote ya Kikristo yanaanzia hapa: si na kile tunachohisi kuwa sawa, bali na mstari ulionyooka ambao Mungu Mwenyewe ameuweka kando ya maisha yetu.

This protects us from two ancient errors, and I want you to be able to name them, because your people will stumble into both. The first error says that things are good because God arbitrarily commands them — that He could have called murder righteous if He had chosen to, and good is simply whatever the Almighty happens to decree. That makes God a tyrant and goodness a coin-flip. The second error says that things are good by some standard above God, to which even He must bow — which makes God no longer God, but a servant of a higher law. The biblical answer slices cleanly between them: a thing is good because it reflects the unchanging character of God. Goodness is neither arbitrary nor above Him. It is Him, expressed. His commands are not random and they are not borrowed; they are the overflow of His own perfect nature.

Hili linatulinda dhidi ya makosa mawili ya kale, nami nataka uweze kuyataja, kwa sababu watu wako watajikwaa katika yote mawili. Kosa la kwanza linasema kwamba mambo ni mema kwa sababu Mungu anayaamuru kiholela — kwamba angeweza kuuita uuaji kuwa haki kama angechagua hivyo, na kwamba wema ni chochote tu ambacho Mwenyezi ameamua kuamuru. Hilo linamfanya Mungu kuwa dhalimu na wema kuwa kama kurusha sarafu. Kosa la pili linasema kwamba mambo ni mema kwa kipimo fulani kilicho juu ya Mungu, ambacho hata Yeye lazima akiinamie — jambo linalomfanya Mungu asiwe Mungu tena, bali mtumishi wa sheria iliyo juu zaidi. Jibu la kibiblia linapita katikati yao kwa usafi: jambo ni jema kwa sababu linaakisi tabia isiyobadilika ya Mungu. Wema si wa kiholela wala hauko juu yake. Ni Yeye, akijidhihirisha. Amri zake si za bahati nasibu wala hazikukopwa; ni kufurika kwa asili yake kamilifu.

From this single truth flows a principle we will lean on again and again in this course, one I have taught for years and built into our Systematic Theology: every human being is made in the image of God, and therefore every human being possesses a worth that cannot be earned, diminished, or revoked. "So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them" (Genesis 1:27). That worth does not rise and fall with a man's usefulness, his health, his morality, or his agreement with us. It is irreducible, because it is grounded not in him but in the God whose image he bears. Hold onto that. When we reach the sanctity of life, the treatment of the poor, and the discipline of the sinning brother, this is the principle we will be applying.

Kutokana na ukweli huu mmoja inatiririka kanuni tutakayoitegemea tena na tena katika kozi hii, kanuni ambayo nimeifundisha kwa miaka mingi na kuijenga ndani ya Teolojia yetu ya Kimfumo: kila mwanadamu ameumbwa kwa sura ya Mungu, na kwa hiyo kila mwanadamu ana thamani isiyoweza kupatikana kwa juhudi, kupunguzwa, wala kunyang'anywa. "Mungu akaumba mtu kwa mfano wake, kwa mfano wa Mungu alimwumba; mwanamume na mwanamke aliwaumba" (Mwanzo 1:27). Thamani hiyo haipandi wala haishuki kutegemea manufaa ya mtu, afya yake, maadili yake, au kukubaliana kwake nasi. Haipunguziki, kwa sababu msingi wake si ndani yake bali ndani ya Mungu ambaye sura yake anaibeba. Lishike hilo. Tutakapofika kwenye utakatifu wa uhai, jinsi ya kuwatendea maskini, na nidhamu ya ndugu anayetenda dhambi, hii ndiyo kanuni tutakayokuwa tukiitumia.

Section 2.2 — Law and Fulfillment: The Moral Law and the Coming of Christ
Kifungu 2.2 — Sheria na Utimilizo: Sheria ya Kimaadili na Kuja kwa Kristo

If God's character is the standard, the law is the place where that character was written down for us in words. God did not leave us to guess at His holiness. He built a moral order into the very creation, and then He stated it plainly at Sinai. The Ten Commandments are not ten arbitrary rules; they are a portrait of God's character translated into the shape of a human life — one God, no idols, His name honored, His day kept, and then the horizontal commands that protect life, marriage, property, truth, and the contented heart.

Ikiwa tabia ya Mungu ndiyo kipimo, torati ndiyo mahali ambapo tabia hiyo iliandikwa kwa ajili yetu kwa maneno. Mungu hakutuacha tukisie utakatifu wake. Alijenga mpangilio wa kimaadili ndani ya uumbaji wenyewe, kisha akautamka waziwazi pale Sinai. Amri Kumi si kanuni kumi za kiholela; ni picha ya tabia ya Mungu iliyotafsiriwa katika umbo la maisha ya mwanadamu — Mungu mmoja, hakuna sanamu, jina lake liheshimiwe, siku yake ishikwe, kisha amri za kando kwa kando (kati ya mtu na mtu) zinazolinda uhai, ndoa, mali, ukweli, na moyo uliotosheka.

Conservative teachers have long found it useful to distinguish three strands within the law of Moses: the ceremonial law that governed sacrifice and temple, the civil law that ordered the nation of Israel, and the moral law that expresses God's unchanging will. The ceremonial pointed forward to Christ and is fulfilled in Him; the civil was given to a particular nation in a particular time; but the moral law, rooted in God's own nature, abides. This is why we still teach the Ten Commandments and no longer offer lambs. Learn this distinction well, because much confusion in the church comes from collapsing it — either binding people to laws Christ has fulfilled, or discarding moral commands that still stand.

Walimu wahafidhina kwa muda mrefu wameona inafaa kutofautisha nyuzi tatu ndani ya torati ya Musa: sheria ya kiibada iliyotawala dhabihu na hekalu, sheria ya kiraia iliyopanga taifa la Israeli, na sheria ya kimaadili inayoeleza mapenzi ya Mungu yasiyobadilika. Sheria ya kiibada ilielekeza mbele kwa Kristo na imetimizwa ndani yake; ya kiraia ilitolewa kwa taifa fulani katika wakati fulani; lakini sheria ya kimaadili, yenye mizizi katika asili ya Mungu Mwenyewe, inadumu. Hii ndiyo sababu bado tunafundisha Amri Kumi lakini hatutoi tena wana-kondoo. Jifunze tofauti hii vizuri, kwa sababu machafuko mengi kanisani hutokana na kuichanganya — ama kuwafunga watu kwa sheria ambazo Kristo amezitimiza, ama kutupilia mbali amri za kimaadili ambazo bado zinasimama.

Then came the Lord Jesus, and here a careful word is needed, for many imagine that He came to soften or set aside the law. He says the opposite. "Do not think that I came to destroy the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to destroy but to fulfill" (Matthew 5:17). And in the Sermon on the Mount He does not lower the law's demand; He drives it inward to the heart. You have heard it said, do not murder — but I say, do not even nurse the anger that kills. You have heard, do not commit adultery — but I say, do not even harbor the lust that betrays. Christ takes the law off the surface of behavior and presses it down into the thoughts and intents, exactly where 2 Timothy told us the Word reaches. This is progressive revelation at its summit: not a new and contradictory standard, but the full unveiling of what the law always meant. The One who gave the law on the mountain now expounds it on another, and then goes to a third to fulfill its every demand in His own body.

Kisha akaja Bwana Yesu, na hapa neno la uangalifu linahitajika, kwa maana wengi hudhani kwamba alikuja kuilainisha au kuiweka kando torati. Yeye anasema kinyume chake. "Msidhani ya kuwa nalikuja kuitangua torati au manabii; la, sikuja kutangua, bali kutimiliza" (Mathayo 5:17). Na katika Mahubiri ya Mlimani hapunguzi dai la torati; analisukuma ndani hadi moyoni. Mmesikia kwamba imenenwa, usiue — lakini mimi nawaambia, hata msiilee hasira inayoua. Mmesikia, usizini — lakini mimi nawaambia, hata msiihifadhi tamaa inayosaliti. Kristo anaiondoa torati kutoka juu juu ya mwenendo na kuikandamiza chini hadi kwenye mawazo na makusudi, mahali hasa ambapo 2 Timotheo ilituambia Neno hufika. Huu ni ufunuo unaoendelea katika kilele chake: si kipimo kipya kinachopingana, bali kufunuliwa kikamilifu kwa kile ambacho torati ilimaanisha siku zote. Yule aliyetoa torati juu ya mlima sasa anaifafanua juu ya mlima mwingine, kisha anakwenda kwenye mlima wa tatu kutimiza kila dai lake katika mwili wake Mwenyewe.
Section 2.3 — Grace-Empowered Obedience and the Fruit of the Spirit
Kifungu 2.3 — Utii Unaowezeshwa na Neema na Tunda la Roho

Now we arrive at the hinge of the whole Christian life, and if a man gets this wrong he will either despair or grow proud, and often both by turns. The question is this: once we see the law in all its inward, heart-searching demand, how can any of us hope to keep it? And the honest biblical answer is that, left to ourselves, we cannot. "There is none righteous, no, not one" (Romans 3:10). The law was never given as a ladder to climb to God. One of its great purposes is to be the mirror that shows us our filth and drives us, despairing of ourselves, to the cross. The law diagnoses; it cannot cure.

Sasa tunafika kwenye bawaba ya maisha yote ya Kikristo, na mtu akikosea hapa atakata tamaa au atajivuna, na mara nyingi yote mawili kwa zamu. Swali ni hili: tukishaiona torati katika dai lake lote la ndani linalochunguza moyo, yeyote kati yetu anawezaje kutumaini kuishika? Na jibu la kweli la kibiblia ni kwamba, tukiachwa wenyewe, hatuwezi. "Hakuna mwenye haki hata mmoja" (Warumi 3:10). Torati haikutolewa kamwe kama ngazi ya kupanda kwa Mungu. Mojawapo ya makusudi yake makuu ni kuwa kioo kinachotuonyesha uchafu wetu na kutusukuma, tukiwa tumekata tamaa juu yetu wenyewe, hadi msalabani. Torati hutambua ugonjwa; haiwezi kuponya.

The cure is the gospel. In Christ, the demand of the law is satisfied and its penalty paid, and the believer is declared righteous as a free gift. But the gospel does not stop at the courtroom. The same grace that justifies also goes to work within, and here is the truth that rescues ethics from being a grim exercise in willpower: holiness is the fruit of the Spirit, not the achievement of the flesh. "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control" (Galatians 5:22–23). Mark the word — fruit, not works. Fruit is not manufactured by the branch gritting its teeth; it is borne as the life of the vine flows through it. Christian character is grown, by the Spirit, in a soul united to Christ.

Tiba ni injili. Ndani ya Kristo, dai la torati limetoshelezwa na adhabu yake imelipwa, na mwamini anatangazwa kuwa mwenye haki kama zawadi ya bure. Lakini injili haikomei mahakamani. Neema ile ile inayohesabia haki pia inafanya kazi ndani, na huu ndio ukweli unaoyaokoa maadili yasiwe zoezi zito la nguvu ya mapenzi: utakatifu ni tunda la Roho, si mafanikio ya mwili. "Lakini tunda la Roho ni upendo, furaha, amani, uvumilivu, utu wema, fadhili, uaminifu, upole, kiasi" (Wagalatia 5:22–23). Tazama neno hilo — tunda, si matendo. Tunda halitengenezwi na tawi linalokaza meno; huzaliwa kadiri uhai wa mzabibu unavyotiririka ndani yake. Tabia ya Kikristo hukuzwa, na Roho, ndani ya nafsi iliyounganishwa na Kristo.

This is why we held so firmly in Unit 1 to the order of grace before obedience, and why we will hold it all the way through. We do not obey in order to be accepted; we have been accepted, and therefore we obey, and the very power to obey is itself a gift. Get that order backward and you produce either a Pharisee or a wreck. Keep it straight and obedience becomes what it was always meant to be — not the anxious payment of a debt, but the glad response of a son to the Father who has already run down the road to embrace him.

Hii ndiyo sababu tulishikilia kwa uthabiti katika Sehemu ya 1 mpangilio wa neema kabla ya utii, na ndiyo sababu tutaushikilia njia yote. Hatutii ili tukubaliwe; tumekubaliwa, na kwa hiyo tunatii, na nguvu yenyewe ya kutii ni zawadi. Ukiugeuza mpangilio huo utazalisha ama Farisayo ama mtu aliyevunjika kabisa. Ukiushika sawasawa, utii unakuwa kile ambacho ulikusudiwa kuwa siku zote — si malipo ya deni yenye wasiwasi, bali jibu la furaha la mwana kwa Baba ambaye tayari amekimbia barabarani kumkumbatia.
Section 2.4 — Reading Scripture Rightly and Weighing the Ethical Systems
Kifungu 2.4 — Kusoma Maandiko kwa Usahihi na Kupima Mifumo ya Maadili

Two practical matters remain before we move into the work of ministry itself. The first is how to handle the Word so that we apply it rightly and do not twist it. We hold to what has been called the grammatical-historical method, which is a careful name for a humble practice: we ask what the human author, carried along by the Spirit, actually meant to say to his original readers, in the ordinary sense of his words and the setting of his time — and only then do we ask how that abiding truth bears on us. We do not make the text a mirror for our own preferences or a wax nose to be bent toward whatever we already wished to do. The pastor who proves his point by ripping a verse from its context has not honored the Word; he has used it. And a congregation trained by such handling will learn to do the same to one another. Read the verse in its paragraph, the paragraph in its book, and the book in the whole counsel of God.

Mambo mawili ya kivitendo yamebaki kabla hatujaingia katika kazi ya huduma yenyewe. La kwanza ni jinsi ya kulishughulikia Neno ili tulitumie kwa usahihi na tusilipotoshe. Tunashikilia kile kinachoitwa njia ya kisarufi-kihistoria, ambalo ni jina la uangalifu kwa zoezi la unyenyekevu: tunauliza mwandishi wa kibinadamu, akiongozwa na Roho, alikusudia kweli kuwaambia nini wasomaji wake wa kwanza, kwa maana ya kawaida ya maneno yake na mazingira ya wakati wake — na hapo tu ndipo tunauliza jinsi ukweli huo unaodumu unavyotuhusu sisi. Hatulifanyi andiko kuwa kioo cha matakwa yetu wenyewe wala pua ya nta ya kupindwa kuelekea chochote tulichotaka tayari kufanya. Mchungaji anayethibitisha hoja yake kwa kung'oa mstari kutoka katika muktadha wake hajaliheshimu Neno; amelitumia tu. Na kusanyiko lililofunzwa kwa ushughulikiaji wa namna hiyo litajifunza kufanya vivyo hivyo wao kwa wao. Soma mstari katika aya yake, aya katika kitabu chake, na kitabu katika shauri lote la Mungu.

The second matter is how to think about the ethical systems the world has built, which you studied in part in Unit 1. The philosophers have largely sorted themselves into three families: those who locate the good in character (the virtue traditions), those who locate it in duty and rule (the deontologists), and those who locate it in consequences (the various utilitarians). Here is the discerning Christian's verdict. Each of the three has hold of something real, and it is no accident, for each is borrowing from the moral order God actually built. Scripture cares about character — it is the whole point of the fruit of the Spirit. Scripture cares about duty — God issues commands and expects obedience. Scripture cares about consequences — love weighs the effect of its actions on a neighbor. The failure of each system is never that it sees nothing true; it is that it tears its one fragment loose from God and tries to make that fragment carry the whole weight of morality alone. The Christian does not choose one of the three and reject the others. He gathers up the truth in each — virtue, duty, and consequence — and orders all of it under the authority of God's revelation, where it finally belongs.

Jambo la pili ni jinsi ya kufikiri kuhusu mifumo ya maadili ambayo ulimwengu umeijenga, ambayo uliisoma kwa sehemu katika Sehemu ya 1. Wanafalsafa kwa kiasi kikubwa wamejipanga katika familia tatu: wale wanaoweka wema katika tabia (mapokeo ya fadhila), wale wanaouweka katika wajibu na kanuni (wanadeontolojia), na wale wanaouweka katika matokeo (wafuasi mbalimbali wa falsafa ya manufaa). Hii ndiyo hukumu ya Mkristo mwenye upambanuzi. Kila moja ya hizo tatu imeshika kitu halisi, na hilo si kwa bahati, kwa maana kila moja inakopa kutoka katika mpangilio wa kimaadili ambao Mungu aliujenga kweli. Maandiko yanajali tabia — ndilo kusudi lote la tunda la Roho. Maandiko yanajali wajibu — Mungu anatoa amri na anatarajia utii. Maandiko yanajali matokeo — upendo hupima athari ya matendo yake kwa jirani. Kushindwa kwa kila mfumo kamwe si kwamba hauoni chochote cha kweli; ni kwamba unakirarua kipande chake kimoja kutoka kwa Mungu na kujaribu kukifanya kipande hicho kibebe uzito wote wa maadili peke yake. Mkristo hachagui mmoja kati ya hiyo mitatu na kuikataa mingine. Anakusanya ukweli ulio katika kila mmoja — fadhila, wajibu, na matokeo — na kuupanga wote chini ya mamlaka ya ufunuo wa Mungu, mahali unapostahili hatimaye.
