Section 3.1 — The Call to the Ministry
Kifungu cha 3.1 — Wito wa Huduma

Before a man asks how to do the work of a pastor, he must settle a prior and more searching question: has God called him to it at all? There are two errors here, and both have wrecked churches. The first is the man who runs without being sent — ambitious, gifted perhaps, but never truly summoned, building a ministry as he would build a business. The second is the man who flees when he has plainly been sent — like Jonah, like Moses at the bush, hiding behind his unworthiness to escape a burden God has laid on him. The doctrine of calling is meant to deliver us from both: from presumption on the one hand and from disobedient cowardice on the other.

Kabla mtu hajauliza jinsi ya kufanya kazi ya mchungaji, lazima kwanza amalize swali lililo la awali na linalochunguza zaidi: je, Mungu amemwita kwa kazi hiyo kweli? Kuna makosa mawili hapa, na yote mawili yameharibu makanisa. La kwanza ni mtu anayekimbia bila kutumwa — mwenye tamaa ya makuu, labda mwenye vipawa, lakini ambaye hajawahi kuitwa kwa kweli, akijenga huduma kama ambavyo angejenga biashara. La pili ni mtu anayekimbia mbali wakati ametumwa waziwazi — kama Yona, kama Musa pale kichakani, akijificha nyuma ya kutostahili kwake ili kukwepa mzigo ambao Mungu ameuweka juu yake. Fundisho la wito limekusudiwa kutuokoa kutoka katika makosa yote mawili: kutoka katika kujiamini kupita kiasi kwa upande mmoja, na kutoka katika woga usio na utii kwa upande mwingine.

Scripture treats the desire for this work as a good thing, but never as a sufficient thing. "If a man desires the position of a bishop, he desires a good work" (1 Timothy 3:1). The desire is honorable; it is the first stirring of a true call. But desire alone ordains no one. A genuine call has two parts that must meet. There is the internal call — that holy compulsion Paul describes when he says, "woe is me if I do not preach the gospel!" (1 Corinthians 9:16). It is not mere willingness; it is a constraint, a sense that one cannot finally be at peace doing anything else. And there is the external call — the confirmation of the church, which examines a man's gifts and his character and recognizes the hand of God upon him. A man does not ordain himself. The inward fire must be confirmed by the outward judgment of God's people, or it is not yet a call but only a feeling.

Maandiko yanaitazama tamaa ya kazi hii kuwa ni jambo jema, lakini kamwe si jambo linalotosha peke yake. "Mtu akitaka kazi ya askofu, atamani kazi njema" (1 Timotheo 3:1). Tamaa hiyo ni ya heshima; ni mwamko wa kwanza wa wito wa kweli. Lakini tamaa peke yake haimweki mtu wakfu. Wito halisi una sehemu mbili ambazo lazima zikutane. Kuna wito wa ndani — ule msukumo mtakatifu ambao Paulo anaueleza anaposema, "ole wangu nisipoihubiri Injili!" (1 Wakorintho 9:16). Huo si utayari tu; ni shurutisho, ni hisia kwamba mtu hatimaye hawezi kuwa na amani akifanya jambo lingine lolote. Na kuna wito wa nje — uthibitisho wa kanisa, linalochunguza vipawa na tabia ya mtu na kutambua mkono wa Mungu juu yake. Mtu hajiweki wakfu mwenyewe. Moto wa ndani lazima uthibitishwe na hukumu ya nje ya watu wa Mungu; la sivyo bado si wito, bali ni hisia tu.

And once both have met, the man must feel the weight of what he has taken up. He is now responsible for souls for whom Christ shed His blood, and, as we saw in Unit 1, he will be judged as a teacher, by a stricter standard than the rest of the flock. This is not a career. It is a stewardship of eternal things, and it should be entered soberly, with trembling as much as with joy.

Na mara sehemu hizo mbili zikishakutana, mtu huyo lazima ahisi uzito wa kile alichokichukua. Sasa anawajibika kwa ajili ya roho ambazo Kristo alimwaga damu yake kwa ajili yao, na, kama tulivyoona katika Sehemu ya 1, atahukumiwa kama mwalimu, kwa kipimo kikali kuliko kundi lote. Hii si kazi ya kujipatia riziki tu. Ni uwakili wa mambo ya milele, na inapaswa kuingiwa kwa kiasi na umakini, kwa kutetemeka kama vile kwa furaha.
Section 3.2 — The Qualifications: Character Before Competence
Kifungu cha 3.2 — Sifa Zinazostahili: Tabia Kabla ya Ustadi

A word before we go further on how this unit uses "he" and "his" for this office, and on where CTS stands. The requirement that this leader be "the husband of one wife" (1 Timothy 3:2; Titus 1:6) sits at the center of a real disagreement among Bible-believing Christians, so this course lays out three positions rather than treat the question as settled. The complementarian view reads the qualification lists, with 1 Timothy 2:12, as reserving the senior pastoral and eldership office for qualified men, while affirming women's gifting in the church's other ministries. The egalitarian view points to texts such as Galatians 3:28, Philip's four daughters who prophesied (Acts 21:9), and Paul's own regulation of women praying and prophesying in the gathered assembly (1 Corinthians 11:5), arguing a called and qualified woman may hold any ministry office. A third, team-ministry view holds that women may serve in substantial, even titled pastoral roles, while the senior or lead pastor remains a man, so that women's leadership operates under that oversight. This unit describes the qualifications below in the text's own traditional masculine language, without that settling the question for you. Where you land is a matter for your own study, conscience, and the church body you serve.

Neno moja kabla hatujaendelea, kuhusu jinsi sehemu hii inavyotumia lugha ya kiume ("yeye mwanamume", "wake") kwa ajili ya ofisi hii, na kuhusu msimamo wa CTS. Sharti kwamba kiongozi huyu awe "mume wa mke mmoja" (1 Timotheo 3:2; Tito 1:6) liko katikati ya tofauti halisi ya maoni miongoni mwa Wakristo wanaoiamini Biblia, kwa hiyo kozi hii inaeleza misimamo mitatu badala ya kulichukulia swali hili kuwa limekwisha kuamuliwa. Mtazamo wa ukamilishano (complementarian) unasoma orodha za sifa hizi, pamoja na 1 Timotheo 2:12, kuwa zinaihifadhi ofisi ya mchungaji mkuu na ya uzee kwa wanaume wenye sifa zinazostahili, huku ukithibitisha vipawa vya wanawake katika huduma nyingine za kanisa. Mtazamo wa usawa (egalitarian) unaelekeza kwenye maandiko kama Wagalatia 3:28, binti wanne wa Filipo waliotabiri (Matendo 21:9), na maagizo ya Paulo mwenyewe kuhusu wanawake wanaoomba na kutabiri katika kusanyiko la kanisa (1 Wakorintho 11:5), ukisema kwamba mwanamke aliyeitwa na mwenye sifa zinazostahili anaweza kushika ofisi yoyote ya huduma. Mtazamo wa tatu, wa huduma ya timu (team-ministry), unashikilia kwamba wanawake wanaweza kutumika katika nafasi kubwa za kichungaji, hata zenye vyeo, huku mchungaji mkuu au kiongozi akibaki kuwa mwanamume, ili uongozi wa wanawake ufanye kazi chini ya usimamizi huo. Sehemu hii inaeleza sifa zilizo hapa chini kwa lugha ya kiume ya kimapokeo ya maandiko yenyewe, bila hilo kukuamulia swali hili. Mahali utakaposimama ni jambo la kujifunza kwako mwenyewe, la dhamiri yako, na la mwili wa kanisa unalolitumikia.

When the Spirit, through Paul, lists the qualifications for this office, the result should astonish anyone who has spent time in the world's leadership culture. Read 1 Timothy 3:1–7 and Titus 1:5–9 side by side and ask a simple question of each item: is this a skill, or is it a matter of character? You will find that nearly the entire list is character. Above reproach. The husband of one wife. Temperate, sober-minded, of good behavior. Not given to wine, not violent but gentle, not quarrelsome, not greedy for money. One who rules his own house well. Not a new convert. Of good testimony even among those outside the church.

Roho Mtakatifu, kupitia Paulo, anapoorodhesha sifa zinazostahili kwa ofisi hii, matokeo yanapaswa kumshangaza yeyote aliyewahi kukaa katika utamaduni wa uongozi wa ulimwengu huu. Soma 1 Timotheo 3:1–7 na Tito 1:5–9 sambamba, kisha uulize swali rahisi kuhusu kila kipengele: je, huu ni ujuzi, au ni jambo la tabia? Utagundua kwamba karibu orodha yote ni tabia. Asiyelaumika. Mume wa mke mmoja. Mwenye kiasi, mwenye busara, mwenye utaratibu. Si mtu wa kuzoelea mvinyo, si mpiga watu bali mpole, si mgomvi, si mwenye kupenda fedha. Mtu anayeisimamia nyumba yake mwenyewe vizuri. Asiwe mtu aliyeongoka karibuni. Mwenye ushuhuda mzuri hata kwa wale walio nje ya kanisa.

And amid that long catalog of character, how much room is given to raw competency? Very little, and what is given is not about talent or charisma but about the ministry itself: he must be able to teach, and Titus adds that he must hold firmly to sound doctrine so that he can both exhort believers and refute those who contradict it (Titus 1:9). Even household management, listed alongside the character qualities, carries a real leadership dimension — Paul reasons that a man who cannot manage his own household well has not shown he can care for God's household either (1 Timothy 3:4–5). So the list is not pure character with zero competence attached; but character overwhelmingly dominates it, and the competencies required are modest and ministry-shaped rather than the markers the world prizes. The world assembles its leaders by talent — who is the most capable, the most charismatic, the most effective. God assembles His shepherds by holiness first, with sound teaching and demonstrated, humble leadership required alongside it. This is one of the most counter-cultural truths a seminarian will ever absorb, and it must be absorbed deep, because the temptation to reverse it never lets up. A church that selects its leaders the way a corporation selects executives — for giftedness while winking at character — is sowing a harvest of grief it will reap within the decade.

Na katikati ya orodha hiyo ndefu ya tabia, ni nafasi kiasi gani inayopewa ustadi mtupu? Ni ndogo sana, na ile inayotolewa haihusu kipaji wala mvuto wa kibinafsi, bali inahusu huduma yenyewe: lazima awe mwepesi wa kufundisha, na Tito anaongeza kwamba lazima alishike kwa uthabiti fundisho lenye uzima ili aweze kuwaonya waamini na pia kuwashawishi wale wanaopinga (Tito 1:9). Hata usimamizi wa nyumba, unaoorodheshwa pamoja na sifa za tabia, una sura halisi ya uongozi — Paulo anahoji kwamba mtu asiyeweza kuisimamia nyumba yake mwenyewe vizuri hajaonyesha kwamba anaweza kuitunza nyumba ya Mungu pia (1 Timotheo 3:4–5). Kwa hiyo orodha hii si tabia tupu isiyoambatana na ustadi wowote; lakini tabia inaitawala kwa kiasi kikubwa mno, na ustadi unaotakiwa ni wa kiasi na umeundwa kwa ajili ya huduma, si zile alama ambazo ulimwengu unazithamini. Ulimwengu huwakusanya viongozi wake kwa kipaji — nani mwenye uwezo zaidi, nani mwenye mvuto zaidi, nani anayeleta matokeo zaidi. Mungu huwakusanya wachungaji wake kwa utakatifu kwanza, pamoja na mafundisho yenye uzima na uongozi wa unyenyekevu uliothibitishwa vikitakiwa sambamba nao. Hii ni mojawapo ya kweli zinazopingana zaidi na utamaduni wa ulimwengu ambazo mwanafunzi wa seminari atawahi kuzipokea, na lazima ipokewe kwa kina, kwa sababu kishawishi cha kuipindua hakikomi kamwe. Kanisa linalowachagua viongozi wake kama shirika la biashara linavyowachagua wakurugenzi wake — kwa vipawa huku likifumbia macho tabia — linapanda mavuno ya huzuni ambayo litayavuna kabla ya miaka kumi kupita.

Notice too the warning against ordaining a new convert, "lest being puffed up with pride he fall into the same condemnation as the devil" (1 Timothy 3:6). The danger named there is not incompetence; it is pride. And notice the requirement of a good reputation with outsiders. The man's character must be visible and verified not only inside the warm circle of the church but out in the cold light of the marketplace, where reputations are not flattered. God screens His shepherds by who they are when no one is applauding.

Angalia pia onyo dhidi ya kumweka wakfu mtu aliyeongoka karibuni, "asije akajivuna akaanguka katika hukumu ya Ibilisi" (1 Timotheo 3:6). Hatari inayotajwa hapo si ukosefu wa uwezo; ni kiburi. Na angalia sharti la kuwa na sifa njema kwa walio nje. Tabia ya mtu huyo lazima ionekane na ithibitishwe si ndani ya mzunguko wenye joto wa kanisa tu, bali pia nje katika mwanga baridi wa sokoni, ambako sifa za watu hazibembelezwi. Mungu huwachuja wachungaji wake kwa jinsi walivyo wakati hakuna mtu anayewapigia makofi.
Section 3.3 — Holiness, Humility, and the Spiritual Disciplines
Kifungu cha 3.3 — Utakatifu, Unyenyekevu, na Nidhamu za Kiroho

If the office is given to character, then the pastor's first and most neglected labor is the tending of his own soul. Paul's charge to Timothy puts the order beyond dispute: "Take heed to yourself and to the doctrine" (1 Timothy 4:16). To yourself first, and then to the doctrine. The man who reverses that — who pours all his care into his teaching while his own heart goes untended — is building a fine house on a rotting foundation. You cannot give your people water from a cistern you have let run dry. Every public word a pastor speaks should be drawn from a private well he is daily refilling in secret, alone with God.

Ikiwa ofisi hii imetolewa kwa ajili ya tabia, basi kazi ya kwanza ya mchungaji, na inayopuuzwa zaidi, ni kuitunza nafsi yake mwenyewe. Agizo la Paulo kwa Timotheo linaweka mpangilio usio na shaka: "Jitunze nafsi yako, na mafundisho yako" (1 Timotheo 4:16). Nafsi yako kwanza, kisha mafundisho. Mtu anayepindua mpangilio huo — anayemimina uangalifu wake wote katika mafundisho yake huku moyo wake mwenyewe ukiachwa bila kutunzwa — anajenga nyumba nzuri juu ya msingi unaooza. Huwezi kuwapa watu wako maji kutoka katika birika uliloliacha likauke. Kila neno la hadharani ambalo mchungaji analinena linapaswa kuchotwa kutoka katika kisima cha faragha anachokijaza upya kila siku kwa siri, akiwa peke yake pamoja na Mungu.

This is why the spiritual disciplines are not optional refinements for the unusually devout pastor; they are the very supply lines of the ministry. Prayer that is more than the hurried blessing before a meal. The Word read for his own soul and not merely mined for next Sunday's sermon — for a man can study the Scriptures professionally for years and starve spiritually the whole time, handling the bread of life as a baker who never eats. There must be secret communion that no congregation ever sees, a hidden life with God behind the public life of ministry. The visible man in the pulpit must be matched by an invisible man on his knees, or the visible man will eventually become a hollow performance.

Ndiyo sababu nidhamu za kiroho si nyongeza za hiari kwa ajili ya mchungaji aliye mcha Mungu kupita kawaida; ndizo njia zenyewe za kupitishia mahitaji ya huduma. Maombi yaliyo zaidi ya baraka ya haraka kabla ya chakula. Neno linalosomwa kwa ajili ya nafsi yake mwenyewe, si kuchimbwa tu kwa ajili ya mahubiri ya Jumapili ijayo — kwa maana mtu anaweza kuyasoma Maandiko kikazi kwa miaka mingi na kufa njaa kiroho muda wote huo, akishughulikia mkate wa uzima kama mwokaji asiyekula kamwe. Lazima kuwe na ushirika wa siri ambao hakuna kusanyiko linaloweza kuuona kamwe, maisha yaliyofichika pamoja na Mungu nyuma ya maisha ya hadharani ya huduma. Mtu anayeonekana mimbarini lazima alingane na mtu asiyeonekana akiwa amepiga magoti, la sivyo yule anayeonekana hatimaye atakuwa maonyesho matupu.

And over all of it must hang the guard of humility, for pride is the peculiar and besetting sin of those who handle holy things. The very platform that makes a man useful makes him a target; the higher he is lifted in the eyes of others, the deeper the pit that opens beneath his vanity. The shepherd who forgets that he is first a sheep, equally dependent on the grace he proclaims, has already begun to fall, however long it takes the fall to become visible. Keep low. The ground is safest there.

Na juu ya yote hayo lazima pawe na ulinzi wa unyenyekevu, kwa maana kiburi ndiyo dhambi maalum inayowazinga wale wanaoshughulikia mambo matakatifu. Jukwaa lile lile linalomfanya mtu kuwa wa manufaa linamfanya kuwa shabaha; kadiri anavyoinuliwa juu machoni pa wengine, ndivyo shimo linalofunguka chini ya majivuno yake linavyozidi kuwa refu. Mchungaji anayesahau kwamba yeye kwanza ni kondoo, anayeitegemea kwa kiasi kile kile neema anayoihubiri, ameshaanza kuanguka, hata ikichukua muda mrefu kiasi gani anguko hilo kuonekana. Kaa chini. Ardhi ndiyo mahali salama zaidi.

Consider how Nehemiah went about the great work of his life. When word reached him that the wall of Jerusalem was broken down and its gates burned, he did not first reach for a plan. He broke down and wept. He fasted and prayed, confessing the sin of his fathers and his own, and only then, after months of waiting on God, did he set out to build. And notice what kind of builder he was. He did not ride into the city announcing himself or rush the people into stacking bricks. He arose at night, while everyone slept, and rode quietly around the ruins — over rubble so bad that in places he had to go on foot — until he had seen the worst of it for himself and made an honest survey of the facts. Then he laid his plans. The inner work came before the outer; the honest look came before the bold call. And when the work was underway and his enemies tried every weapon to stop it — they laughed at him, they ridiculed him, they tried blackmail, they schemed to lure him away and kill him — he gave them one answer and kept building: "I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down" (Nehemiah 6:3). He does the hidden work of prayer and self-examination before the public work begins, he tells himself the truth about the ruins before he sounds the trumpet, and once he knows the work is God’s, he refuses to be argued, flattered, or frightened down off the wall.

Fikiria jinsi Nehemia alivyoifanya kazi kuu ya maisha yake. Habari zilipomfikia kwamba ukuta wa Yerusalemu umebomoka na malango yake yameteketezwa kwa moto, hakukimbilia kwanza mpango. Aliketi akalia. Alifunga na kuomba, akiungama dhambi ya baba zake na yake mwenyewe, na hapo tu, baada ya miezi kadhaa ya kumngoja Mungu, ndipo alipoanza safari ya kujenga. Na angalia alikuwa mjenzi wa aina gani. Hakuingia mjini kwa farasi akijitangaza, wala hakuwaharakisha watu kupanga matofali. Aliondoka usiku, wakati kila mtu amelala, akazunguka kimya kimya kando ya magofu — juu ya kifusi kibaya kiasi kwamba mahali pengine ilimbidi kwenda kwa miguu — mpaka alipokuwa ameona ubaya wake wote kwa macho yake mwenyewe na kufanya uchunguzi wa kweli wa hali halisi. Kisha akaweka mipango yake. Kazi ya ndani ilitangulia ile ya nje; kutazama kwa uaminifu kulitangulia mwito wa ujasiri. Na kazi ilipokuwa ikiendelea na adui zake wakajaribu kila silaha ili kuisimamisha — walimcheka, walimdhihaki, walijaribu kumtisha kwa vitisho vya kumchafua, walipanga hila za kumvuta mbali ili wamuue — aliwapa jibu moja na kuendelea kujenga: "Mimi ninafanya kazi kubwa, siwezi kushuka" (Nehemia 6:3). Anafanya kazi iliyofichika ya maombi na ya kujichunguza kabla kazi ya hadharani haijaanza, anajiambia ukweli kuhusu magofu kabla hajapiga tarumbeta, na mara anapojua kwamba kazi ni ya Mungu, anakataa kushushwa kutoka ukutani kwa mabishano, kwa kubembelezwa, au kwa kutishwa.
Section 3.4 — The Pastor as Example, and Guarding Against Disqualification
Kifungu cha 3.4 — Mchungaji kama Kielelezo, na Kujilinda Dhidi ya Kukataliwa

We return now to a truth first sounded in Unit 1, because it is the hinge of pastoral character: the pastor leads chiefly by what he is. Peter charges the elders to shepherd the flock "being examples to the flock" (1 Peter 5:3). The people will become, over time, more like what they watch their shepherd be than like what they hear him say. This is a glorious privilege and a terrifying responsibility in the same breath.

Sasa tunarudi kwenye kweli tuliyoitaja kwanza katika Sehemu ya 1, kwa sababu ndiyo bawaba ya tabia ya kichungaji: mchungaji huongoza hasa kwa jinsi alivyo. Petro anawaagiza wazee kulichunga kundi "kwa kuwa vielelezo kwa lile kundi" (1 Petro 5:3). Kwa kupita kwa wakati, watu watafanana zaidi na kile wanachomwona mchungaji wao akiwa, kuliko kile wanachomsikia akisema. Hili ni pendeleo tukufu na jukumu la kutisha kwa pumzi moja.

And because the stakes are so high, every pastor must reckon honestly with the possibility of his own ruin. Here is a truth I want pressed into you: moral catastrophe is almost never a sudden leap. It is a slow drift — a series of small, deniable compromises, each one excused, that quietly carve a channel down which the final disaster will one day rush. The unguarded glance becomes the entertained thought; the entertained thought becomes the secret habit; the secret habit becomes the public scandal that ends a ministry. No man wakes up one morning and decides to destroy his life's work. He drifts there, one unconfessed inch at a time. Even the apostle Paul refused to presume on his own standing: "I discipline my body and bring it into subjection, lest, when I have preached to others, I myself should become disqualified" (1 Corinthians 9:27). If Paul guarded himself, the man who thinks he has no need to is the man already in gravest danger.

Na kwa sababu hatari ni kubwa mno, kila mchungaji lazima akabiliane kwa uaminifu na uwezekano wa kuanguka kwake mwenyewe. Hii ni kweli ninayotaka ikuingie ndani kabisa: maafa ya kimaadili karibu kamwe si mruko wa ghafla. Ni kuteleza polepole — mfululizo wa maafikiano madogo yanayoweza kukanushwa, kila moja likisamehewa, ambayo kimya kimya huchimba mfereji ambao siku moja maafa ya mwisho yatapita kwa kasi ndani yake. Mtazamo usiolindwa unakuwa wazo linalokaribishwa; wazo linalokaribishwa linakuwa tabia ya siri; tabia ya siri inakuwa kashfa ya hadharani inayokomesha huduma. Hakuna mtu anayeamka asubuhi moja na kuamua kuiharibu kazi ya maisha yake. Huteleza mpaka huko, inchi moja isiyoungamwa baada ya nyingine. Hata mtume Paulo alikataa kujiamini kwa sababu ya hali yake mwenyewe: "bali nautesa mwili wangu, na kuutumikisha; isiwe, nikiisha kuwahubiri wengine, mwenyewe niwe mtu wa kukataliwa" (1 Wakorintho 9:27). Ikiwa Paulo alijilinda, basi mtu anayedhani hana haja ya kufanya hivyo ndiye mtu aliye tayari katika hatari kubwa kuliko zote.

What, then, are the safeguards? Honest accountability to men who are permitted to ask the hard questions and will not be flattered out of asking them. A vigilant guard over the eyes, the schedule, and the private hours, where ruin is always seeded. A refusal to minister from isolation, for the lone shepherd, cut off and accountable to no one, is the easiest of all to pick off. And the immediate confession of sin while it is still small, before it has had time to take root and grow strong in the dark. A pastor must also guard his marriage as part of guarding his ministry — a matter so weighty that we devote the next unit to it. The whole aim of this vigilance is summed up in the testimony every faithful minister longs to give at the end: "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith" (2 Timothy 4:7). The goal is not merely to begin well. It is to finish.

Basi, kinga ni zipi? Uwajibikaji wa kweli kwa wanaume wanaoruhusiwa kuuliza maswali magumu na ambao hawatabembelezwa hadi waache kuyauliza. Ulinzi wa macho, wa ratiba, na wa saa za faragha, kwa maana huko ndiko mbegu za maangamizi hupandwa kila mara. Kukataa kuhudumu ukiwa peke yako, kwa maana mchungaji aliye peke yake, aliyetengwa na asiyewajibika kwa mtu yeyote, ndiye rahisi kuliko wote kunaswa. Section 4.1 — The Home as the First Proof of Ministry
Kifungu cha 4.1 — Nyumbani kama Uthibitisho wa Kwanza wa Huduma

We ended the last unit with a promise to take up the pastor's family, and we do so now because Scripture itself places the home at the very center of a man's fitness for the office. It is easy to imagine that a pastor's home is the private backdrop to his public work — the place he retreats to after the real ministry is done. The Bible turns that picture exactly around. The home is not the backdrop to the ministry; it is the first proving ground of it.

Tulimaliza sehemu iliyopita kwa ahadi ya kuishughulikia familia ya mchungaji, na tunafanya hivyo sasa kwa sababu Maandiko yenyewe yanaiweka nyumba katikati kabisa ya kufaa kwa mtu kwa ajili ya ofisi hii. Ni rahisi kudhani kwamba nyumba ya mchungaji ni mandhari ya faragha nyuma ya kazi yake ya hadharani — mahali anapokimbilia baada ya huduma halisi kukamilika. Biblia inaipindua picha hiyo kabisa. Nyumbani si mandhari ya nyuma ya huduma; ndipo uwanja wa kwanza wa kuithibitisha.

Paul makes the logic inescapable. Among the qualifications for an overseer, he writes that a man must be "one who rules his own house well, having his children in submission with all reverence" — and then he presses the reason home with a question that has no comfortable answer: "for if a man does not know how to rule his own house, how will he take care of the church of God?" (1 Timothy 3:4–5). Read that as the argument it is. The household is the smaller trust by which God tests a man's fitness for the larger one. A man who cannot shepherd the few souls placed under his own roof, who cannot lead with love and patience the wife and children who know him best, has given no evidence that he can shepherd the many. The church is, in a real sense, simply the household of God writ large, and the qualifying test runs from the small house to the great one.

Paulo anaifanya hoja hii isiweze kukwepeka. Miongoni mwa sifa zinazostahili kwa mwangalizi, anaandika kwamba mtu lazima awe "mwenye kuisimamia nyumba yake vizuri, mwenye kuwatiisha watoto wake kwa ustahivu wote" — kisha anaisisitiza sababu kwa swali lisilo na jibu la kustarehesha: "Lakini mtu asiyejua kuisimamia nyumba yake mwenyewe, atalitunzaje kanisa la Mungu?" (1 Timotheo 3:4–5). Isome kama hoja ilivyo. Nyumba ni dhamana ndogo ambayo kwayo Mungu hupima kufaa kwa mtu kwa ajili ya dhamana kubwa zaidi. Mtu asiyeweza kuzichunga roho chache zilizowekwa chini ya paa lake mwenyewe, asiyeweza kumwongoza kwa upendo na uvumilivu mke na watoto wanaomjua kuliko wote, hajatoa ushahidi wowote kwamba anaweza kuwachunga wengi. Kanisa, kwa maana halisi, ni nyumba ya Mungu iliyopanuliwa kwa ukubwa, na kipimo cha kufaa kinatoka katika nyumba ndogo hadi ile kubwa.

This means that the order of a pastor's priorities is settled before he ever sets it himself. His walk with God comes first, as we saw in Unit 3; his family comes next; and the church, for all its weight, comes after the family it must never be allowed to consume. The home is also a witness, and not only a test. The watching world and the watching congregation read a pastor's doctrine of grace, of patience, of love, far more clearly in how he treats his wife at the end of a hard week than in his most polished sermon on the subject. What he is at home is what he actually believes. The rest is theory.

Hii inamaanisha kwamba mpangilio wa vipaumbele vya mchungaji umekwisha kuamuliwa kabla yeye mwenyewe hajauweka. Kutembea kwake na Mungu kunakuja kwanza, kama tulivyoona katika Sehemu ya 3; familia yake inafuata; na kanisa, pamoja na uzito wake wote, linakuja baada ya familia ambayo halipaswi kamwe kuruhusiwa kuimeza. Nyumbani pia ni ushuhuda, si kipimo tu. Ulimwengu unaotazama na kusanyiko linalotazama husoma fundisho la mchungaji kuhusu neema, uvumilivu, na upendo kwa uwazi zaidi sana katika jinsi anavyomtendea mke wake mwishoni mwa wiki ngumu kuliko katika mahubiri yake yaliyoandaliwa vizuri kuliko yote juu ya somo hilo. Kile alicho nyumbani ndicho anachokiamini kweli. Mengine yote ni nadharia.
Section 4.2 — The Husband’s Loving Leadership and the Father’s Charge
Kifungu cha 4.2 — Uongozi wa Upendo wa Mume na Agizo kwa Baba

Scripture assigns the husband a position of leadership in the home, and we will not apologize for teaching it, because God's Word teaches it. But everything turns on how that leadership is defined, and here the Bible's definition is so far from the world's caricature that the two can scarcely be spoken of in the same breath. The world hears "headship" and imagines domination, the strong imposing his will on the weak. Paul hears it and points to a cross. "Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself for her" (Ephesians 5:25). There is the pattern, and it is devastating to every form of petty male tyranny. The head of the home is to lead the way Christ led — by laying himself down, by serving, by spending himself for the good of the one entrusted to him, even unto death. A husband's authority is real, but it is the authority of the one who washes feet. The man who uses headship as a license for selfishness has not understood the first thing about it; he has inverted it.

Maandiko yanampa mume nafasi ya uongozi nyumbani, na hatutaomba radhi kwa kulifundisha hilo, kwa sababu Neno la Mungu linalifundisha. Lakini kila kitu kinategemea jinsi uongozi huo unavyofafanuliwa, na hapa ufafanuzi wa Biblia uko mbali mno na picha potofu ya ulimwengu kiasi kwamba haviwezi kutajwa kwa pumzi moja. Ulimwengu unaposikia "ukichwa" unawaza utawala wa kukandamiza, mwenye nguvu akilazimisha mapenzi yake juu ya aliye dhaifu. Paulo anapousikia, anaelekeza kwenye msalaba. "Enyi waume, wapendeni wake zenu, kama Kristo naye alivyolipenda Kanisa, akajitoa kwa ajili yake" (Waefeso 5:25). Hicho ndicho kielelezo, nacho kinaangamiza kila namna ya udhalimu mdogo wa kiume. Kichwa cha nyumba anapaswa kuongoza jinsi Kristo alivyoongoza — kwa kujitoa, kwa kutumikia, kwa kujitumia kwa ajili ya mema ya yule aliyekabidhiwa, hata hadi kifo. Mamlaka ya mume ni halisi, lakini ni mamlaka ya yule anayeosha miguu. Mtu anayetumia ukichwa kama kibali cha ubinafsi hajaelewa hata jambo la kwanza kuuhusu; ameupindua.

The same self-giving love reaches down to the children. "And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up in the training and admonition of the Lord" (Ephesians 6:4). Notice that the charge cuts in two directions at once. There is a positive duty — to bring them up, to train, to instruct, to point them again and again to the Lord. And there is a sharp negative warning — do not provoke them, do not exasperate them with harshness, inconsistency, or a standard you demand of them but never of yourself. A great many children raised in the manse have been driven not toward Christ but away from Him, not by the gospel their father preached but by the bitterness their father bred at home. Parenting in a pastor's house must hold these together: a discipline that is firm but never cruel, and a tenderness that is warm but never indulgent, all of it aimed at the heart and not merely the behavior.

Upendo ule ule wa kujitoa unawafikia watoto pia. "Nanyi, akina baba, msiwachokoze watoto wenu, bali waleeni katika adabu ya Bwana na maonyo yake" (Waefeso 6:4). Angalia kwamba agizo hili linakata pande mbili kwa wakati mmoja. Kuna wajibu chanya — kuwalea, kuwafundisha, kuwaelekeza, kuwaonyesha Bwana tena na tena. Na kuna onyo kali hasi — msiwachokoze, msiwakasirishe kwa ukali, kwa kutokuwa thabiti, au kwa kipimo mnachowadai wao lakini hamjidai nacho ninyi wenyewe. Watoto wengi sana waliolelewa katika nyumba za wachungaji wamesukumwa si kumwelekea Kristo bali mbali naye, si kwa Injili ambayo baba yao aliihubiri bali kwa uchungu ambao baba yao aliuzalisha nyumbani. Malezi katika nyumba ya mchungaji lazima yashike mambo haya pamoja: nidhamu iliyo thabiti lakini isiyo ya ukatili kamwe, na upole ulio na joto lakini usio wa kudekeza kamwe, yote yakiulenga moyo na si tabia ya nje tu.
Section 4.3 — Purity, Singleness, and the Question of Divorce and Remarriage
Kifungu cha 4.3 — Usafi, Useja, na Swali la Talaka na Kuoa au Kuolewa Tena

Sexual purity is required of every servant of God, the married no less than the single, and we will treat its hardest modern pressures in a later unit. Here we lay the foundation. The married man guards his purity by cherishing his own wife and by fleeing, as Joseph fled, every situation that would compromise him. The single man — and let us say plainly that singleness is no second-class calling; our Lord Himself was single, and the apostle Paul commended it as a gift — guards his purity by chastity and by the same fleeing. The standard is one heart, kept clean before God, whatever a man's marital state.

Usafi wa kijinsia unatakiwa kwa kila mtumishi wa Mungu, aliyeoa kama vile asiyeoa, na tutashughulikia shinikizo zake ngumu zaidi za kisasa katika sehemu ya baadaye. Hapa tunaweka msingi. Mtu aliyeoa hulinda usafi wake kwa kumthamini mke wake mwenyewe na kwa kukimbia, kama Yusufu alivyokimbia, kila hali ambayo ingemtia hatarini. Mtu asiyeoa — na tuseme waziwazi kwamba useja si wito wa daraja la pili; Bwana wetu mwenyewe hakuoa, na mtume Paulo aliusifu kama karama — hulinda usafi wake kwa kujizuia kikamilifu na kwa kukimbia vivyo hivyo. Kipimo ni moyo mmoja, uliotunzwa safi mbele za Mungu, vyovyote ilivyo hali ya ndoa ya mtu.

This brings us to marriage's permanence, and to one of the most pastorally difficult questions a minister will ever face. Scripture holds an exceedingly high view of the marriage covenant. It is not a contract to be dissolved when it ceases to please, but a covenant joined by God: "Therefore what God has joined together, let not man separate" (Matthew 19:6). The biblical default, the thing we must teach and model, is permanence. Within that high view, the New Testament names certain grounds on which a marriage may be biblically dissolved — our Lord's words concerning sexual immorality (Matthew 19:9), and Paul's concerning desertion by an unbelieving spouse (1 Corinthians 7:15). I will tell you honestly that faithful, conservative, Bible-believing men have differed over exactly how far these exceptions extend and whether they permit remarriage, and a wise pastor holds his convictions here firmly while granting that godly brothers land in somewhat different places. What no faithful pastor may do is either to cheapen the covenant by treating divorce as easy, or to crush the wounded by treating the divorced as though they were beyond the reach of grace. The same gospel that upholds the permanence of marriage also binds up those whose marriages have broken, and the pastor must be a faithful guardian of the first without ever becoming a hard man toward the second.

Hili linatuleta kwenye kudumu kwa ndoa, na kwenye mojawapo ya maswali magumu zaidi ya kichungaji ambayo mhudumu atawahi kukabiliana nayo. Maandiko yana mtazamo wa juu mno juu ya agano la ndoa. Si mkataba wa kuvunjwa unapoacha kupendeza, bali ni agano lililounganishwa na Mungu: "Basi aliowaunganisha Mungu, mwanadamu asiwatenganishe" (Mathayo 19:6). Msimamo wa msingi wa Biblia, jambo ambalo lazima tulifundishe na kuliishi kama kielelezo, ni kudumu. Ndani ya mtazamo huo wa juu, Agano Jipya linataja sababu fulani ambazo kwazo ndoa inaweza kuvunjwa kwa njia ya Kibiblia — maneno ya Bwana wetu kuhusu uasherati (Mathayo 19:9), na ya Paulo kuhusu kuachwa na mwenzi asiyeamini (1 Wakorintho 7:15). Nitakuambia kwa uaminifu kwamba wanaume waaminifu, wahafidhina, wanaoiamini Biblia wametofautiana kuhusu ni kwa kiasi gani hasa vighairi hivi vinaenea na kama vinaruhusu kuoa au kuolewa tena, na mchungaji mwenye hekima hushikilia imani yake hapa kwa uthabiti huku akikubali kwamba ndugu wacha Mungu hufikia mahali tofauti kwa kiasi fulani. Kile ambacho mchungaji mwaminifu hawezi kufanya ni kulidharau agano kwa kuichukulia talaka kuwa jambo jepesi, au kuwaponda waliojeruhiwa kwa kuwatendea walioachana kana kwamba wako nje ya uwezo wa neema kuwafikia. Injili ile ile inayotetea kudumu kwa ndoa pia inawafunga majeraha wale ambao ndoa zao zimevunjika, na mchungaji lazima awe mlinzi mwaminifu wa jambo la kwanza bila kuwa kamwe mtu mgumu kwa wale wa pili.
Section 4.4 — Protecting the Family from the Pressures of Ministry
Kifungu cha 4.4 — Kuilinda Familia Dhidi ya Shinikizo za Huduma

There is a peculiar set of pressures that falls on a pastor's family and on no other, and the man who does not see them coming will let them do their quiet damage unopposed. The first is the fishbowl. The pastor's wife and children live their lives under a scrutiny no one elected them to bear, watched and judged by a congregation that often expects of them a perfection it does not expect of itself. A wise pastor shields his family from that glare, refuses to make his children into sermon illustrations, and never lets the church's expectations be laid as a yoke on shoulders too small to carry them.

Kuna mfululizo maalum wa shinikizo zinazoiangukia familia ya mchungaji na si familia nyingine yoyote, na mtu asiyeziona zikija ataziacha zifanye uharibifu wao wa kimya bila kupingwa. Ya kwanza ni bakuli la samaki la kioo. Mke wa mchungaji na watoto wake wanaishi maisha yao chini ya uchunguzi ambao hakuna mtu aliyewachagua kuubeba, wakitazamwa na kuhukumiwa na kusanyiko ambalo mara nyingi linatarajia kwao ukamilifu ambao halijitarajii lenyewe. Mchungaji mwenye hekima huikinga familia yake na mwanga huo mkali, hukataa kuwafanya watoto wake kuwa mifano ya mahubiri, na kamwe haruhusu matarajio ya kanisa yawekwe kama nira juu ya mabega madogo mno kuweza kuibeba.

The second and graver pressure is subtler, and I have watched it destroy more ministers' homes than any scandal. It is the slow theft of the man from his own family by the very work he loves. The ministry is endless; there is always one more visit, one more meeting, one more soul in need, and a conscientious pastor can always find holy-sounding reasons to give the church the time and the best energies that belonged to his wife and children. The church becomes, in effect, a mistress — not of the body, but of the heart and the hours — and the family is left with a husband and father who is present in the house but absent from the home. Do not do this. Guard your days. Defend the evening, the table, the Sabbath rest, the ordinary unhurried time in which a marriage and a family are actually built. Learn to say no to good things in order to protect the best things.

Shinikizo la pili, lililo zito zaidi, ni la kujificha zaidi, nami nimeliona likiharibu nyumba nyingi za wahudumu kuliko kashfa yoyote. Ni kuibwa polepole kwa mtu kutoka kwa familia yake mwenyewe na kazi ile ile anayoipenda. Huduma haina mwisho; daima kuna ziara moja zaidi, mkutano mmoja zaidi, roho moja zaidi yenye shida, na mchungaji mwenye dhamiri anaweza kila mara kupata sababu zinazosikika kuwa takatifu za kulipa kanisa muda na nguvu zake bora zilizokuwa za mke wake na watoto wake. Kwa hakika kanisa linakuwa hawara — si wa mwili, bali wa moyo na wa saa — na familia inabaki na mume na baba aliyepo ndani ya nyumba lakini hayupo katika maisha ya nyumbani. Usifanye hivi. Linda siku zako. Itetee jioni, meza ya chakula, pumziko la Sabato, ule muda wa kawaida usio na haraka ambamo ndoa na familia hujengwa kwa kweli. Jifunze kusema hapana kwa mambo mazuri ili kuyalinda mambo bora zaidi.

For let us be perfectly clear about what is at stake. It will profit a man nothing to gain the whole church and lose his own children. The man who builds a thriving ministry on the rubble of his neglected family has not succeeded; he has committed a tragedy with a respectable face. The faithful pastor finishes his course, as we said, having kept the faith — and he keeps it first of all in the small, holy congregation that bears his own name. Tend that flock well, and you will be the better shepherd of the larger one. Neglect it, and no measure of public success will ever make up the loss.

Kwa maana tuwe wazi kabisa kuhusu kile kilicho hatarini. Haitamfaidia mtu kitu kulipata kanisa zima na kuwapoteza watoto wake mwenyewe. Mtu anayejenga huduma inayostawi juu ya magofu ya familia yake aliyoipuuza hajafanikiwa; ametenda msiba wenye sura ya kuheshimika. Mchungaji mwaminifu humaliza mwendo wake, kama tulivyosema, akiwa ameilinda imani — na huilinda kwanza kabisa katika lile kusanyiko dogo, takatifu, linalobeba jina lake mwenyewe. Lichunge kundi hilo vizuri, nawe utakuwa mchungaji bora wa lile kubwa zaidi. Lipuuze, na hakuna kiasi chochote cha mafanikio ya hadharani kitakachoweza kufidia hasara hiyo.

Section 5.1 — Confidentiality and Its Limits
Kipengele 5.1 — Usiri na Mipaka Yake

A pastor is, among other things, a keeper of confidences. People will tell him things they have told no one else on earth — old sins, present fears, the secret griefs of a marriage, the failures they would die before letting the congregation see. This trust is one of the most sacred things entrusted to the office, and it is built slowly and shattered instantly. A man known to repeat what he hears in private will soon find that no one tells him anything that matters, and a pastor whom no one trusts with the truth cannot shepherd anyone's soul. Guard the confidences of your people as you would guard your own honor, for in handling them you are handling their honor.

Mchungaji ni, miongoni mwa mambo mengine, mtunzaji wa siri. Watu watamwambia mambo ambayo hawajamwambia mtu mwingine yeyote duniani — dhambi za zamani, hofu za sasa, huzuni za siri za ndoa, makosa ambayo wangependelea kufa kuliko kuruhusu kusanyiko liyaone. Imani hii ni mojawapo ya mambo matakatifu kabisa yaliyokabidhiwa kwa cheo hiki, nayo hujengwa polepole na kuvunjika mara moja. Mtu anayejulikana kurudia anachosikia faraghani hivi karibuni atagundua kwamba hakuna anayemwambia jambo lolote la maana, na mchungaji ambaye hakuna anayemwamini na ukweli hawezi kuchunga nafsi ya mtu yeyote. Linda siri za watu wako kama ambavyo ungelinda heshima yako mwenyewe, kwa maana unaposhughulikia siri hizo unashughulikia heshima yao.

And yet — and this is the part the textbooks too often pass over — confidentiality is a stewardship, not an absolute. It serves the good of the soul and the protection of the flock; it was never meant to become a wall behind which evil hides and the vulnerable are sacrificed. There are confidences a faithful pastor must not keep, and a man who does not settle this in advance will be paralyzed in the very moment he most needs clarity. The governing principle is this: the seal of confidence yields when keeping it would leave someone in danger of serious harm.

Na bado — na hii ndiyo sehemu ambayo vitabu vya kiada mara nyingi huipita — usiri ni uwakili, si jambo lisilo na mipaka kabisa. Unatumikia mema ya nafsi na ulinzi wa kundi; haukukusudiwa kamwe kuwa ukuta ambao nyuma yake uovu hujificha na walio hatarini hutolewa kafara. Kuna siri ambazo mchungaji mwaminifu hapaswi kuzitunza, na mtu asiyelitatua jambo hili mapema atapooza katika wakati ule ule anapohitaji uwazi zaidi. Kanuni inayoongoza ni hii: muhuri wa siri hulegea pale ambapo kuutunza kungemwacha mtu katika hatari ya madhara makubwa.

Consider the plainest cases. When a person discloses that he intends to take his own life or to harm another, the pastor's duty to protect life overrides his promise of secrecy; he must act to get that person real and immediate help, not merely pray and say nothing. When a child or other vulnerable person is being abused, the pastor is not free to bury that disclosure in the name of confidentiality; the protection of the helpless and, very often, the requirements of the law oblige him to bring it into the light and to involve the authorities and protective help that God has appointed for exactly such evils. To stay silent in these cases is not discretion; it is complicity. The shepherd who shields a wolf to keep a confidence has betrayed the sheep he was set to guard. Know the reporting laws of your own land, settle your conscience before the crisis comes, and resolve that you will never let a misplaced loyalty to secrecy make you an accomplice to harm.

Fikiria mifano iliyo wazi kabisa. Mtu anapofunua kwamba anakusudia kujiua au kumdhuru mwingine, wajibu wa mchungaji wa kulinda uhai unashinda ahadi yake ya kutunza siri; ni lazima achukue hatua kumpatia mtu huyo msaada halisi na wa haraka, si kuomba tu na kunyamaza. Mtoto au mtu mwingine aliye hatarini anapodhulumiwa, mchungaji hana uhuru wa kuuzika ufunuo huo kwa jina la usiri; ulinzi wa wasio na msaada na, mara nyingi sana, matakwa ya sheria yanamlazimu kulileta jambo hilo nuruni na kuwahusisha mamlaka na msaada wa ulinzi ambao Mungu ameuweka kwa ajili ya maovu ya namna hiyo hasa. Kunyamaza katika hali hizi si busara; ni kushiriki katika uovu. Mchungaji anayemkinga mbwa-mwitu ili kutunza siri amewasaliti kondoo aliowekwa kuwalinda. Zijue sheria za kuripoti za nchi yako, itulize dhamiri yako kabla mgogoro haujaja, na uamue kwamba kamwe hutaruhusu uaminifu uliowekwa mahali pasipofaa kwa usiri ukufanye mshirika wa madhara.

Hold these two truths together, then, without letting go of either. Be a man whose mouth can be trusted with a thousand ordinary secrets — and be a man who knows the few, grave moments when love for the endangered must break the seal.

Basi, shika kweli hizi mbili kwa pamoja, bila kuachilia hata moja. Uwe mtu ambaye kinywa chake kinaweza kuaminiwa na siri elfu za kawaida — na uwe mtu anayezijua zile nyakati chache, nzito, ambapo upendo kwa walio hatarini lazima uuvunje muhuri.
Section 5.2 — Power, Proximity, and Sexual Boundaries
Kipengele 5.2 — Mamlaka, Ukaribu, na Mipaka ya Kijinsia

We must speak frankly about something the pastor is often slow to admit: he holds real power. He is trusted, respected, granted spiritual authority, and given intimate access to people at their most vulnerable — the grieving, the lonely, the broken, the spiritually hungry. That combination of power and proximity is precisely the soil in which the gravest pastoral failures grow. And here is a truth that must be stated without flinching: because of that imbalance of power, a sexual or romantic entanglement between a pastor and someone under his spiritual care is never a meeting of equals, and the language of "it was mutual" is a lie the guilty tell themselves. The shepherd who preys on a sheep he was meant to feed has not had an affair; he has committed an abuse of the trust of his office, and the greater share of the guilt is his because the greater share of the power was his.

Ni lazima tuzungumze waziwazi kuhusu jambo ambalo mchungaji mara nyingi huchelewa kulikubali: ana mamlaka halisi. Anaaminiwa, anaheshimiwa, amepewa mamlaka ya kiroho, na amepewa nafasi ya karibu sana kwa watu wakati walipo dhaifu zaidi — wenye huzuni, walio peke yao, waliovunjika, wenye njaa ya kiroho. Mchanganyiko huo wa mamlaka na ukaribu ndio hasa udongo ambamo makosa mazito zaidi ya kichungaji hukua. Na hapa kuna kweli ambayo lazima isemwe bila kusita: kwa sababu ya kutolingana huko kwa mamlaka, uhusiano wa kingono au wa kimapenzi kati ya mchungaji na mtu aliye chini ya uangalizi wake wa kiroho kamwe si makutano ya watu walio sawa, na maneno "tulikubaliana wote wawili" ni uongo ambao wenye hatia hujiambia wenyewe. Mchungaji anayemwinda kondoo aliyekusudiwa kumlisha hajafanya uasherati tu; ametenda matumizi mabaya ya imani ya cheo chake, na sehemu kubwa zaidi ya hatia ni yake kwa sababu sehemu kubwa zaidi ya mamlaka ilikuwa yake.

Because the danger is so real and so destructive, wise pastors have always built fences well back from the cliff's edge. Do not counsel a member of the opposite sex alone, behind a closed and windowed-over door, hour after private hour; meet where there is visibility, involve your wife or another mature woman, keep the door and the schedule open to scrutiny. These are not signs of a dirty mind; they are the ordinary prudence of a man who knows his own heart is deceitful and that the strongest have fallen. Transparency is the great protector. The sin that thrives in secrecy withers in the light. A pastor who lives an open life — whose comings and goings, finances, and friendships are visible to those who may rightly ask — has built around himself the very conditions in which integrity is easiest to keep.

Kwa kuwa hatari hii ni halisi na yenye uharibifu mkubwa hivyo, wachungaji wenye hekima siku zote wamejenga ua mbali kabisa na ukingo wa genge. Usimshauri mtu wa jinsia tofauti akiwa peke yake, nyuma ya mlango uliofungwa na dirisha lililozibwa, saa baada ya saa ya faragha; kutaneni mahali panapoonekana, mhusishe mke wako au mwanamke mwingine aliyekomaa, uache mlango na ratiba wazi kwa ukaguzi. Hizi si dalili za akili chafu; ni busara ya kawaida ya mtu anayejua kwamba moyo wake mwenyewe ni mdanganyifu na kwamba hata walio hodari kabisa wameanguka. Uwazi ndio mlinzi mkuu. Dhambi inayositawi gizani hunyauka nuruni. Mchungaji anayeishi maisha ya wazi — ambaye kuja na kwenda kwake, fedha zake, na urafiki wake vinaonekana kwa wale wenye haki ya kuuliza — amejijengea kuzunguka nafsi yake mazingira yale yale ambamo uadilifu ni rahisi zaidi kudumishwa.

Scripture gives us a sobering picture of what secrecy does. Remember how the conquest began: Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground, worshiped at Gilgal, and marched around Jericho until the walls came down. So far, so good. Then came Ai — a small town, an easy target, or so the scouts said. They sent up only three thousand men, and the men of Ai routed them and killed thirty-six. Joshua was staggered; he tore his clothes and fell on his face before the Lord. And then he learned the reason: the Lord had sheathed His sword because of sin. One man, Achan, had taken for himself what belonged to God and hidden it in the earth under his tent — and no one knew. But hidden sin is never as private as the sinner imagines. Like ripples on a stream, it spreads outward; the whole camp had been defeated by what one man buried in the ground. None of us sins alone. The remedy was not deeper secrecy but light: the thing had to be uncovered, named, and dealt with openly before the nation could stand again. So it is with the pastor. The sin you can confess, expose, and bring under the counsel of others loses its power; the sin you bury under the tent only waits, and spreads, and brings down more than yourself.

Maandiko yanatupa picha ya kutisha ya kile ambacho usiri hufanya. Kumbuka jinsi uteka wa nchi ulivyoanza: Israeli walivuka Yordani kwenye nchi kavu, waliabudu huko Gilgali, na wakaizunguka Yeriko hadi kuta zikaanguka. Mpaka hapo, mambo yalikuwa mazuri. Kisha ukaja Ai — mji mdogo, shabaha rahisi, au ndivyo wapelelezi walivyosema. Walipeleka watu elfu tatu tu, na watu wa Ai wakawafukuza na kuwaua thelathini na sita. Yoshua alishtuka sana; alirarua mavazi yake na kuanguka kifudifudi mbele za BWANA. Kisha akajua sababu: BWANA alikuwa ameutia upanga wake alani kwa sababu ya dhambi. Mtu mmoja, Akani, alikuwa amejichukulia kile kilichokuwa mali ya Mungu na kukificha ardhini chini ya hema yake — na hakuna aliyejua. Lakini dhambi iliyofichwa kamwe si ya faragha kama mwenye dhambi anavyodhani. Kama mawimbi katika kijito, huenea nje; kambi yote ilikuwa imeshindwa kwa sababu ya kile ambacho mtu mmoja alikizika ardhini. Hakuna hata mmoja wetu anayetenda dhambi peke yake. Dawa haikuwa usiri zaidi bali nuru: jambo hilo lilipaswa kufunuliwa, kutajwa, na kushughulikiwa waziwazi kabla taifa halijaweza kusimama tena. Ndivyo ilivyo kwa mchungaji. Dhambi unayoweza kuiungama, kuifunua, na kuileta chini ya ushauri wa wengine hupoteza nguvu zake; dhambi unayoizika chini ya hema husubiri tu, na kuenea, na kuangusha zaidi ya wewe mwenyewe.

None of this is to make the ministry cold or to treat every hurting woman as a temptation. It is to take seriously what Scripture says of the human heart and to honor the power the office places in our hands by refusing to abuse it — even by accident, even by carelessness. The man who guards these boundaries is not being suspicious; he is being faithful.

Hakuna lolote kati ya haya linalokusudiwa kuifanya huduma kuwa baridi au kumchukulia kila mwanamke anayeumia kama jaribu. Linakusudiwa kuchukua kwa uzito kile ambacho Maandiko yanasema kuhusu moyo wa mwanadamu na kuyaheshimu mamlaka ambayo cheo huweka mikononi mwetu kwa kukataa kuyatumia vibaya — hata kwa bahati mbaya, hata kwa uzembe. Mtu anayelinda mipaka hii hana shaka mbaya; yeye ni mwaminifu.
Section 5.3 — Sheep-Stealing and the Ethics of Church Growth
Kipengele 5.3 — Kuiba Kondoo na Maadili ya Ukuaji wa Kanisa

Now to a sin that wears respectable clothes and is rarely named for what it is: the deliberate poaching of another congregation's members to swell one's own. We must be careful and fair here, because not every transfer of membership is theft. People move; people are providentially relocated; people sometimes have legitimate, conscience-driven reasons to leave one fellowship for another, and a pastor may rightly receive a believer who comes to him after leaving his former church in good order. Receiving the one who genuinely comes is not poaching. The sin lies elsewhere — in the heart that recruits, that targets a neighboring flock and courts its people, that quietly fans dissatisfaction in another man's sheep in order to draw them into one's own fold and call the resulting growth a blessing of God.

Sasa tugeukie dhambi inayovaa mavazi ya heshima na ambayo mara chache hutajwa kwa jina lake halisi: kuwavuta kwa makusudi washiriki wa kusanyiko lingine ili kuongeza wingi wa lako mwenyewe. Ni lazima tuwe waangalifu na wa haki hapa, kwa sababu si kila uhamisho wa ushirika ni wizi. Watu huhama; watu huhamishwa kwa majaliwa ya Mungu; watu wakati mwingine wana sababu halali, zinazotokana na dhamiri, za kuacha ushirika mmoja na kwenda mwingine, na mchungaji anaweza kwa haki kumpokea mwamini anayemjia baada ya kuliacha kanisa lake la zamani kwa utaratibu mzuri. Kumpokea yule anayekuja kwa dhati si kuiba kondoo. Dhambi iko mahali pengine — katika moyo unaoandikisha watu kwa ushawishi (recruits), unaolilenga kundi la jirani na kuwabembeleza watu wake, unaochochea kimya kimya kutoridhika miongoni mwa kondoo wa mtu mwingine ili kuwavuta katika zizi lake mwenyewe na kuuita ukuaji unaotokana nao kuwa baraka ya Mungu.

What is wrong with it is that it treats the kingdom of God as a competition between brothers and a man's own congregation as the prize. Paul will have none of that spirit. "Let nothing be done through selfish ambition or conceit, but in lowliness of mind let each esteem others better than himself" (Philippians 2:3). And to the church he writes of "endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace" (Ephesians 4:3). The man who builds his ministry by tearing down a brother's has gained members and lost the very unity those members were called to embody. He has also, almost always, exposed the true engine of his ministry, which is not love for Christ's whole church but ambition for his own corner of it.

Kosa lake ni kwamba unauchukulia ufalme wa Mungu kama mashindano kati ya ndugu na kusanyiko la mtu mwenyewe kama zawadi ya ushindi. Paulo hakubali roho hiyo hata kidogo. "Msitende neno lo lote kwa kushindana wala kwa kujisifu bure; bali kwa unyenyekevu kila mtu na amhesabu mwenzake kuwa bora kuliko nafsi yake" (Wafilipi 2:3). Na kwa kanisa anaandika juu ya "kujitahidi kuuhifadhi umoja wa Roho katika kifungo cha amani" (Waefeso 4:3). Mtu anayejenga huduma yake kwa kubomoa huduma ya ndugu yake amepata washiriki na amepoteza umoja ule ule ambao washiriki hao waliitwa kuudhihirisha. Pia, karibu kila mara, amefunua injini halisi ya huduma yake, ambayo si upendo kwa kanisa lote la Kristo bali tamaa ya makuu kwa ajili ya kona yake mwenyewe ya kanisa hilo.

The test of the heart is simple. Do you rejoice when the faithful church across town flourishes, even when it flourishes more than yours? Or does its growth sour something in you? The kingdom is one. Your calling is to build Christ's church, not your brand within it, and a man who cannot be glad at another shepherd's increase has not yet understood whose sheep these are.

Kipimo cha moyo ni rahisi. Je, unafurahi kanisa aminifu lililo upande wa pili wa mji linapositawi, hata linapositawi kuliko lako? Au je, ukuaji wake unachachusha kitu ndani yako? Ufalme ni mmoja. Wito wako ni kulijenga kanisa la Kristo, si chapa yako ndani yake, na mtu asiyeweza kufurahia ongezeko la mchungaji mwingine bado hajaelewa kondoo hawa ni mali ya nani.
Section 5.4 — Living by a Clear Ministerial Code
Kipengele 5.4 — Kuishi kwa Kanuni Iliyo Wazi ya Maadili ya Huduma

Everything in this unit comes to rest in a single practice that has served faithful ministers for generations: living by a clear and settled code of ministerial ethics, ideally one a man has thought through and written down before the pressures arrive. The value of a written code is not that it adds rules to grace — we have labored from Unit 1 to keep that order straight — but that it forces a man to decide in the calm what he will do in the storm. The time to resolve how you will handle a confidence, a counseling boundary, or a neighboring church's member is not in the heat of the moment, when desire and self-interest cloud the judgment, but long before, in the clear light of prayer.

Kila kitu katika sehemu hii kinatulia katika desturi moja ambayo imewafaa wahudumu waaminifu kwa vizazi vingi: kuishi kwa kanuni iliyo wazi na thabiti ya maadili ya huduma, kwa kweli kanuni ambayo mtu ameitafakari na kuiandika kabla shinikizo hazijafika. Thamani ya kanuni iliyoandikwa si kwamba inaongeza sheria juu ya neema — tumejitahidi tangu Sehemu ya 1 kuuweka mpangilio huo sawa — bali kwamba inamlazimu mtu kuamua wakati wa utulivu kile atakachofanya wakati wa dhoruba. Wakati wa kuamua jinsi utakavyoshughulikia siri, mpaka katika ushauri, au mshiriki wa kanisa jirani si katika joto la wakati wenyewe, tamaa na maslahi binafsi yanapotia giza busara, bali muda mrefu kabla, katika nuru safi ya maombi.

Such a code touches the ordinary integrity of ministerial life. It means telling the truth when you give a reference for a man leaving your staff, neither flattering him into another church's pulpit nor quietly destroying him with hints. It means honoring your predecessor rather than building yourself up by running him down to a congregation glad to hear it, and serving your successor by leaving well rather than meddling from the wings once you have gone. It means keeping your word — that a minister's promise, once given, is as good as a bond — and dealing with the church's resources and your own compensation with a transparency that invites scrutiny rather than avoiding it. We will take up the theology of money and stewardship in full in Unit 9; here it is enough to say that financial integrity is simply one more application of the open and honest life this whole unit commends.

Kanuni ya namna hiyo inagusa uadilifu wa kawaida wa maisha ya huduma. Inamaanisha kusema kweli unapotoa barua ya mapendekezo kwa mtu anayeondoka katika timu yako ya watumishi, bila kumsifu kupita kiasi ili apate mimbari ya kanisa lingine wala kumwangamiza kimya kimya kwa vidokezo. Inamaanisha kumheshimu mtangulizi wako badala ya kujijenga mwenyewe kwa kumshusha mbele ya kusanyiko linalofurahi kusikia hivyo, na kumtumikia mrithi wako kwa kuondoka vizuri badala ya kuingilia kutoka pembeni baada ya kuondoka. Inamaanisha kutimiza neno lako — kwamba ahadi ya mhudumu, ikishatolewa, ni thabiti kama dhamana — na kushughulikia mali ya kanisa na malipo yako mwenyewe kwa uwazi unaokaribisha ukaguzi badala ya kuukwepa. Tutalishughulikia kikamilifu suala la theolojia ya fedha na uwakili katika Sehemu ya 9; hapa inatosha kusema kwamba uadilifu wa kifedha ni matumizi mengine tu ya maisha ya wazi na ya uaminifu ambayo sehemu hii yote inayapendekeza.

The Scriptures give us a stark picture of what it means to keep an oath that has grown costly. When the Gibeonites came to Joshua, they came in disguise — worn-out sandals, cracked wineskins, dry and crumbling bread — pretending to be travelers from a far country so that Israel would make a treaty God had forbidden with the peoples of the land. At the crucial moment Joshua and the leaders did not stop to ask counsel of the Lord, and they were deceived into swearing a covenant, ratified by an oath in the name of the Lord, the God of Israel. Three days later the trick came to light. And here is the part a minister must take to heart: even though he had been deceived, Joshua held to his word. The trickery of the Gibeonites did not nullify the contract. An oath sworn in the name of the Lord was binding, and to break it would have brought God's wrath on the nation — as it later did, generations on, when Saul disregarded that same treaty and his house suffered for it. Joshua rebuked the Gibeonites for their deceit, and he held them to a humble service, but he did not break faith. So it must be with the man of God. He does not wriggle free of a commitment because keeping it has become inconvenient, or because he can now see he agreed too quickly.

Maandiko yanatupa picha kali ya maana ya kutimiza kiapo ambacho kimekuwa ghali. Wagibeoni walipomjia Yoshua, walikuja wamejificha — viatu vilivyochakaa, viriba vya divai vilivyopasuka, mkate mkavu uliokuwa ukibomoka — wakijifanya kuwa wasafiri kutoka nchi ya mbali ili Israeli wafanye nao mapatano ambayo Mungu alikuwa amekataza kufanya na watu wa nchi ile. Katika wakati ule muhimu Yoshua na viongozi hawakusimama kutaka shauri kwa BWANA, nao wakadanganywa hata wakaapa agano, lililothibitishwa kwa kiapo katika jina la BWANA, Mungu wa Israeli. Siku tatu baadaye hila hiyo ikajulikana. Na hapa ndipo sehemu ambayo mhudumu lazima aitie moyoni: ingawa alikuwa amedanganywa, Yoshua alishika neno lake. Udanganyifu wa Wagibeoni haukulibatilisha agano hilo. Kiapo kilichoapwa katika jina la BWANA kilikuwa cha lazima kutimizwa, na kukivunja kungeleta ghadhabu ya Mungu juu ya taifa — kama ilivyotokea baadaye, vizazi vingi baadaye, Sauli alipoyadharau mapatano hayo hayo na nyumba yake ikateseka kwa sababu hiyo. Yoshua aliwakemea Wagibeoni kwa udanganyifu wao, na akawaweka katika utumishi wa unyenyekevu, lakini hakuvunja uaminifu wake. Ndivyo inavyopaswa kuwa kwa mtu wa Mungu. Hajinasui kutoka katika ahadi kwa sababu kuitimiza kumekuwa jambo lisilofaa kwake, au kwa sababu sasa anaona kwamba alikubali haraka mno.

Behind all of it stands the watching world. "Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside" (Colossians 4:5). The unbeliever who will never read your statement of faith reads your conduct closely, and a single act of pastoral dishonesty does more to discredit the gospel in his eyes than a hundred sermons can repair. Let your ethics preach. A man whose life is clean, whose word is trustworthy, and whose dealings are open has built a platform from which the gospel can be heard — and that, in the end, is what all these boundaries are for.

Nyuma ya yote haya kuna ulimwengu unaotazama. "Enendeni kwa hekima mbele yao walio nje" (Wakolosai 4:5). Asiyeamini ambaye kamwe hatasoma tamko lako la imani anasoma mwenendo wako kwa makini, na tendo moja la udanganyifu wa kichungaji hufanya mengi zaidi kuiaibisha injili machoni pake kuliko mahubiri mia moja yanavyoweza kurekebisha. Acha maadili yako yahubiri. Mtu ambaye maisha yake ni safi, ambaye neno lake laaminika, na ambaye shughuli zake ziko wazi amejenga jukwaa ambalo kutoka kwake injili inaweza kusikika — na hilo, hatimaye, ndilo kusudi la mipaka hii yote.
Confidentiality is a stewardship, not a wall. Keep a thousand ordinary secrets faithfully — and know the few grave moments when love for the endangered must break the seal.
Usiri ni uwakili, si ukuta. Tunza kwa uaminifu siri elfu za kawaida — na uzijue zile nyakati chache, nzito, ambapo upendo kwa walio hatarini lazima uuvunje muhuri.

Section 6.1 — The Ethics of the Pulpit: Faithful Exposition and Honest Speech
Kipengele 6.1 — Maadili ya Mimbari: Ufafanuzi Aminifu na Usemi wa Kweli

A pulpit is a position of enormous trust, and like every position of trust it can be abused. We have already learned, in Unit 2, how to handle the Word honestly — reading each text in its context and submitting to what the author actually meant. Here we press that into a matter of ethics, for to twist the Scriptures to say what we want them to say, to make a text serve our agenda rather than God's, is not merely poor exegesis; it is a kind of lying in God's name, and there is scarcely a graver sin a preacher can commit. The man in the pulpit speaks as though he speaks the words of God. If he bends those words to his own purposes, he has made the Almighty the endorser of his private opinions, and the people, trusting him, will never know the difference.

Mimbari ni nafasi ya dhamana kubwa sana, na kama kila nafasi ya dhamana inaweza kutumiwa vibaya. Tayari tumejifunza, katika Sehemu ya 2, jinsi ya kulishughulikia Neno kwa uaminifu — kusoma kila kifungu katika muktadha wake na kujitiisha chini ya kile ambacho mwandishi alikimaanisha hasa. Hapa tunalisukuma jambo hilo kuwa suala la maadili, kwa maana kuyapotosha Maandiko ili yaseme kile tunachotaka yaseme, kukifanya kifungu kitumikie ajenda yetu badala ya ile ya Mungu, si tafsiri mbaya tu; ni aina ya uongo katika jina la Mungu, na hakuna dhambi nyingi zilizo nzito kuliko hiyo ambazo mhubiri anaweza kutenda. Mtu aliye mimbarini husema kana kwamba anasema maneno ya Mungu. Akiyapinda maneno hayo kwa makusudi yake mwenyewe, amemfanya Mwenyezi kuwa mthibitishaji wa maoni yake binafsi, na watu, wakimwamini, hawatajua kamwe tofauti.

From this flows a whole cluster of pulpit sins to be named and shunned. There is manipulation — the working of the congregation's emotions for effect, the engineered tears, the pressure tactics that bypass the mind and the conscience to extract a response the truth itself did not produce. There is the use of the pulpit as a weapon, the preacher who, too cowardly to confront a man privately, instead aims his sermon at him from the safety of the platform where the target cannot answer. And there is plagiarism, which our age has made easy and common: the preaching of another man's labor as though it were your own. To stand and deliver a sermon you did not study, prayed over by someone else, and let your people believe it came from your own communion with God, is theft and deceit braided together. Use the labors of other men, by all means — no preacher is an island — but use them honestly, and let your preaching be the overflow of your own walk with God and your own wrestling with the text.

Kutoka hapa hutiririka kundi zima la dhambi za mimbarini ambazo zinapaswa kutajwa na kuepukwa. Kuna hila ya kuwaendesha watu kihisia (manipulation) — kuzichezea hisia za kusanyiko kwa ajili ya matokeo, machozi yaliyotengenezwa, mbinu za shinikizo zinazopita kando ya akili na dhamiri ili kulazimisha mwitikio ambao kweli yenyewe haikuuzaa. Kuna matumizi ya mimbari kama silaha, mhubiri ambaye, akiwa mwoga mno kumkabili mtu faraghani, badala yake anamlenga kwa mahubiri yake akiwa salama jukwaani ambapo mlengwa hawezi kujibu. Na kuna wizi wa kazi ya wengine (plagiarism), ambao zama zetu zimeufanya kuwa rahisi na wa kawaida: kuhubiri kazi ya mtu mwingine kana kwamba ni yako mwenyewe. Kusimama na kutoa mahubiri ambayo hukujifunza, yaliyoombewa na mtu mwingine, na kuwaacha watu wako waamini kwamba yalitoka katika ushirika wako mwenyewe na Mungu, ni wizi na udanganyifu vilivyosukwa pamoja. Tumia kazi za watu wengine, kwa vyovyote vile — hakuna mhubiri aliye kisiwa — lakini zitumie kwa uaminifu, na mahubiri yako yawe mfuriko wa mwenendo wako mwenyewe pamoja na Mungu na wa mapambano yako mwenyewe na kifungu.

Behind all of this stands a conviction I have taught for many years: you do not give a sermon, you preach from the soul. Preaching is not a performance to be admired but a man set on fire by the truth, occupying the space God has given him and speaking what he himself has first been gripped by. The pulpit is not a stage, and the preacher who learns to play it as one — preaching for the applause, the reputation, the effect — has traded a holy calling for a cheap one.

Nyuma ya haya yote kuna msimamo ambao nimeufundisha kwa miaka mingi: hutoi mahubiri, unahubiri kutoka nafsini. Kuhubiri si onyesho la kusifiwa bali ni mtu aliyewashwa moto na kweli, akiikalia nafasi ambayo Mungu amempa na kusema kile ambacho yeye mwenyewe ameshikwa nacho kwanza. Mimbari si jukwaa la maonyesho, na mhubiri anayejifunza kuicheza kama jukwaa la maonyesho — akihubiri kwa ajili ya makofi, sifa, matokeo — amebadilishana wito mtakatifu kwa wito duni.
