Section 6.2 — Servant Leadership: Authority, Submission, and Impartiality
Kipengele 6.2 — Uongozi wa Kitumishi: Mamlaka, Kujitiisha, na Kutopendelea

The pastor genuinely holds authority in the church; Scripture does not pretend otherwise, and the congregation is called to submit to its faithful leaders. But the manner in which that authority is held is everything, and here our Lord drew the sharpest possible line. "You know that those who are considered rulers over the Gentiles lord it over them... Yet it shall not be so among you" (Mark 10:42–43). Not so among you. The world's pattern of leadership — the strong commanding, the great being served — is precisely the pattern Christ forbids to His undershepherds. Peter echoes it exactly: elders are to lead "not as being lords over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock" (1 Peter 5:3). The model is the towel and the basin, the King who knelt to wash the feet of men He could have commanded.

Mchungaji kwa kweli ana mamlaka katika kanisa; Maandiko hayajifanyi kuwa sivyo, na kusanyiko linaitwa kujitiisha chini ya viongozi wake waaminifu. Lakini namna mamlaka hayo yanavyoshikwa ndiyo kila kitu, na hapa Bwana wetu alichora mstari mkali kuliko yote. "Mnajua ya kuwa wale wanaohesabiwa kuwa wakuu wa mataifa huwatawala kwa nguvu... Lakini haitakuwa hivyo kwenu" (Marko 10:42–43). Haitakuwa hivyo kwenu. Mfumo wa ulimwengu wa uongozi — wenye nguvu wakiamuru, wakubwa wakitumikiwa — ndio hasa mfumo ambao Kristo anawakataza wachungaji walio chini yake. Petro anarudia jambo hilo hilo kikamilifu: wazee wanapaswa kuongoza "wala si kama wajifanyao mabwana juu ya wale walio chini ya uangalizi wenu, bali kama mfano kwa lile kundi" (1 Petro 5:3). Kielelezo ni taulo na bakuli, Mfalme aliyepiga magoti kuwatawadha miguu watu ambao angeweza kuwaamuru.

Let me put it in a homely picture. I have a big metal yardstick in my shop. When I am working on a large project I do not reach for a retractable tape or a cloth measure; I lay that yardstick down and I know at once what size a thing is. The trouble is that my yardstick reads in feet and inches. I lived years in Canada and now in Mexico, where everything is measured in meters, but my mind is still stuck in the measure I grew up with. We all carry a measuring stick for success, and most of us inherited the world’s. We say a man has done well if he is clever, or good-looking, or a leader, or makes a great deal of money, or is known. We would not likely brag, “My son has become a wonderful servant.” But God’s ruler is a different ruler altogether. On the night before His death, with His disciples still arguing over which of them was greatest, the Lord of glory rose from supper, wrapped a towel around His waist, took a basin, and washed their feet — the task of the lowest servant in the house. Then He said, "If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet" (John 13:14). That is the measure. The world asks, “How many people work for you?” The Lord asks, “For how many people do you work?” A man called to lead in Christ’s church is called first to kneel in it.

Niliweke jambo hili katika picha ya nyumbani. Nina rula kubwa ya chuma ya yadi moja katika karakana yangu. Ninapofanya kazi ya mradi mkubwa sifikii utepe wa kupimia unaojikunja wala kipimo cha kitambaa; ninaiweka chini rula hiyo na ninajua mara moja kitu kina ukubwa gani. Shida ni kwamba rula yangu inasoma kwa futi na inchi. Niliishi miaka mingi Kanada na sasa Meksiko, ambapo kila kitu hupimwa kwa mita, lakini akili yangu bado imekwama katika kipimo nilichokulia nacho. Sote tunabeba kijiti cha kupimia mafanikio, na wengi wetu tulirithi kile cha ulimwengu. Tunasema mtu amefanikiwa ikiwa ni mwerevu, au mzuri wa sura, au kiongozi, au anapata fedha nyingi sana, au anajulikana. Si rahisi tujigambe, “Mwanangu amekuwa mtumishi wa ajabu.” Lakini rula ya Mungu ni rula tofauti kabisa. Usiku ule kabla ya kifo chake, wanafunzi wake wakiwa bado wanabishana ni nani kati yao aliye mkubwa, Bwana wa utukufu aliondoka chakulani, akajifunga taulo kiunoni, akatwaa bakuli, akawatawadha miguu — kazi ya mtumishi wa chini kabisa nyumbani. Kisha akasema, "Basi ikiwa mimi niliye Bwana na Mwalimu wenu nimewatawadha miguu, imewapasa ninyi nanyi kutawadhana miguu" (Yohana 13:14). Hicho ndicho kipimo. Ulimwengu unauliza, “Watu wangapi wanakufanyia kazi?” Bwana anauliza, “Unawafanyia kazi watu wangapi?” Mtu aliyeitwa kuongoza katika kanisa la Kristo ameitwa kwanza kupiga magoti ndani yake.

So the pastor's authority is real but inverted from the world's: it is the authority of a servant, exercised for the good of those served and never for the comfort or aggrandizement of the one who holds it. And the submission Scripture asks of the congregation is the glad following of a shepherd who plainly loves them and points them to Christ — not the cowed obedience extracted by a domineering man who has confused his own will with the will of God. A leader who must demand submission has usually already forfeited the right to it.

Kwa hiyo mamlaka ya mchungaji ni halisi lakini yamegeuzwa kinyume na yale ya ulimwengu: ni mamlaka ya mtumishi, yanayotumiwa kwa ajili ya mema ya wale wanaotumikiwa na kamwe si kwa ajili ya starehe au kujikweza kwa yule aliye nayo. Na kujitiisha ambako Maandiko yanaliomba kusanyiko ni kumfuata kwa furaha mchungaji ambaye waziwazi anawapenda na kuwaelekeza kwa Kristo — si utii wa woga unaolazimishwa na mtu mtawala kwa nguvu aliyechanganya mapenzi yake mwenyewe na mapenzi ya Mungu. Kiongozi anayelazimika kudai kutiiwa kwa kawaida tayari amepoteza haki ya kutiiwa.

One more mark belongs to godly leadership: impartiality. The church is the one place on earth where the distinctions the world lives by are to mean nothing. "My brethren, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with partiality" (James 2:1). The pastor who fawns over the wealthy donor and overlooks the poor widow, who bends the rules for his friends and applies them strictly to those he dislikes, has betrayed the gospel of a God who shows no favoritism. Justice in the church must be blind to wealth, to status, to friendship, and to the leader's own preferences. The same standard, the same patience, and the same grace must reach the influential man and the inconvenient one alike.

Alama moja zaidi ni ya uongozi wa kimungu: kutopendelea. Kanisa ni mahali pekee duniani ambapo tofauti ambazo ulimwengu huishi nazo zinapaswa kutokuwa na maana yoyote. "Ndugu zangu, imani ya Bwana wetu Yesu Kristo, Bwana wa utukufu, msiwe nayo pamoja na kupendelea watu" (Yakobo 2:1). Mchungaji anayembembeleza mtoaji tajiri na kumpuuza mjane maskini, anayezipinda kanuni kwa ajili ya marafiki zake na kuzitumia kwa ukali kwa wale asiowapenda, ameisaliti injili ya Mungu asiyependelea watu. Haki katika kanisa lazima isione utajiri, cheo, urafiki, wala mapendeleo ya kiongozi mwenyewe. Kiwango kile kile, uvumilivu ule ule, na neema ile ile lazima vimfikie mtu mwenye ushawishi na yule anayesumbua vilevile.
Section 6.3 — Biblical Church Discipline — and Its Misuse
Kipengele 6.3 — Nidhamu ya Kanisa ya Kibiblia — na Matumizi Yake Mabaya

Few subjects are more neglected, and few more easily mishandled, than the discipline of the church. Our Lord laid out the process Himself with great care. "If your brother sins against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone" (Matthew 18:15). That is the first step and the one most often skipped: a private word, between the two, aimed at winning the brother. If he will not hear, the second step is to take one or two others, that every word may be established by witnesses. If he still refuses, the matter comes before the church. And only if he will not hear even the church is he finally to be treated as one outside it. Note the patient escalation, each stage giving room for repentance, each stage widening the circle only as far as the brother's hardness requires and no farther.

Ni masomo machache yanayopuuzwa zaidi, na machache yanayoshughulikiwa vibaya kwa urahisi zaidi, kuliko nidhamu ya kanisa. Bwana wetu mwenyewe aliuweka utaratibu huo kwa uangalifu mkubwa. "Na ndugu yako akikukosa, enenda ukamwonye, wewe na yeye peke yenu" (Mathayo 18:15). Hiyo ndiyo hatua ya kwanza na ile inayorukwa mara nyingi zaidi: neno la faragha, kati ya wawili hao, likilenga kumpata ndugu. Asiposikia, hatua ya pili ni kuwachukua mmoja au wawili wengine, ili kila neno lithibitishwe kwa vinywa vya mashahidi. Akiendelea kukataa, jambo hilo linaletwa mbele ya kanisa. Na ikiwa tu hatalisikia hata kanisa, ndipo hatimaye atahesabiwa kuwa mtu aliye nje yake. Angalia ongezeko hili la hatua kwa uvumilivu, kila hatua ikitoa nafasi ya toba, kila hatua ikipanua mzunguko kadiri tu ugumu wa moyo wa ndugu unavyohitaji na si zaidi.

Alongside Matthew 18 stands the graver case of 1 Corinthians 5, where a notorious, unrepented, public sin in the church demanded decisive action for the sake of the whole body. From these passages we draw the three purposes of all discipline, and they must be held in this order: first, the restoration of the sinning brother, which is always the goal; second, the purity of the church, that a little leaven not corrupt the whole lump; and third, the honor of Christ's name before a watching world. A useful distinction governs the process: private sins are dealt with privately and need never become public if repentance comes early, while sins that are public or that harden into open defiance may require the wider steps.

Kando ya Mathayo 18 kuna kesi nzito zaidi ya 1 Wakorintho 5, ambapo dhambi mashuhuri, isiyotubiwa, ya hadharani katika kanisa ilidai hatua thabiti kwa ajili ya mwili wote. Kutoka katika vifungu hivi tunapata makusudi matatu ya nidhamu yote, nayo lazima yashikwe kwa mpangilio huu: kwanza, kurejeshwa kwa ndugu anayetenda dhambi, ambalo daima ndilo lengo; pili, usafi wa kanisa, ili chachu kidogo kisilichachue donge zima; na tatu, heshima ya jina la Kristo mbele ya ulimwengu unaotazama. Tofauti moja yenye msaada inaongoza utaratibu huu: dhambi za faragha hushughulikiwa faraghani na kamwe hazihitaji kuwa za hadharani ikiwa toba inakuja mapema, wakati dhambi zilizo za hadharani au zinazogeuka kuwa ukaidi wa wazi zinaweza kuhitaji hatua pana zaidi.

Now I must speak plainly about something the manuals too often leave unsaid, because nothing in pastoral ministry is more easily turned into a weapon than discipline. The same process our Lord gave for healing can be perverted into an instrument of control, and a great deal of spiritual abuse has been committed under its banner. Discipline is misused when a leader skips the patient private steps and escalates straight to public exposure, satisfying his anger rather than seeking the brother. It is misused when its true engine is the leader's wounded pride and not the sinner's good. It is misused when it becomes a tool for silencing those who question the leadership, or for crushing rather than restoring. Hear me on this: a discipline that has lost the goal of restoration has ceased to be biblical discipline and has become something else, something cruel. Paul fixes the spirit forever: "if a man is overtaken in any trespass, you who are spiritual restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself lest you also be tempted" (Galatians 6:1). Restore — not destroy. In gentleness — not in fury. And considering yourself — for the man who corrects another while forgetting his own capacity for the very same sin is the likeliest of all to become a tyrant in God's name. Discipline must always sharpen the leader's own self-examination at least as much as it confronts the offender.

Sasa lazima niseme waziwazi kuhusu jambo ambalo vitabu vya mwongozo mara nyingi huliacha bila kusemwa, kwa sababu hakuna kitu katika huduma ya kichungaji kinachogeuzwa kuwa silaha kwa urahisi zaidi kuliko nidhamu. Utaratibu ule ule ambao Bwana wetu aliutoa kwa ajili ya uponyaji unaweza kupotoshwa kuwa chombo cha kutawala, na unyanyasaji mwingi wa kiroho umefanywa chini ya bendera yake. Nidhamu inatumiwa vibaya kiongozi anaporuka hatua za faragha za uvumilivu na kwenda moja kwa moja kwenye kumwanika hadharani, akiridhisha hasira yake badala ya kumtafuta ndugu. Inatumiwa vibaya injini yake halisi inapokuwa kiburi kilichojeruhiwa cha kiongozi na si mema ya mwenye dhambi. Inatumiwa vibaya inapogeuka kuwa chombo cha kuwanyamazisha wale wanaouhoji uongozi, au cha kuponda badala ya kurejesha. Nisikilizeni katika hili: nidhamu iliyopoteza lengo la kurejesha imekoma kuwa nidhamu ya kibiblia na imekuwa kitu kingine, kitu cha ukatili. Paulo anaiweka roho yake milele: "mtu akighafilika katika kosa lo lote, ninyi mlio wa Roho mrejesheni upya mtu huyo kwa roho ya upole; ukijiangalia nafsi yako usije ukajaribiwa wewe mwenyewe" (Wagalatia 6:1). Rejesha — si kuangamiza. Kwa upole — si kwa ghadhabu. Na ukijiangalia nafsi yako — kwa maana mtu anayemrekebisha mwingine huku akisahau uwezo wake mwenyewe wa kutenda dhambi ile ile ndiye anayeelekea zaidi kuliko wote kuwa dhalimu katika jina la Mungu. Nidhamu lazima siku zote inoe kujichunguza kwa kiongozi mwenyewe angalau kama inavyomkabili mkosaji.
Section 6.4 — The Tongue: Gossip, Destructive Speech, and a Vital Distinction
Kipengele 6.4 — Ulimi: Umbea, Usemi wa Kuharibu, na Tofauti Muhimu

If the pulpit can be abused and authority can be abused, so above all can the simple human tongue, and Scripture treats it with a seriousness we rarely match. James calls it a fire, "a world of iniquity" set among our members (James 3:6). Solomon warns that "a whisperer separates the best of friends" (Proverbs 16:28). And Paul, listing the sins he feared to find festering in a church, names alongside the grosser vices the quieter killers: "backbitings, whisperings" (2 Corinthians 12:20). We are slow to see gossip as the church-destroyer it is, precisely because it feels so small, so natural, so easily disguised as concern or prayer request. But it is among the chief solvents of Christian unity, and a congregation given to it will be eaten hollow from within while everyone professes love.

Ikiwa mimbari inaweza kutumiwa vibaya na mamlaka yanaweza kutumiwa vibaya, zaidi ya yote ndivyo ulimi wa kawaida wa mwanadamu unavyoweza, na Maandiko yanaushughulikia kwa uzito ambao mara chache tunaufikia. Yakobo anauita moto, "ule ulimwengu wa uovu" uliowekwa kati ya viungo vyetu (Yakobo 3:6). Sulemani anaonya kwamba "mchongezi hutenganisha rafiki wapendanao" (Mithali 16:28). Na Paulo, akiorodhesha dhambi alizoogopa kuzikuta zikioza katika kanisa, anataja kando ya maovu yaliyo dhahiri zaidi wale wauaji walio kimya: "masingizio, manong'onezo" (2 Wakorintho 12:20). Tunachelewa kuuona umbea kama mharibifu wa kanisa ulivyo, hasa kwa sababu unaonekana mdogo sana, wa kawaida sana, unaojificha kwa urahisi kama kujali au ombi la maombi. Lakini ni miongoni mwa viyeyusho vikuu vya umoja wa Kikristo, na kusanyiko lililojitoa kwao litaliwa na kuwa tupu kutoka ndani huku kila mtu akidai upendo.

The pastor bears a double responsibility here. He must refuse to traffic in it himself — never repeating what he need not repeat, never being the source or the eager hearer of a tale — and he must have the courage to confront it in the flock, gently stopping the whisper at his own door and teaching his people to do the same. A man cannot lead a pure-tongued church while indulging an impure tongue in private.

Mchungaji ana wajibu maradufu hapa. Lazima akatae kuufanyia biashara yeye mwenyewe — kamwe asirudie asichohitaji kurudia, kamwe asiwe chanzo wala msikilizaji mwenye hamu wa hadithi ya umbea — na lazima awe na ujasiri wa kuukabili katika kundi, akiyazuia kwa upole manong'onezo mlangoni pake mwenyewe na kuwafundisha watu wake kufanya vivyo hivyo. Mtu hawezi kuongoza kanisa lenye ulimi safi huku akiendekeza ulimi mchafu faraghani.

And now the distinction this unit has been building toward, because it is the one most often abused in both directions. What separates sinful gossip from the legitimate confrontation of sin? Not the subject matter, for both may concern another person's fault. The difference lies in direction, motive, and goal. Gossip talks about a person to those who are neither part of the problem nor part of the solution; biblical confrontation goes to the person, through the very channels our Lord laid out in Matthew 18. Gossip aims to wound, to vent, or to elevate the teller by lowering the subject; discipline aims at the offender's restoration. To carry a brother's sin privately to him, or through the proper steps to those charged with helping, is not gossip — it is obedience. To carry that same sin sideways, into idle conversation with those who can do nothing but think less of him, is gossip however piously it is framed. Learn to tell the two apart, and teach your people to, and you will have done much to guard both the holiness and the unity of the church at once.

Na sasa tofauti ambayo sehemu hii imekuwa ikiijengea, kwa sababu ndiyo inayotumiwa vibaya mara nyingi zaidi pande zote mbili. Ni nini kinachotenganisha umbea wa dhambi na kumkabili mtu kwa halali kuhusu dhambi? Si mada yenyewe, kwa maana yote mawili yanaweza kuhusu kosa la mtu mwingine. Tofauti iko katika mwelekeo, nia, na lengo. Umbea huzungumza kuhusu mtu kwa wale ambao si sehemu ya tatizo wala si sehemu ya suluhisho; makabiliano ya kibiblia huenda kwa mtu huyo, kupitia njia zile zile ambazo Bwana wetu aliziweka katika Mathayo 18. Umbea unalenga kujeruhi, kutoa hasira, au kumpandisha msimulizi kwa kumshusha anayezungumziwa; nidhamu inalenga kurejeshwa kwa mkosaji. Kupeleka dhambi ya ndugu kwake faraghani, au kupitia hatua zinazofaa kwa wale waliokabidhiwa kusaidia, si umbea — ni utii. Kuipeleka dhambi ile ile pembeni, katika mazungumzo ya bure na wale wasioweza kufanya lolote isipokuwa kumdharau, ni umbea hata ikipambwa kwa namna ya kidini kiasi gani. Jifunze kuvitofautisha viwili hivi, uwafundishe watu wako kufanya hivyo, nawe utakuwa umefanya mengi kulinda utakatifu na umoja wa kanisa kwa wakati mmoja.

Section 7.1 — Personhood and the Image of God
Kipengele 7.1 — Utu na Sura ya Mungu

Everything in this unit rests on a single truth we planted back in Unit 2 and now must put to work: every human being bears the image of God, and therefore possesses a worth that is given, not earned, and that cannot be diminished or revoked. I called it then an irreducible worth, and the word was chosen with care. It cannot be reduced — not by age, not by size, not by usefulness, not by the failure of a body or a mind to perform. The image of God is conferred by God, and what God confers no man may strip away.

Kila kitu katika sehemu hii kinasimama juu ya kweli moja tuliyoipanda tangu Sehemu ya 2 na ambayo sasa ni lazima tuitumie kazini: kila binadamu anabeba sura ya Mungu, na kwa hiyo ana thamani aliyopewa, si aliyoipata kwa juhudi, thamani isiyoweza kupunguzwa wala kufutwa. Wakati ule niliiita thamani isiyopunguzika, na neno hilo lilichaguliwa kwa uangalifu. Haiwezi kupunguzwa — si kwa umri, si kwa ukubwa wa mwili, si kwa manufaa ya mtu, si kwa kushindwa kwa mwili au akili kufanya kazi. Sura ya Mungu inatolewa na Mungu, na kile ambacho Mungu amekitoa hakuna mwanadamu awezaye kukinyang'anya.

This is the great dividing line between the biblical view of life and the spirit of our age. The world increasingly grants personhood on a sliding scale, measuring a human being's worth by his capacities — can he think, choose, feel, contribute, want to live? On that logic the very young, the very old, the severely disabled, and the unconscious all begin to slide toward the margins, their worth made to depend on what they can do. Scripture will not have it. The worth of a man is grounded not in his abilities but in his Maker. "For You formed my inward parts; You covered me in my mother's womb... I am fearfully and wonderfully made" (Psalm 139:13–14). God says to the prophet, "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you" (Jeremiah 1:5). And when the unborn John heard the greeting of Mary, he "leaped in her womb" for joy (Luke 1:41) — a person, responding to his Lord, months before his birth.

Huu ndio mstari mkuu unaotenganisha mtazamo wa Biblia kuhusu uhai na roho ya zama zetu. Ulimwengu unazidi kutoa utu kwa kipimo kinachopanda na kushuka, ukipima thamani ya binadamu kwa uwezo wake — je, anaweza kufikiri, kuchagua, kuhisi, kuchangia, kutaka kuishi? Kwa mantiki hiyo, wachanga sana, wazee sana, wenye ulemavu mkubwa, na wasio na fahamu wote wanaanza kusukumwa pembeni, thamani yao ikifanywa kutegemea kile wanachoweza kufanya. Maandiko hayakubali jambo hilo. Thamani ya mtu imejengwa si juu ya uwezo wake bali juu ya Muumba wake. "Maana Wewe ndiwe uliyeniumba mtima wangu, Uliniunga tumboni mwa mama yangu... nimeumbwa kwa jinsi ya ajabu ya kutisha" (Zaburi 139:13–14). Mungu anamwambia nabii, "Kabla sijakuumba katika tumbo nalikujua" (Yeremia 1:5). Na Yohana ambaye bado hakuwa amezaliwa aliposikia salamu ya Mariamu, "kitoto kichanga kiliruka ndani ya tumbo lake" kwa furaha (Luka 1:41) — mtu, akimwitikia Bwana wake, miezi kadhaa kabla ya kuzaliwa kwake.

Fix this principle deeply, because the whole of bioethics flows from it. The unborn child, the newborn, the profoundly disabled man, the woman lost in dementia, the patient who will never wake — each one bears the image of God as fully as the strongest among us, and each is owed the same protection and the same reverence. Where the world sees a life not worth living, the church must see a person made in the image of God. That single conviction will steer you rightly through every question this unit raises.

Ishike kanuni hii kwa kina, kwa sababu maadili yote ya kibiolojia yanatiririka kutoka kwake. Mtoto aliye tumboni, mtoto mchanga, mwanamume mwenye ulemavu mkubwa, mwanamke aliyepotea katika upungufu wa akili wa uzeeni (dementia), mgonjwa ambaye hataamka kamwe — kila mmoja anabeba sura ya Mungu kikamilifu kama aliye na nguvu kuliko wote miongoni mwetu, na kila mmoja anastahili ulinzi ule ule na heshima ile ile. Pale ambapo ulimwengu unaona maisha yasiyostahili kuishiwa, kanisa ni lazima lione mtu aliyeumbwa kwa sura ya Mungu. Imani hiyo moja thabiti itakuongoza sawasawa katika kila swali ambalo sehemu hii inaliibua.

Section 7.2 — The Protection of Life at Its Beginning
Kipengele 7.2 — Kulinda Uhai Mwanzoni Mwake

We do not need to pinpoint the exact moment personhood begins to know we are dealing with a human life somewhere on the continuum from conception onward. The ground of the unborn child's worth is not a resolved biological timeline; it is the same imago Dei we have just established — the God who forms, knows, and covers every human being in the womb does not withhold that dignity from the earliest stages of a life He is already forming. Reasonable, Bible-believing people can hold different convictions about precisely when personhood begins. But genuine uncertainty about a boundary case is not a reason for carelessness; when the stakes of being wrong include the taking of an innocent human life, the morally serious response is to err on the side of protecting that life, not on the side of risking it. This is not a position the believer chooses for political reasons; it is the sober application of the sanctity of life, and of caution in the face of real uncertainty, to the smallest and most defenseless of all our neighbors. The God who forbids the shedding of innocent blood does not suspend that command at the edge of the womb. The unborn child is precisely the kind of vulnerable, voiceless neighbor the people of God have always been called to defend.

Hatuhitaji kubainisha wakati kamili ambapo utu unaanza ili tujue kwamba tunashughulika na uhai wa binadamu mahali fulani katika mfululizo kuanzia kutungwa kwa mimba na kuendelea. Msingi wa thamani ya mtoto aliye tumboni si ratiba ya kibiolojia iliyokwisha kuamuliwa; ni ile ile imago Dei tuliyoithibitisha hivi punde — Mungu anayemuumba, kumjua, na kumfunika kila binadamu tumboni hamnyimi heshima hiyo katika hatua za mwanzo kabisa za uhai ambao tayari anauumba. Watu wenye busara wanaoiamini Biblia wanaweza kushikilia imani tofauti kuhusu ni lini hasa utu unaanza. Lakini mashaka ya kweli kuhusu jambo lililo mpakani si sababu ya uzembe; pale ambapo hasara ya kukosea inajumuisha kuondoa uhai wa binadamu asiye na hatia, jibu lenye uzito wa kimaadili ni kuegemea upande wa kuulinda uhai huo, si upande wa kuuhatarisha. Huu si msimamo ambao mwamini anauchagua kwa sababu za kisiasa; ni matumizi ya busara ya utakatifu wa uhai, na ya tahadhari mbele ya mashaka halisi, kwa jirani zetu walio wadogo kuliko wote na wasio na kinga kuliko wote. Mungu anayekataza kumwaga damu isiyo na hatia hasitishi amri hiyo kwenye ukingo wa tumbo la mama. Mtoto aliye tumboni ndiye hasa aina ya jirani dhaifu, asiye na sauti, ambaye watu wa Mungu wameitwa siku zote kumtetea.

Honesty requires that we acknowledge the genuinely hard cases rather than pretend they do not exist. Where a pregnancy truly threatens the mother's life, conservative ethicists have long recognized a real moral difference between an act that directly intends to kill the child and a medically necessary intervention to save the mother's life that results, tragically and unintentionally, in the loss of the child. That is a far cry from abortion as a chosen end, and a wise pastor will not flatten these distinctions, nor will he abandon a family in such an anguish to face it alone. But the hard cases, real as they are, account for the smallest fraction of the question, and they must never be used as a screen behind which to justify the whole.

Uaminifu unatudai tukiri kuwepo kwa visa vigumu kweli badala ya kujifanya havipo. Pale ambapo mimba inatishia kweli uhai wa mama, wataalamu wahafidhina wa maadili kwa muda mrefu wametambua tofauti halisi ya kimaadili kati ya tendo linalokusudia moja kwa moja kumuua mtoto na hatua ya lazima ya kitabibu ya kuokoa uhai wa mama ambayo, kwa huzuni na bila kukusudiwa, inasababisha kumpoteza mtoto. Hilo liko mbali sana na utoaji mimba unaochaguliwa kama lengo lenyewe, na mchungaji mwenye hekima hatazifuta tofauti hizi, wala hataiacha familia iliyo katika uchungu kama huo ikabiliane nao peke yake. Lakini visa vigumu, ingawa ni vya kweli, ni sehemu ndogo sana ya suala zima, na kamwe visitumiwe kama pazia la kujificha nyuma yake ili kuhalalisha suala lote.

And now hear the most important pastoral word in this section, for you will minister to women and men who carry this particular grief. The pastor who proclaims the sanctity of life must in the same breath proclaim the sufficiency of grace, or he has preached only half the gospel and will crush the very people he is sent to save. There is no sin, including this one, that the blood of Christ cannot cleanse. The post-abortive woman does not need a stone thrown at a wound that is already bleeding; she needs the Savior who said to a guilty woman, "Neither do I condemn you; go and sin no more" (John 8:11) — conviction and pardon together, in that order, both of them real. Let your church be the safest place on earth for such a person to bring such a sorrow, a place of healing and not of condemnation. Truth and compassion are not rivals here; they are the two hands with which the shepherd lifts the fallen.

Na sasa sikiliza neno la kichungaji lililo muhimu kuliko yote katika kipengele hiki, kwa maana utawahudumia wanawake na wanaume wanaobeba huzuni hii mahususi. Mchungaji anayetangaza utakatifu wa uhai ni lazima, kwa pumzi ile ile, atangaze utoshelevu wa neema, la sivyo amehubiri nusu tu ya injili na atawaponda wale wale watu aliotumwa kuwaokoa. Hakuna dhambi, ikiwemo hii, ambayo damu ya Kristo haiwezi kuitakasa. Mwanamke aliyetoa mimba hahitaji jiwe kurushwa kwenye jeraha ambalo tayari linavuja damu; anamhitaji Mwokozi aliyemwambia mwanamke mwenye hatia, "Wala mimi sikuhukumu. Enenda zako; wala usitende dhambi tena" (Yohana 8:11) — kuhakikishwa dhambi na kusamehewa pamoja, kwa mpangilio huo, vyote viwili vikiwa vya kweli. Kanisa lako na liwe mahali salama kuliko pote duniani ambapo mtu kama huyo anaweza kuleta huzuni kama hiyo, mahali pa uponyaji na si pa hukumu. Kweli na huruma si washindani hapa; ni mikono miwili ambayo mchungaji huitumia kumwinua aliyeanguka.
Section 7.3 — The Protection of Life at Its End
Kipengele 7.3 — Kulinda Uhai Mwishoni Mwake

The same principle that guards the cradle guards the deathbed, but here a careful distinction must be drawn, and many sincere believers blur it to their own confusion. Life and death belong to God. "The Lord kills and makes alive" (1 Samuel 2:6). Therefore euthanasia and assisted suicide — the deliberate, intentional taking of a human life, whether another's or one's own, to end suffering — usurp an authority that belongs to God alone. To intend death as the means of relieving pain is to set oneself in the place of the Author of life, and the church must say so plainly however compassionate the motives that drive it.

Kanuni ile ile inayolinda kitanda cha mtoto mchanga inalinda pia kitanda cha mtu anayekufa, lakini hapa tofauti ya makini ni lazima iwekwe, na waamini wengi wenye moyo mnyoofu huichanganya na kujiletea mkanganyiko. Uhai na kifo ni mali ya Mungu. "BWANA huua, naye hufanya kuwa hai" (1 Samweli 2:6). Kwa hiyo eutanasia (kuua kwa huruma) na kujiua kwa kusaidiwa — kuondoa uhai wa binadamu kwa makusudi na kwa nia, iwe wa mtu mwingine au wa mtu mwenyewe, ili kumaliza mateso — vinanyakua mamlaka ambayo ni ya Mungu peke yake. Kukusudia kifo kama njia ya kuondoa maumivu ni kujiweka mahali pa Mwanzilishi wa uhai, na kanisa ni lazima liseme hivyo waziwazi hata kama nia zinazoyasukuma mambo hayo ni za huruma kiasi gani.

But — and this is the distinction so easily missed — there is a real and morally crucial difference between killing a patient and allowing a dying patient to die. To accept that a person is dying, and to cease imposing burdensome, futile treatments that only prolong the act of dying, is not euthanasia; it is the humble acceptance of mortality. The older moral tradition spoke of the difference between ordinary means of care, which we are obliged to provide, and extraordinary means — treatments that are excessively burdensome or offer no real hope of benefit — which a person may in good conscience decline. No one is obliged to demand that every machine be deployed to wring out a few more hours; to let a loved one go peacefully when the time has come is not to kill him. So too with the relief of pain: medicine given in proper measure to ease a dying person's suffering is a mercy, even in the rare case where it may, as a foreseen but unintended side effect, hasten the end — for the intent is to relieve, not to kill, and intent is the heart of the matter.

Lakini — na hii ndiyo tofauti inayopuuzwa kwa urahisi — kuna tofauti halisi na muhimu sana kimaadili kati ya kumuua mgonjwa na kumwacha mgonjwa anayekufa afe. Kukubali kwamba mtu anakufa, na kuacha kumlazimishia matibabu mazito, yasiyo na faida, ambayo yanarefusha tu tendo la kufa, si eutanasia; ni kukubali kwa unyenyekevu hali ya kufa kwa mwanadamu. Mapokeo ya zamani ya kimaadili yalizungumza juu ya tofauti kati ya njia za kawaida za huduma, ambazo tunalazimika kuzitoa, na njia za ziada (zisizo za kawaida) — matibabu yaliyo mazito kupita kiasi au yasiyotoa tumaini halisi la faida — ambayo mtu anaweza kuyakataa kwa dhamiri safi. Hakuna anayelazimika kudai kwamba kila mashine itumike ili kubana saa chache zaidi; kumwacha mpendwa aende kwa amani wakati wake umefika si kumuua. Vivyo hivyo kuhusu kupunguza maumivu: dawa inayotolewa kwa kipimo kinachofaa ili kupunguza mateso ya mtu anayekufa ni rehema, hata katika hali nadra ambapo, kama athari inayotarajiwa lakini isiyokusudiwa, inaweza kuharakisha mwisho — kwa maana nia ni kupunguza maumivu, si kuua, na nia ndiyo kiini cha jambo hili.

Around all of this the pastor stands as a minister of comfort. You will be called to the bedsides of the dying and into the agonized counsels of families weighing these very decisions, and they will need you not as a bioethicist reciting principles but as a shepherd who can pray, who can help them distinguish faithful stewardship from despair, and who can point them to the One who has conquered death. To die well, surrounded by love and committed into the hands of God, is one of the last great works of the Christian life, and you have the privilege of helping your people do it.

Katika mambo haya yote mchungaji anasimama kama mhudumu wa faraja. Utaitwa kando ya vitanda vya wanaokufa na katika mashauri ya uchungu ya familia zinazopima maamuzi haya hasa, nao watakuhitaji si kama mtaalamu wa maadili ya kibiolojia anayekariri kanuni bali kama mchungaji anayeweza kuomba, anayeweza kuwasaidia kutofautisha uwakili mwaminifu na kukata tamaa, na anayeweza kuwaelekeza kwa Yule aliyekishinda kifo. Kufa vizuri, ukizungukwa na upendo na ukikabidhiwa mikononi mwa Mungu, ni mojawapo ya kazi kuu za mwisho za maisha ya Kikristo, nawe una fursa ya kuwasaidia watu wako kufanya hivyo.
Section 7.4 — Reproductive Technology and Compassionate Counsel
Kipengele 7.4 — Teknolojia ya Uzazi na Ushauri wa Huruma

Few sorrows in a congregation run deeper or more silently than the grief of a couple who long for a child and cannot conceive. Let the pastor begin here, with tenderness, for the desire for children is a good desire, woven into us by God, and infertility is a real bereavement that the church too often leaves to mourn alone. Whatever counsel follows must be spoken to people in pain, not to a problem on a page.

Huzuni chache katika kusanyiko huenda kwa kina zaidi au kwa ukimya zaidi kuliko huzuni ya wanandoa wanaotamani mtoto na hawawezi kupata mimba. Mchungaji na aanzie hapa, kwa upole, kwa maana tamaa ya kupata watoto ni tamaa njema, iliyofumwa ndani yetu na Mungu, na ugumba ni msiba halisi ambao mara nyingi kanisa huwaacha watu waombolezee peke yao. Ushauri wowote unaofuata ni lazima uzungumzwe kwa watu walio katika maumivu, si kwa tatizo lililoandikwa kwenye karatasi.

And yet the same principle that governs the beginning and the end of life must govern its making, for the new reproductive technologies raise their questions precisely there. If every human embryo is a person bearing the image of God — and our foundation in 7.1 allows no other conclusion — then procedures that routinely create human embryos only to freeze, discard, or destroy those not used cannot be treated as morally neutral conveniences; they touch the lives of persons. This is the gravest of the concerns, and it presses on couples a weighty question about the disposition of every life so created. Other technologies raise questions of a different order — the introduction of a third party's genetic material, or of a surrogate, into what God designed as the one-flesh union of husband and wife — questions a thoughtful couple must weigh against the covenant nature of marriage we studied in Unit 4.

Hata hivyo, kanuni ile ile inayotawala mwanzo na mwisho wa uhai ni lazima itawale pia utengenezwaji wake, kwa maana teknolojia mpya za uzazi zinaibua maswali yake hapo hasa. Ikiwa kila kiinitete cha binadamu ni mtu anayebeba sura ya Mungu — na msingi wetu katika 7.1 hauruhusu hitimisho jingine — basi taratibu ambazo kwa kawaida huunda viinitete vya binadamu ili tu kuvigandisha, kuvitupa, au kuviharibu vile visivyotumika haziwezi kuchukuliwa kama urahisi usio na uzito wa kimaadili; zinagusa maisha ya watu. Hili ndilo jambo zito kuliko yote yanayotia wasiwasi, nalo linawabebesha wanandoa swali zito kuhusu hatima ya kila uhai ulioundwa kwa namna hiyo. Teknolojia nyingine zinaibua maswali ya aina tofauti — kuingiza vinasaba vya mtu wa tatu, au mama mbeba mimba, katika kile ambacho Mungu alikiunda kuwa muungano wa mwili mmoja wa mume na mke — maswali ambayo wanandoa wenye kufikiri ni lazima wayapime dhidi ya asili ya kiagano ya ndoa tuliyojifunza katika Sehemu ya 4.

Here, more than almost anywhere, the pastor must hold truth and compassion together without letting go of either, which has been the burden of this whole unit. He must not, out of sympathy for a couple's pain, wave away questions that concern the lives of image-bearers; neither may he, out of zeal for principle, become a cold man who hands the grieving a rule and walks away. He counsels gently, he counsels truthfully, he weeps with those who weep, and he helps them seek a path that honors both their longing and their God. That posture — never truth without love, never a love that abandons truth — is the whole art of pastoral bioethics, and indeed of the pastoral ministry itself.

Hapa, kuliko karibu mahali pengine popote, mchungaji ni lazima ashike kweli na huruma pamoja bila kuachilia mojawapo, jambo ambalo limekuwa mzigo wa sehemu hii yote. Hapaswi, kwa kuwahurumia wanandoa katika maumivu yao, kuyapuuza maswali yanayohusu maisha ya wabebaji wa sura ya Mungu; wala hapaswi, kwa bidii yake kwa ajili ya kanuni, kuwa mtu baridi anayemkabidhi mwenye huzuni sheria kisha kuondoka. Anashauri kwa upole, anashauri kwa kweli, analia pamoja nao waliao, na anawasaidia kutafuta njia inayoheshimu tamaa yao na Mungu wao pia. Mkao huo — kamwe kweli bila upendo, kamwe upendo unaoiacha kweli — ndio sanaa nzima ya maadili ya kibiolojia ya kichungaji, na kwa kweli ya huduma ya kichungaji yenyewe.

Section 8.1 — The Biblical Design for Sex and Marriage
Kipengele 8.1 — Mpango wa Kibiblia kwa Tendo la Ndoa na Ndoa

We must begin where Scripture begins, with a good gift and not a prohibition, because the church has too often let the world cast it as the enemy of sex when in fact the church is its truest friend. God made human beings male and female, and He made sexual union, and He pronounced His creation very good before sin ever entered. Sex is not a regrettable necessity or a shameful thing the Bible reluctantly tolerates. It is the deliberate design of a wise and generous God, who gave it to husband and wife as a gift of union, delight, and the bringing forth of life. "Marriage is honorable among all, and the bed undefiled" (Hebrews 13:4). Honorable. Undefiled. Let no preacher leave his people thinking God is embarrassed by what God Himself created.

Ni lazima tuanzie pale Maandiko yanapoanzia, kwa kipawa chema na si kwa katazo, kwa sababu mara nyingi mno kanisa limeuacha ulimwengu ulionyeshe kama adui wa tendo la ndoa, ilhali kwa kweli kanisa ndilo rafiki yake wa kweli kuliko wote. Mungu aliwaumba wanadamu mume na mke, akaumba muungano wa kimwili wa tendo la ndoa, na akatamka kwamba uumbaji wake ni mwema sana kabla dhambi haijaingia. Tendo la ndoa si jambo la lazima la kusikitisha wala jambo la aibu ambalo Biblia inalivumilia kwa kusita. Ni mpango wa makusudi wa Mungu mwenye hekima na ukarimu, aliyewapa mume na mke kama kipawa cha muungano, furaha, na kuzaa uhai. "Ndoa na iheshimiwe na watu wote, na malazi yawe safi" (Waebrania 13:4). Yenye heshima. Safi. Mhubiri yeyote asiwaache watu wake wakidhani kwamba Mungu anaona aibu kwa kile ambacho Mungu Mwenyewe aliumba.

But the goodness of the gift is inseparable from the design of the Giver, and here the world and the Word part ways. From the beginning, sexual union was ordered to one place and one place only: the covenant of marriage between a man and a woman. "Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and they shall become one flesh" (Genesis 2:24). The one-flesh union is covenantal, not casual; it is the bodily seal of a lifelong promise, not a recreation to be enjoyed wherever desire leads. This is why Scripture calls for chastity outside of marriage and fidelity within it — not because it thinks little of sex, but because it thinks so much of it. You honor a fire by keeping it in the hearth, where it warms the house; loosed from the hearth, the same fire burns the house down. The Christian sexual ethic is not the suppression of a good thing but the protection of it.

Lakini wema wa kipawa hauwezi kutenganishwa na mpango wa Mtoaji, na hapa ndipo ulimwengu na Neno vinapoachana. Tangu mwanzo, muungano wa kimwili ulipangiwa mahali pamoja na mahali pamoja tu: agano la ndoa kati ya mwanamume na mwanamke. "Kwa hiyo mwanamume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake, ataambatana na mkewe, nao watakuwa mwili mmoja" (Mwanzo 2:24). Muungano wa mwili mmoja ni wa kiagano, si wa kubahatisha; ni muhuri wa kimwili wa ahadi ya maisha yote, si burudani ya kufurahiwa popote tamaa inapoongoza. Hii ndiyo sababu Maandiko yanadai usafi wa kujizuia nje ya ndoa na uaminifu ndani yake — si kwa sababu yanalidharau tendo la ndoa, bali kwa sababu yanalithamini sana. Unauheshimu moto kwa kuuweka mekoni, ambapo unaipasha nyumba joto; ukiachiliwa kutoka mekoni, moto huo huo unaiteketeza nyumba. Maadili ya Kikristo ya kijinsia si kukandamiza jambo jema bali ni kulilinda.

This vision of the male-and-female, one-flesh covenant rests on the design we studied in Unit 4, and it is the standard against which every question in this unit will be measured. Teach it positively. A people who have seen the beauty of God's design will be far better armed against its counterfeits than a people who have only ever heard what is forbidden.

Maono haya ya agano la mwili mmoja la mume na mke yanasimama juu ya mpango tuliojifunza katika Sehemu ya 4, nayo ndiyo kipimo ambacho kila swali katika sehemu hii litapimwa kwacho. Yafundishe kwa namna chanya. Watu walioona uzuri wa mpango wa Mungu watakuwa wamejihami vizuri zaidi dhidi ya bandia zake kuliko watu ambao wamewahi kusikia tu yaliyokatazwa.
Section 8.2 — Pornography: Its Destructiveness and the Path to Freedom
Kipengele 8.2 — Ponografia: Uharibifu Wake na Njia ya Uhuru

Of all the sexual sins now besieging the church, none is more widespread or more quietly devastating than pornography, and the pastor who imagines his congregation untouched by it is dreaming. It reaches into Christian homes, into the lives of officeholders, and, let us be honest, into the studies of pastors themselves. We must speak of it plainly and without panic, as physicians speak of a disease they intend to treat.

Kati ya dhambi zote za kijinsia zinazolizingira kanisa sasa, hakuna iliyoenea zaidi wala inayoharibu kimyakimya zaidi kuliko ponografia (picha na video za ngono), na mchungaji anayedhani kusanyiko lake halijaguswa nayo anaota ndoto. Inafika ndani ya nyumba za Kikristo, katika maisha ya wenye vyeo kanisani, na, tuwe wakweli, hata katika vyumba vya kujisomea vya wachungaji wenyewe. Ni lazima tuizungumzie waziwazi na bila hofu kuu, kama madaktari wanavyozungumzia ugonjwa wanaokusudia kuutibu.

Understand first why it is so destructive. Pornography takes human beings made in the image of God and trains the heart to consume them as objects for one's own use — the very opposite of love, which gives itself for the good of another. It is, by our Lord's own definition, a form of adultery committed in the heart: "whoever looks at a woman to lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart" (Matthew 5:28). And it does not stay still. It follows the pattern of every enslaving sin, demanding more to deliver less, isolating its captive, corroding his capacity for real intimacy, and feeding always on secrecy — for as we learned in earlier units, sin grows strong in the dark and withers in the light.

Kwanza elewa kwa nini inaharibu sana. Ponografia inawachukua wanadamu walioumbwa kwa sura ya Mungu na kuufundisha moyo kuwatumia kama vitu kwa manufaa yake mwenyewe — kinyume kabisa cha upendo, ambao hujitoa kwa ajili ya mema ya mwingine. Kwa ufafanuzi wa Bwana wetu Mwenyewe, ni aina ya uzinzi unaofanywa moyoni: "kila mtu atazamaye mwanamke kwa kumtamani amekwisha kuzini naye moyoni mwake" (Mathayo 5:28). Na haibaki mahali pamoja. Inafuata mtindo wa kila dhambi inayofanya mtumwa, ikidai zaidi ili kutoa kidogo, ikimtenga mateka wake, ikiharibu uwezo wake wa ukaribu wa kweli, na ikijilisha daima kwa usiri — kwa maana kama tulivyojifunza katika sehemu zilizopita, dhambi hupata nguvu gizani na hunyauka nuruni.

Which points directly to the path of freedom, and there is a real path; no one need despair. The first step is confession that drags the thing into the light: "Confess your trespasses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed" (James 5:16). The secret sin thrives in darkness and isolation; once spoken aloud to a trusted brother, its power to control through shame and secrecy is broken, even though the underlying struggle itself is not instantly resolved. Then comes honest accountability — not a one-time confession but an ongoing openness to men permitted to ask the hard questions. And undergirding it all must be the gospel, for here above all a man must remember the lesson of Unit 2: holiness is the fruit of the Spirit, not the achievement of gritted teeth. Willpower alone has never broken an enslaving sin and never will; what breaks it is the grace of God working in a soul that has stopped fighting alone. The pastor's task is to address this sin in his flock without ever winking at it as harmless or crushing the struggler as hopeless — to call men to repentance and to walk patiently beside them in it, knowing that freedom in Christ is real and that many who now stand free once thought they never could.

Jambo hilo linaelekeza moja kwa moja kwenye njia ya uhuru, na njia halisi ipo; hakuna anayehitaji kukata tamaa. Hatua ya kwanza ni kuungama kunakolivuta jambo hilo nuruni: "Ungameni dhambi zenu ninyi kwa ninyi, na kuombeana ninyi kwa ninyi, mpate kuponywa" (Yakobo 5:16). Dhambi ya siri hustawi gizani na katika upweke; inapotamkwa kwa sauti mbele ya ndugu anayeaminika, nguvu yake ya kutawala kupitia aibu na usiri inavunjika, ingawa mapambano yenyewe yaliyo chini yake hayamaliziki papo hapo. Kisha unakuja uwajibikaji wa kweli — si kuungama mara moja tu bali uwazi unaoendelea mbele ya wanaume walioruhusiwa kuuliza maswali magumu. Na chini ya hayo yote ni lazima iwepo injili, kwa maana hapa kuliko pote mtu ni lazima akumbuke somo la Sehemu ya 2: utakatifu ni tunda la Roho, si mafanikio ya kukaza meno. Nguvu ya mapenzi peke yake haijawahi kuvunja dhambi inayofanya mtumwa wala haitaweza; kinachoivunja ni neema ya Mungu ikifanya kazi ndani ya nafsi iliyoacha kupigana peke yake. Kazi ya mchungaji ni kushughulikia dhambi hii katika kundi lake bila kamwe kuifumbia macho kana kwamba haina madhara wala kumponda anayepambana kana kwamba hana tumaini — kuwaita watu watubu na kutembea nao kwa subira katika toba hiyo, akijua kwamba uhuru ndani ya Kristo ni halisi na kwamba wengi ambao sasa wamesimama huru waliwahi kudhani hawangeweza kamwe.
Section 8.3 — Pastoral Wisdom in Contested Cultural Questions
Kipengele 8.3 — Hekima ya Kichungaji katika Maswali ya Kitamaduni Yanayobishaniwa

Some of the questions raised in this unit have become denominational and cultural flashpoints. This course does not require students to adopt a CTS position on those disputed questions. Pastors should study the relevant biblical texts carefully, understand how faithful Christians and their church traditions interpret them, and teach within their ministry setting with theological integrity, humility, and pastoral care.

Baadhi ya maswali yanayoibuliwa katika sehemu hii yamekuwa vyanzo vya mivutano ya kimadhehebu na ya kitamaduni. Kozi hii haiwalazimishi wanafunzi kukubali msimamo wa CTS kuhusu maswali hayo yanayobishaniwa. Wachungaji wanapaswa kujifunza kwa makini maandiko ya Biblia yanayohusika, kuelewa jinsi Wakristo waaminifu na mapokeo ya makanisa yao wanavyoyafasiri, na kufundisha katika mazingira ya huduma yao kwa uadilifu wa kiteolojia, unyenyekevu, na huduma ya kichungaji.

Whatever conclusion a pastor or church reaches, every person must be treated as one who bears the image of God. Controversy never gives Christians permission for contempt, cruelty, caricature, or careless speech. Pastoral ministry deals with people rather than abstractions, and difficult questions should therefore be approached with patience, careful listening, truthfulness, and compassion.

Hitimisho lolote ambalo mchungaji au kanisa litafikia, kila mtu ni lazima atendewe kama mtu anayebeba sura ya Mungu. Mabishano kamwe hayawapi Wakristo ruhusa ya dharau, ukatili, kubeza kwa kupotosha, au maneno ya ovyo. Huduma ya kichungaji inashughulika na watu badala ya mawazo dhahania, na kwa hiyo maswali magumu yanapaswa kushughulikiwa kwa subira, kusikiliza kwa makini, ukweli, na huruma.

A pastor must guard against treating any single sin as though it sat in a class by itself, more disqualifying than the sins a congregation tolerates comfortably in itself. The very word Scripture most often uses for sin, hamartia, means simply to miss the mark — and Scripture's own lists of sin are strikingly plural, never built around one offense alone. Our Lord Himself gave such a list: "For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lewdness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness. All these evil things come from within and defile a man" (Mark 7:21-23, NKJV). Thirteen things named in one breath, with no ranking among them — pride and foolishness standing beside murder and adultery. A pastor who has read that list carefully will be slow to build his preaching, or his congregation's sense of shame, around any single item drawn out and elevated above the rest.

Mchungaji ni lazima ajihadhari asichukulie dhambi yoyote moja kana kwamba imekaa katika kundi lake peke yake, inayomwondolea mtu sifa kuliko dhambi ambazo kusanyiko linazivumilia kwa raha ndani yake lenyewe. Neno ambalo Maandiko hulitumia mara nyingi zaidi kwa dhambi, hamartia, linamaanisha tu kukosa shabaha — na orodha za dhambi katika Maandiko zenyewe ni za wingi kwa namna ya kushangaza, kamwe hazijajengwa kuzunguka kosa moja peke yake. Bwana wetu Mwenyewe alitoa orodha kama hiyo: "Kwa maana ndani, kutoka mioyoni mwa watu, hutoka mawazo mabaya, uasherati, wivi, uuaji, uzinzi, tamaa mbaya, ukorofi, hila, ufisadi, kijicho, matukano, kiburi, upumbavu; haya yote mabaya hutoka ndani, nayo humtia mtu unajisi" (Marko 7:21-23, SUV). Mambo kumi na matatu yametajwa kwa pumzi moja, bila kupangwa kwa daraja — kiburi na upumbavu vikisimama kando ya uuaji na uzinzi. Mchungaji aliyeisoma orodha hiyo kwa makini atakuwa mzito kujenga mahubiri yake, au hisia ya aibu ya kusanyiko lake, kuzunguka kipengele kimoja kilichotolewa na kuinuliwa juu ya vingine.

History offers a case in point, and Scripture is not silent on it. God's own verdict on divorce is plain: "For the LORD God of Israel says That He hates divorce, for it covers one's garment with violence," says the LORD of hosts (Malachi 2:16, NKJV). And Christ Himself named the sin directly: "whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery" (Matthew 19:9, NKJV). This is not a minor matter softened by time; it is a sin God says He hates, and one Christ calls by its full name. Yet a generation or two ago, many congregations treated divorce as very nearly the unpardonable sin, and a divorced believer often carried a weight of shame the rest of the church never had to carry for its own besetting faults. Today, with a large share of any congregation having experienced divorce and remarriage, that same sin — real, named, and taken seriously by God Himself — is rarely singled out that way at all, and divorced and remarried believers sit in the pew forgiven, restored, and serving alongside everyone else. If a sin God hates and Christ names adultery can be received into the ordinary, forgiven life of the church without being held over anyone forever, no pastor has grounds to treat some other struggle as though it stood outside that same grace.

Historia inatoa mfano wa jambo hili, na Maandiko hayanyamazi juu yake. Hukumu ya Mungu Mwenyewe kuhusu talaka iko wazi: "Kwa maana mimi nakuchukia kuachana, asema BWANA, Mungu wa Israeli, naye aifunikaye nguo yake kwa udhalimu, asema BWANA wa majeshi" (Malaki 2:16, SUV). Na Kristo Mwenyewe aliitaja dhambi hiyo moja kwa moja: "Kila mtu atakayemwacha mkewe, isipokuwa ni kwa sababu ya uasherati, akaoa mke mwingine, azini" (Mathayo 19:9, SUV). Hili si jambo dogo lililolainishwa na wakati; ni dhambi ambayo Mungu anasema anaichukia, na ambayo Kristo anaiita kwa jina lake kamili. Hata hivyo, kizazi kimoja au viwili vilivyopita, makusanyiko mengi yaliichukulia talaka kuwa karibu dhambi isiyosameheka, na mwamini aliyetalikiana mara nyingi alibeba mzigo wa aibu ambao kanisa lote halikuwahi kuubeba kwa ajili ya makosa yake ya kawaida yanayolizonga. Leo, kwa kuwa sehemu kubwa ya kusanyiko lolote imepitia talaka na kuoa au kuolewa tena, dhambi hiyo hiyo — halisi, iliyotajwa, na inayochukuliwa kwa uzito na Mungu Mwenyewe — ni nadra kutengwa kwa namna hiyo hata kidogo, na waamini waliotalikiana na kuoa au kuolewa tena huketi kanisani wakiwa wamesamehewa, wamerejeshwa, na wakihudumu pamoja na wengine wote. Ikiwa dhambi ambayo Mungu anaichukia na ambayo Kristo anaiita uzinzi inaweza kupokelewa katika maisha ya kawaida ya kanisa yaliyosamehewa bila kushikiliwa juu ya mtu milele, hakuna mchungaji mwenye msingi wa kuchukulia pambano lingine kana kwamba liko nje ya neema hiyo hiyo.

Scripture also distinguishes, as it does with every temptation, between an attraction and an act. To be tempted is not the same as to sin; every believer, whatever the particular shape of his own temptations, wages the same war against desires he did not choose and does not fully control (James 1:14-15). Whatever chastity or repentance a pastor calls a congregant to, he is calling him to nothing stranger or harder than what he asks of every believer in the church — the same call to hold every desire under Christ that every saint, whatever his own struggle, is asked to carry.

Maandiko pia yanatofautisha, kama yanavyofanya kwa kila jaribu, kati ya mvuto na tendo. Kujaribiwa si sawa na kutenda dhambi; kila mwamini, vyovyote vile umbo la majaribu yake mwenyewe, anapigana vita ile ile dhidi ya tamaa ambazo hakuzichagua na ambazo hazitawali kikamilifu (Yakobo 1:14-15). Usafi wowote wa kujizuia au toba yoyote ambayo mchungaji anamwita mshiriki, hamwiti kwenye jambo lolote geni zaidi au gumu zaidi kuliko analowaomba waamini wote kanisani — wito ule ule wa kuweka kila tamaa chini ya Kristo ambao kila mtakatifu, vyovyote vile pambano lake mwenyewe, anaombwa kuubeba.

No person's past, and no person's present struggle, places him beyond grace. The gospel that changed the church's comfortable sins can change any sin, and a pastor who has watched an entire congregation's attitude toward one sin soften over a generation should be slow to declare any other sin the permanent exception.

Hakuna historia ya mtu, wala pambano la sasa la mtu, linalomweka nje ya neema. Injili iliyobadilisha dhambi za kanisa zilizozoeleka inaweza kubadilisha dhambi yoyote, na mchungaji ambaye ameona mtazamo wa kusanyiko zima kuhusu dhambi moja ukilainika katika kipindi cha kizazi kimoja anapaswa kuwa mzito kutangaza dhambi nyingine yoyote kuwa tofauti ya kudumu.

CTS distinguishes between doctrines central to the gospel and secondary or disputed questions on which evangelical churches may draw their boundaries differently. Students should learn to explain their own convictions from Scripture without pretending that every Christian who interprets a difficult passage differently has abandoned biblical authority. The church is called to hold the truth it believes with the posture of a hospital, not a battlefield — treating every person who walks through its doors, whatever he is carrying, as someone Christ died to heal, not an enemy to be defeated. The goal here is not to settle a denominational controversy for the student, but to form pastors who can handle controversial questions biblically, accurately, and graciously.

CTS inatofautisha kati ya mafundisho yaliyo kiini cha injili na maswali ya daraja la pili au yanayobishaniwa ambayo makanisa ya Kiinjilisti yanaweza kuweka mipaka yao kwa njia tofauti. Wanafunzi wanapaswa kujifunza kueleza imani zao wenyewe kutoka katika Maandiko bila kujifanya kwamba kila Mkristo anayefasiri kifungu kigumu kwa njia tofauti ameacha mamlaka ya Biblia. Kanisa limeitwa kuishika kweli linaloiamini kwa mkao wa hospitali, si wa uwanja wa vita — likimtendea kila mtu anayeingia milangoni mwake, vyovyote vile anachobeba, kama mtu ambaye Kristo alimfia ili amponye, si adui wa kushindwa. Lengo hapa si kumwamulia mwanafunzi mabishano ya kimadhehebu, bali kuwaunda wachungaji wanaoweza kushughulikia maswali yenye mabishano kwa namna ya kibiblia, kwa usahihi, na kwa neema.
Section 8.4 — Truth-Telling with Compassion in the Local Church
Kipengele 8.4 — Kusema Kweli kwa Huruma katika Kanisa la Mahali

All of this comes to rest, finally, not in a position paper but in a pastoral practice carried out in the local church, for that is where sexual discipleship actually happens or fails to happen. And make no mistake: every person in your congregation is being discipled in his sexuality by something. If the church is silent, the culture will not be; it catechizes relentlessly, through every screen and song, and a people left untaught by their pastor will simply be taught by the world instead. Silence is not neutrality. The pastor who will not speak of these things has not avoided forming his people's sexual ethic; he has merely surrendered the forming of it to other hands.

Hayo yote hatimaye yanatua, si katika waraka wa msimamo, bali katika utendaji wa kichungaji unaofanyika katika kanisa la mahali, kwa maana huko ndiko ufuasi wa kijinsia unapotokea kwa kweli au unaposhindwa kutokea. Wala usidanganyike: kila mtu katika kusanyiko lako anafundishwa ufuasi katika jinsia yake na kitu fulani. Kanisa likinyamaza, utamaduni hautanyamaza; unafundisha kama katekisimu bila kuchoka, kupitia kila skrini na kila wimbo, na watu wasiofundishwa na mchungaji wao watafundishwa tu na ulimwengu badala yake. Kunyamaza si kutokuwa upande wowote. Mchungaji asiyetaka kuzungumzia mambo haya hajaepuka kuunda maadili ya kijinsia ya watu wake; amekabidhi tu kazi ya kuyaunda mikononi mwa wengine.

So teach — and teach positively, not only prohibitively. A congregation that hears only the list of forbidden things will conclude that Christianity is against sex, and will be defenseless when the world offers what looks like a more generous vision. But a congregation that has been shown the beauty and meaning of God's design — sex as covenant, the body as the Lord's, marriage as a picture of Christ and the church, singleness as an honorable and fruitful calling — has been given something worth living for, and the prohibitions then make sense as the fence around a garden rather than the bars of a cage.

Kwa hiyo fundisha — na fundisha kwa namna chanya, si kwa makatazo tu. Kusanyiko linalosikia tu orodha ya mambo yaliyokatazwa litahitimisha kwamba Ukristo unapinga tendo la ndoa, na litakosa kinga ulimwengu utakapotoa kile kinachoonekana kuwa maono ya ukarimu zaidi. Lakini kusanyiko lililoonyeshwa uzuri na maana ya mpango wa Mungu — tendo la ndoa kama agano, mwili kama mali ya Bwana, ndoa kama picha ya Kristo na kanisa, useja kama wito wenye heshima na wenye kuzaa matunda — limepewa kitu kinachostahili kuishi kwa ajili yake, na makatazo kisha yanaeleweka kama uzio unaozunguka bustani badala ya nondo za kizimba.

Through all of it, hold the posture this course has pressed again and again: never truth without love, and never a love that abandons truth. The two are not in tension; they meet perfectly in Christ, who was full of grace and truth, and who neither lowered the standard for the woman caught in sin nor crushed her beneath it. Let your church be a community where strugglers of every kind — and that is all of us — find at once the clear call to holiness and the abundant means of grace and honest friendship to pursue it. No one who walks through your doors is beyond the reach of the gospel, and there is no sexual sin the blood of Christ cannot cleanse and no sexual brokenness His grace cannot, in time, redeem. Preach that, and live as though you believe it, and you will be the kind of shepherd these wounded and confused generations most desperately need.

Katika hayo yote, shika mkao ambao kozi hii imeusisitiza tena na tena: kamwe kweli bila upendo, na kamwe upendo unaoiacha kweli. Hivyo viwili havipingani; vinakutana kikamilifu ndani ya Kristo, aliyejaa neema na kweli, ambaye hakushusha kiwango kwa ajili ya mwanamke aliyekamatwa katika dhambi wala hakumponda chini yake. Kanisa lako na liwe jumuiya ambamo wanaopambana wa kila aina — na hao ni sisi sote — wanapata kwa wakati mmoja wito ulio wazi wa utakatifu na njia tele za neema na urafiki wa kweli wa kuufuatilia. Hakuna anayeingia milangoni mwako aliye nje ya kufikiwa na injili, na hakuna dhambi ya kijinsia ambayo damu ya Kristo haiwezi kuitakasa wala uvunjikaji wa kijinsia ambao neema yake haiwezi, kwa wakati wake, kuukomboa. Hubiri hilo, na uishi kana kwamba unaliamini, nawe utakuwa mchungaji wa aina ambayo vizazi hivi vilivyojeruhiwa na kuchanganyikiwa vinamhitaji kwa dharura kuliko wote.

Section 9.1 — Money: A Good Servant and a Cruel Master
Kipengele 9.1 — Fedha: Mtumishi Mwema na Bwana Katili

Money is one of the great test cases of the heart, which is why our Lord spoke of it more than He spoke of heaven or hell. He knew that what a man does with his money tells the truth about what he worships, however carefully his lips may say otherwise. So let us begin with a distinction that will steer this whole unit: money is a good servant and a cruel master, and everything depends on which one it is allowed to become.

Fedha ni mojawapo ya vipimo vikuu vya moyo, na ndiyo sababu Bwana wetu alizungumza juu yake zaidi kuliko alivyozungumza juu ya mbinguni au jehanamu. Alijua kwamba kile mtu anachofanya na fedha yake kinasema ukweli juu ya kile anachokiabudu, hata kama midomo yake inasema kinyume kwa uangalifu kiasi gani. Basi na tuanze kwa tofauti moja itakayoongoza sehemu hii yote: fedha ni mtumishi mwema na bwana katili, na kila kitu kinategemea ni kipi kati ya hivyo viwili inaruhusiwa kuwa.

Scripture nowhere says that money is evil. It says something far more searching: "For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, for which some have strayed from the faith in their greediness, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows" (1 Timothy 6:10). Mark the words carefully, for the verse is constantly misquoted. It is not money that is the root, but the love of it; not the thing in the hand, but the grip of the thing on the heart. A poor man can love money as idolatrously as a rich one. The question is never how much a man has, but whom he serves — and on this our Lord allowed no middle ground. "No one can serve two masters... You cannot serve God and mammon" (Matthew 6:24). Not should not. Cannot. Money makes a fine servant, sent out to feed families, support the work of the gospel, and relieve the poor; but the moment it climbs into the throne of the heart it becomes a god, and a jealous one, that will drive a man and never satisfy him.

Maandiko hayasemi popote kwamba fedha ni ovu. Yanasema jambo linalochunguza moyo zaidi sana: "Kwa maana shina moja la mabaya ya kila namna ni kupenda fedha; ambayo wengine hali wakiitamani hiyo wamefarakana na imani, na kujichoma kwa maumivu mengi" (1 Timotheo 6:10). Yaangalie maneno haya kwa makini, kwa maana mstari huu hunukuliwa vibaya kila mara. Si fedha iliyo shina, bali kuipenda; si kitu kilicho mkononi, bali jinsi kitu hicho kinavyoushika moyo. Mtu maskini anaweza kuipenda fedha kwa ibada ya sanamu sawasawa na tajiri. Swali kamwe si mtu ana kiasi gani, bali anamtumikia nani — na katika jambo hili Bwana wetu hakuruhusu njia ya kati. "Hakuna mtu awezaye kutumikia mabwana wawili... Hamwezi kumtumikia Mungu na mali" (Mathayo 6:24). Si hampaswi. Hamwezi. Fedha ni mtumishi mzuri, anayetumwa kulisha familia, kuitegemeza kazi ya Injili, na kuwasaidia maskini; lakini mara inapopanda kwenye kiti cha enzi cha moyo inakuwa mungu, tena mungu mwenye wivu, atakayemsukuma mtu bila kumtosheleza kamwe.

Against that mastery Scripture sets the great weapon of contentment. "Now godliness with contentment is great gain... And having food and clothing, with these we shall be content" (1 Timothy 6:6–8). The contented man has broken money's power over him, for there is nothing it can promise that he is desperate to buy. This frees him to work honestly, to handle debt with sober care rather than presumption, to save with prudence and give with joy — to use money rather than be used by it. Teach your people contentment and you will have armed them against ten thousand financial follies. Leave them discontented, forever reaching for the next thing, and no amount of income will ever be enough.

Dhidi ya utawala huo Maandiko yanaweka silaha kuu ya kuridhika. "Lakini utauwa pamoja na kuridhika ni faida kubwa... Basi tukiwa na chakula na mavazi, vitutoshe" (1 Timotheo 6:6–8). Mtu aliyeridhika ameuvunja uwezo wa fedha juu yake, kwa maana hakuna kitu inachoweza kuahidi ambacho anatamani sana kukinunua. Jambo hili linamwacha huru kufanya kazi kwa uaminifu, kushughulikia madeni kwa uangalifu wa busara badala ya kujiamini kupita kiasi, kuweka akiba kwa hekima na kutoa kwa furaha — kuitumia fedha badala ya kutumiwa nayo. Wafundishe watu wako kuridhika, nawe utakuwa umewapa silaha dhidi ya upumbavu elfu kumi wa mambo ya fedha. Waache wasiridhike, wakinyoosha mikono daima kwa kitu kinachofuata, na hakuna kipato chochote kitakachotosha kamwe.
Section 9.2 — The Prosperity Gospel: A Lie Refuted by Its Own Lord
Kipengele 9.2 — Injili ya Mafanikio: Uongo Uliokanushwa na Bwana Wake Mwenyewe

We must now confront directly one of the most damaging distortions of our age, the so-called prosperity gospel — the teaching that God wills every faithful believer to be materially rich and physically well, and that poverty or sickness is the mark of weak faith. I will not be gentle with it, because it is not a harmless error; it preys on the desperate, enriches the preacher at the expense of the poor, and slanders the character of God. And the simplest refutation of it is the life of the One it claims to preach.

Sasa ni lazima tukabiliane moja kwa moja na mojawapo ya upotoshaji unaoleta madhara makubwa zaidi katika zama zetu, ile iitwayo injili ya mafanikio — fundisho kwamba Mungu anataka kila mwamini mwaminifu awe tajiri wa mali na mzima wa mwili, na kwamba umaskini au ugonjwa ni alama ya imani dhaifu. Sitakuwa mpole nalo, kwa sababu si kosa lisilo na madhara; linawawinda watu walio katika dhiki, linamtajirisha mhubiri kwa gharama ya maskini, na linakashifu tabia ya Mungu. Na njia rahisi kabisa ya kulikanusha ni maisha ya Yule linalodai kumhubiri.

Consider Jesus of Nazareth. He owned no house: "Foxes have holes and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head" (Matthew 8:20). The whole of His earthly life was marked by material humility. He was laid at birth in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn (Luke 2:7). He rode into Jerusalem that final week on a borrowed colt that His disciples had to go and fetch. He ate the Last Supper in a borrowed upper room. He was buried in a borrowed tomb. And the one possession He had, the seamless robe upon His back, was stripped from Him and gambled away by soldiers as He died (John 19:23–24). If material wealth were the sure sign of the Father's favor, then the Son of God, the only perfectly faithful man who ever lived, was the most poorly rewarded of all. The prosperity gospel cannot survive ten minutes in the company of its own Lord.

Mfikirie Yesu wa Nazareti. Hakuwa na nyumba: "Mbweha wana pango, na ndege wa angani wana viota; bali Mwana wa Adamu hana pa kujilaza kichwa" (Mathayo 8:20). Maisha yake yote ya duniani yalikuwa na alama ya unyenyekevu wa kimali. Alipozaliwa alilazwa horini, kwa sababu hawakupata nafasi katika nyumba ya wageni (Luka 2:7). Aliingia Yerusalemu juma lile la mwisho akiwa amepanda mwana-punda wa kuazima ambaye wanafunzi wake walilazimika kwenda kumleta. Alikula Karamu ya Mwisho katika chumba cha juu cha kuazima. Alizikwa katika kaburi la kuazima. Na mali pekee aliyokuwa nayo, lile kanzu lisilo na mshono mgongoni mwake, alinyang'anywa, nao askari wakalipigia kura alipokuwa akifa (Yohana 19:23–24). Kama utajiri wa mali ungekuwa alama hakika ya kibali cha Baba, basi Mwana wa Mungu, mtu pekee aliyewahi kuishi akiwa mwaminifu kikamilifu, ndiye angekuwa amepewa thawabu ndogo kuliko wote. Injili ya mafanikio haiwezi kusimama hata dakika kumi mbele ya Bwana wake mwenyewe.

And it is contradicted not only by His life but by His very first words from the mountain. "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 5:3); and in Luke's account, barer still, "Blessed are you poor, for yours is the kingdom of God" — with a matching woe the prosperity preacher never quotes: "woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation" (Luke 6:20, 24). Hear how completely that overturns the lie. The prosperity teacher pronounces blessing on the rich and suspicion on the poor; Jesus pronounces blessing on the poor and woe on the comfortable. He warned that it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom — easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle (Matthew 19:23–24). A message that promises God will make you wealthy is offering a blessing Christ never gave and ignoring a warning He plainly did. Do not preach it, and protect your people from those who do.

Tena inapingwa si kwa maisha yake tu bali hata kwa maneno yake ya kwanza kabisa pale mlimani. "Heri walio maskini wa roho; maana ufalme wa mbinguni ni wao" (Mathayo 5:3); na katika habari ya Luka, kwa maneno yaliyo wazi zaidi, "Heri ninyi mlio maskini; kwa kuwa ufalme wa Mungu ni wenu" — pamoja na ole inayolingana nayo ambayo mhubiri wa mafanikio hainukuu kamwe: "ole wenu ninyi mlio matajiri; kwa kuwa mmekwisha kupata faraja yenu" (Luka 6:20, 24). Sikia jinsi hilo linavyoupindua uongo huo kabisa. Mwalimu wa mafanikio anatamka baraka juu ya matajiri na mashaka juu ya maskini; Yesu anatamka baraka juu ya maskini na ole juu ya wanaostarehe. Alionya kwamba ni vigumu kwa tajiri kuingia katika ufalme — ni rahisi ngamia kupenya katika tundu la sindano (Mathayo 19:23–24). Ujumbe unaoahidi kwamba Mungu atakufanya tajiri unatoa baraka ambayo Kristo hakuwahi kuitoa, na kupuuza onyo ambalo alilitoa waziwazi. Usiuhubiri, na uwalinde watu wako na wale wanaouhubiri.
Section 9.3 — The Grace of Giving
Kipengele 9.3 — Neema ya Kutoa

If money is to be a servant, the noblest errand we can send it on is generosity, and the New Testament treats Christian giving not as a grim duty but as a grace — one more fruit of the Spirit at work in a freed heart. Its pattern and its power is the gospel itself: "For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, that you through His poverty might become rich" (2 Corinthians 8:9). There is the whole theology of giving in one verse. We give because we have first received from a Giver who gave away His very riches, His glory, His life, to make beggars like us rich. Christian generosity is simply the overflow of a heart that has grasped that grace; it gives because it has been given to.

Ikiwa fedha ni ya kuwa mtumishi, basi kazi tukufu kuliko zote tunayoweza kuituma kufanya ni ukarimu, na Agano Jipya linauchukulia utoaji wa Kikristo si kama wajibu mzito wenye huzuni bali kama neema — tunda moja zaidi la Roho akitenda kazi katika moyo uliowekwa huru. Kielelezo chake na nguvu yake ni Injili yenyewe: "Maana mmejua neema ya Bwana wetu Yesu Kristo, kwamba, ingawa alikuwa tajiri, alikuwa maskini kwa ajili yenu, ili ninyi kwa umaskini wake mpate kuwa matajiri" (2 Wakorintho 8:9). Hapo ndipo ilipo teolojia nzima ya kutoa katika mstari mmoja. Tunatoa kwa sababu kwanza tumepokea kutoka kwa Mtoaji aliyetoa utajiri wake wenyewe, utukufu wake, uhai wake, ili kuwafanya waombaji kama sisi kuwa matajiri. Ukarimu wa Kikristo ni kufurika tu kwa moyo ulioielewa neema hiyo; unatoa kwa sababu umepewa.

From this Paul draws two principles every pastor must teach and guard. The first concerns the spirit of giving: "So let each one give as he purposes in his heart, not grudgingly or of necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver" (2 Corinthians 9:7). Giving is to be free, glad, and from the heart — and this rules out, sharply, the manipulative fundraising that has so often disgraced the church. There is no warrant anywhere in Scripture for pressure campaigns, guilt-driven appeals, or the emotional extortion of money from God's people, least of all from the poor. The pastor who works his congregation's feelings to open their wallets has corrupted a grace into a racket. Let the giving be cheerful, or do not seek it at all. The second principle is the promise that attends such giving: "God is able to make all grace abound toward you, that you, always having all sufficiency in all things, may have an abundance for every good work" (2 Corinthians 9:8). Note well what God promises the generous — not personal luxury, but sufficiency and the means for every good work. He resupplies the cheerful giver so the giver can keep on giving, not so he can hoard.

Kutokana na hili Paulo anatoa kanuni mbili ambazo kila mchungaji anapaswa kuzifundisha na kuzilinda. Ya kwanza inahusu roho ya kutoa: "Kila mtu na atoe kama alivyokusudia moyoni mwake, si kwa huzuni, wala si kwa lazima; maana Mungu humpenda yeye atoaye kwa moyo wa ukunjufu" (2 Wakorintho 9:7). Kutoa kunapaswa kuwa kwa hiari, kwa furaha, na kutoka moyoni — na jambo hili linakataza kabisa uchangishaji wa fedha wa hila ambao mara nyingi umeliaibisha kanisa. Hakuna kibali popote katika Maandiko kwa kampeni za shinikizo, maombi ya michango yanayoendeshwa kwa kuwatia watu hatia, au unyang'anyi wa kihisia wa fedha kutoka kwa watu wa Mungu, na hasa kutoka kwa maskini. Mchungaji anayechezea hisia za kusanyiko lake ili wafungue pochi zao ameigeuza neema kuwa ulaghai. Kutoa na kuwe kwa moyo wa ukunjufu, la sivyo usikutafute kabisa. Kanuni ya pili ni ahadi inayoambatana na utoaji wa namna hiyo: "Na Mungu aweza kuwajaza kila neema kwa wingi, ili ninyi, mkiwa na riziki za kila namna siku zote, mpate kuzidi sana katika kila kazi njema" (2 Wakorintho 9:8). Angalia vizuri kile ambacho Mungu anawaahidi wakarimu — si anasa ya binafsi, bali utoshelevu na njia za kufanya kila kazi njema. Anamjaza tena mtoaji mkunjufu ili mtoaji aendelee kutoa, si ili ajilimbikizie.

The tithe and the regular, disciplined support of the local church flow naturally from this. A congregation taught to give cheerfully will fund the work of God without ever being badgered, and the church's own finances must then be handled with the same transparency we required of the pastor in Unit 5 — open books, honest accounting, and not a whiff of the love of money about those who handle the Lord's.

Zaka na utegemezaji wa kawaida, wenye nidhamu, wa kanisa la mahali hapo hutokana na jambo hili kwa kawaida. Kusanyiko lililofundishwa kutoa kwa moyo wa ukunjufu litaigharimia kazi ya Mungu bila kusumbuliwa kamwe, na fedha za kanisa lenyewe zinapaswa kushughulikiwa kwa uwazi uleule tuliomtaka mchungaji awe nao katika Sehemu ya 5 — vitabu vya hesabu vilivyo wazi, uhasibu wa kweli, na hata dalili ndogo ya kupenda fedha isionekane kwa wale wanaoshughulikia fedha za Bwana.
