Section 9.4 — Caring for the Poor — and the Pastor’s Own Table
Kipengele 9.4 — Kuwajali Maskini — na Meza ya Mchungaji Mwenyewe

The God of Scripture is, from beginning to end, the defender of the poor, and a church that does not care for the needy has not understood the God it claims to worship. This is not an optional add-on to the gospel; it is the gospel showing its hands and feet. James will not let us spiritualize it away: "If a brother or sister is naked and destitute of daily food, and one of you says to them, 'Depart in peace, be warmed and filled,' but you do not give them the things which are needed for the body, what does it profit?" (James 2:15–16). Faith that feeds the hungry only with kind words is, he says bluntly, dead. And our Lord pressed it further than we are comfortable with, identifying Himself with the needy so closely that what we do for them we do to Him: "Inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me" (Matthew 25:40). The hungry man at the door is, in a mystery, Christ at the door.

Mungu wa Maandiko ni, tangu mwanzo hadi mwisho, mtetezi wa maskini, na kanisa lisilowajali wahitaji halijamwelewa Mungu linalodai kumwabudu. Hili si nyongeza ya hiari kwa Injili; ni Injili ikionyesha mikono na miguu yake. Yakobo hataturuhusu kulifanya kuwa la kiroho tu na kulikwepa: "Ikiwa ndugu mume au ndugu mke hana nguo, akapungukiwa na riziki ya kila siku, na mmoja wenu akawaambia, Enendeni zenu kwa amani, mkaote moto na kushiba; lakini asiwape vile vitu vinavyohitajiwa na mwili, yafaa nini?" (Yakobo 2:15–16). Imani inayowalisha wenye njaa kwa maneno mazuri tu, anasema waziwazi, imekufa. Na Bwana wetu alilisukuma jambo hili mbali zaidi kuliko tunavyostarehe nalo, akijitambulisha na wahitaji kwa ukaribu mno kiasi kwamba tunachowatendea wao tunamtendea Yeye: "Kadiri mlivyomtendea mmojawapo wa hao ndugu zangu walio wadogo, mlinitendea mimi" (Mathayo 25:40). Mtu mwenye njaa aliye mlangoni ni, kwa siri ya ajabu, Kristo aliye mlangoni.

The prophets thundered this same truth long before. Amos heard God say something startling about the worship of His own people: "I hate, I despise your feast days... Take away from Me the noise of your songs" (Amos 5:21–23). How could God reject the very offerings He had commanded? Because the people bringing them were trampling the poor — bribing judges, cheating with dishonest scales, selling the needy for the price of a pair of sandals — and no offering covers for that. I learned the principle long before I could name it, from a friend I grew up with. On a Saturday night he would sometimes go out and do things he was not proud of, things involving alcohol and girls. But on Sunday he was faithful to put his tithe in the offering plate — almost as if the money were restitution, a way to settle the account. It does not work that way. God does not accept sacrifice in the place of obedience. What He asks, Micah said, is "to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God" (Micah 6:8) — and no check in the plate is a substitute for justice toward the people around us.

Manabii walinguruma kweli hiyohiyo zamani sana. Amosi alimsikia Mungu akisema jambo la kushtua juu ya ibada ya watu wake mwenyewe: "Nazichukia sikukuu zenu, nazidharau... Niondolee kelele za nyimbo zako" (Amosi 5:21–23). Mungu angewezaje kukataa sadaka zilezile alizoziamuru? Kwa sababu watu waliokuwa wakizileta walikuwa wakiwakanyaga maskini — wakiwahonga waamuzi, wakidanganya kwa mizani isiyo ya haki, wakimuuza mhitaji kwa bei ya jozi moja ya viatu — na hakuna sadaka inayofunika jambo hilo. Nilijifunza kanuni hii muda mrefu kabla sijaweza kuipa jina, kutoka kwa rafiki niliyekua pamoja naye. Jumamosi usiku wakati mwingine alikuwa akitoka na kufanya mambo ambayo hakujivunia, mambo yaliyohusu pombe na wasichana. Lakini Jumapili alikuwa mwaminifu kuweka zaka yake katika sahani ya sadaka — karibu kana kwamba fedha ile ilikuwa fidia, njia ya kulipa deni. Haifanyi kazi hivyo. Mungu hapokei dhabihu badala ya utii. Anachokitaka, Mika alisema, ni "kutenda haki, na kupenda rehema, na kwenda kwa unyenyekevu pamoja na Mungu wako" (Mika 6:8) — na hakuna hundi katika sahani ya sadaka inayoweza kuchukua nafasi ya haki kwa watu wanaotuzunguka.

The negative warning is just as sharp, and our Lord gave it in the story of the rich man and Lazarus, the beggar at his gate (Luke 16). The rich man's sin was not that he actively harmed Lazarus; it was that he stepped over him day after day and did nothing, feasting in comfort while a fellow image-bearer starved at his doorstep. That is a sin a comfortable church commits constantly, and it damns. We help the poor, then, not with a careless sentimentality that merely throws money and feels good, but with the wise, personal, dignifying love that sees the person and not just the need — remembering always that the poor man bears the image of God as fully as we do, the principle we laid down in Unit 7.

Onyo la upande wa pili ni kali vilevile, na Bwana wetu alilitoa katika habari ya yule tajiri na Lazaro, mwombaji aliyekuwa langoni pake (Luka 16). Dhambi ya tajiri haikuwa kwamba alimdhuru Lazaro kwa vitendo; ilikuwa kwamba alimpita juu yake siku baada ya siku na hakufanya lolote, akifanya karamu kwa starehe huku mwanadamu mwenzake mwenye sura ya Mungu akifa njaa mlangoni pake. Hiyo ni dhambi ambayo kanisa linalostarehe hutenda daima, na inaleta hukumu ya milele. Basi, tunawasaidia maskini si kwa huruma ya juujuu isiyo na uangalifu ambayo hutupa fedha tu na kujisikia vizuri, bali kwa upendo wenye hekima, wa kibinafsi, unaoheshimu utu, unaomwona mtu na si hitaji lake tu — tukikumbuka daima kwamba mtu maskini anabeba sura ya Mungu kikamilifu kama sisi, kanuni tuliyoiweka katika Sehemu ya 7.

And now a hard word that I will not soften, because it touches us who lead. It is a scandal and a contradiction for a pastor to live in a mansion while the members of his own congregation languish in poverty. Hear the principle plainly: if God blesses us with material resources, He gives them to us in order that we might share them. Wealth in a Christian's hand is a trust to be distributed, not a reward to be displayed. John puts the knife in: "whoever has this world's goods, and sees his brother in need, and shuts up his heart from him, how does the love of God abide in him?" (1 John 3:17). The pastor who grows fat on the offerings of poor people and parades his wealth before them has inverted the entire purpose of what God entrusted to him; he has become the rich man, and his flock is Lazarus at his gate. Let the shepherd's own standard of living be a sermon on contentment and generosity, not a monument to greed. He who handles the people's gifts must be, of all men, the freest from the love of money and the readiest to share.

Na sasa neno gumu ambalo sitalilainisha, kwa sababu linatugusa sisi tunaoongoza. Ni aibu kubwa na ni mgongano kwa mchungaji kuishi katika jumba la kifahari huku washiriki wa kusanyiko lake mwenyewe wakidhoofika katika umaskini. Sikia kanuni hii waziwazi: Mungu akitubariki kwa rasilimali za kimali, anatupa hizo ili tuzigawe kwa wengine. Utajiri katika mkono wa Mkristo ni amana ya kugawanywa, si thawabu ya kuonyeshwa. Yohana anachoma kisu ndani kabisa: "yeye aliye na riziki ya dunia, kisha akamwona ndugu yake ana uhitaji, akamzuilia huruma zake, je! Kupenda kwa Mungu kwakaaje ndani yake huyo?" (1 Yohana 3:17). Mchungaji anayenenepa kwa sadaka za watu maskini na kujionyesha utajiri wake mbele yao ameligeuza kabisa kusudi la kile Mungu alichomkabidhi; amekuwa yule tajiri, na kundi lake ni Lazaro langoni pake. Kiwango cha maisha ya mchungaji mwenyewe na kiwe mahubiri juu ya kuridhika na ukarimu, si mnara wa ukumbusho wa tamaa. Yeye anayeshughulikia matoleo ya watu anapaswa kuwa, kuliko watu wote, huru zaidi mbali na kupenda fedha na tayari zaidi kugawa.
